description: When a task requires both analytical framing and domain-specific institutional knowledge, and only one can be supplied by composition: supply the framing. Domain knowledge must come from the base model or the source document, not from primitives.

name: human-evaluates-discovered-frames
description: When composition introduces an analytical lens the prompt did not specify: present the lens and its findings as candidates for human evaluation, not as conclusions. The human decides whether the discovered frame is relevant to their context.

name: audience-specific-failure-mode-anchoring
description: When advising on a proposal, plan, or design for a specific audience: anchor recommendations in failure modes that audience has actually experienced, not generic improvement suggestions

name: composition-efficiency-cost-on-smaller-models
description: When composing agents for smaller models: expect 1.5-2x processing time overhead from composition. If latency matters more than output quality for this task, skip composition.

name: backup-modify-test-restore-for-reversible-experiments
description: When testing configuration changes that affect a shared resource (database, model weights, primitive pool), copy the resource before modification and restore after testing, ensuring the experiment is fully reversible without side effects on production state

name: test-one-variable-per-round-in-calibration
description: When running calibration rounds to compare system configurations, change exactly one variable per round to enable clean attribution of outcome differences; compound changes in a single round make results uninterpretable

name: pre-approve-subagent-permissions-over-inline-fallback
description: When dispatching background subagents: audit and batch-request all required file, tool, and shell permissions before dispatch. If permissions cannot be pre-approved, execute inline rather than dispatching agents that will fail on first tool call. The cost of a permission audit is one consolidated request; the cost of unapproved dispatch is N failed agents plus inline rework.

name: pm-audit-before-tag-not-after
description: When releasing software: run a consistency audit (version strings, documentation accuracy, stale references, dead code) after tests pass but before tagging and publishing. Fixes found after publish require version bumps and re-release cycles; fixes found before publish cost nothing.

name: insert-tracing-links-for-referenced-artefacts
description: Scan a document for every mention of a file, URL, project, book, dataset, specification, or named artefact, then for each one insert a working link — using the format appropriate to the context (wikilink for Obsidian, markdown link for general markdown, HTML anchor for web output) — with descriptor text that concisely states what the linked resource contains or why it is referenced, so a reader encountering the link understands both what is at the destination and why the author cited it without leaving the current document

name: architecture-migration-feasibility-assessor
description: Given a current system architecture, assess migration feasibility across three axes: (1) auth model — does the current credential/delegation approach scale to the target deployment model (single-tenant → multi-tenant, consultant-controlled → client-controlled)?; (2) compute model — do runtime characteristics (job duration, latency, concurrency) fit the target host constraints (serverless timeouts, managed service limits)?; (3) data model — does the current storage layer (spreadsheet, flat file, embedded DB) support the target integrity, concurrency, and query requirements? Output: blockers requiring rethinking, components that port unchanged, net-new work required.

name: living-witness-corroboration-interviewer
description: When interviewing a contemporaneous observer to confirm or disconfirm a historical claim: (1) establish their first-hand position as a witness before any framing; (2) let them characterise timing and landscape from their own memory; (3) use a controlled-experiment question to test the claim indirectly; (4) hold the thesis reveal for an optional final section, only if the conversation warrants. Never introduce the thesis before the witness has landed on their own observations — this protects testimony independence.

name: controlled-experiment-question
description: Given a thesis claim and a known comparable case without the hypothesised cause, formulate a question that lets the interviewee confirm or disconfirm the claim without being told the thesis. The question names both cases and asks the interviewee to account for the difference. Output: a single question that surfaces the contrast without revealing the investigator's interpretation.

name: pre-interview-source-triangulation
description: Before any research interview, read three source types in parallel: (1) the interviewee's own published writing on the subject — establishes what they have already said publicly and what their framing is; (2) the project continuity file — establishes what you need from them; (3) editorial or advisor feedback — establishes the specific gap the interview must fill. When choosing between going in open vs going in informed: triangulate all three. This resolves the apparent conflict: the interviewee's writing tells you what not to re-ask; the continuity file tells you what is missing; the editorial feedback tells you what must land.

name: cases-as-structured-qa
description: Write each concrete case in a portfolio as structured answers to a fixed set of diagnostic questions, not as prose narrative

name: test-case-portfolio-coherence-via-diagnostic-questions
description: Test each case against shared diagnostic questions; flag any that cannot answer all questions cleanly as not illustrating the same underlying problem

name: separate-structurally-distinct-cases
description: Separate cases with structurally distinct answers to the problem-framing question into individual entries rather than treating them as variants of the same case

name: case-portfolio-entry-schema
description: Return a case portfolio where each entry answers: (1) the granularity of intent or need in this case, (2) the granularity of what existing tooling or infrastructure provides, (3) the problem arising from the mismatch between (1) and (2), (4) what becomes possible if the mismatch is resolved. Flag any case that cannot answer all four questions rather than forcing an answer.

name: load-style-constraints-before-drafting
description: When loading all style constraint sources before drafting and drafting first conflict: load all relevant style sources before writing; the cost of a full rewrite after a style failure exceeds the cost of loading an additional source upfront

name: split-cases-with-distinct-problem-framings
description: When two use cases feel related but have structurally different answers to the problem-framing question: write them as separate cases; do not merge them to reduce quantity

name: dual-strategic-value-of-feasibility-outcomes
description: When a use case has two possible engineering feasibility outcomes (buildable on existing infrastructure vs. requires rearchitecting): present both as strategically useful positions rather than treating the second as failure — the second outcome justifies a research direction and a different funding ask

name: cta-explicitness-by-audience-role
description: When choosing how explicit to make a call to action: if the audience refers or connects people as part of their professional role (teachers, coordinators, case workers), state the ask directly at the opening. If the audience self-identifies their engagement mode (executives, investors, senior professionals), make the ask tacit — close with an open invitation rather than a named request. Never use an explicit directive ask for self-identifying audiences.

name: continuation-programme-as-separate
description: When describing a multi-stage programme: present each stage as a programme with its own application, not as a small number are selected to continue. State explicitly who is eligible to apply to later stages, including whether outside applicants can bypass earlier stages. The selected-to-continue framing implies internal gatekeeping; separate application correctly represents open eligibility.

name: structural-gap-framing-senior-audience
description: Lead programme or initiative descriptions for senior audiences with the structural gap that existing systems cannot address, then position the initiative as addressing it. Do not open with a programme overview or an explicit ask.

name: source-doc-identification-before-copy
description: When producing copy for a programme or initiative with multiple document versions: before writing, identify and confirm which file is the current authoritative working document. Prefer pausing to verify over assuming based on filename or recency. Writing from a superseded version invalidates all output.

name: continuation-option-at-section-end
description: Return a multi-stage programme description where each programme section ends with a sentence noting the participant option to apply into the next programme, including its key terms (funding amount and duration). Place this sentence as the last substantive point before any call to action.

name: propagate-changes-across-parallel-versions
description: When parallel audience versions of a document exist, propagate content changes from any updated version to all others without waiting for per-version instruction.

name: identify-inconsistent-clause-standards
description: Identify sections in a multi-clause document that apply different standards to the same underlying concern

name: flag-overbroad-unenforceable-terms
description: Flag contract terms that may be overbroad or unenforceable under applicable employment law

name: propose-amendment-preserving-counterparty-interests
description: Propose targeted amendment language that resolves identified ambiguity while preserving the other party's legitimate interests

name: clause-by-clause-issue-list
description: Return a clause-by-clause issue list with: clause reference, issue type (ambiguity / overreach / inconsistency / gap), proposed amendment language, risk level (high / medium / low)

name: principle-over-instance-enumeration
description: When choosing between enumerating specific instances (clients, engagements, cases) and stating the underlying principle or vehicle: prefer the principle — it remains valid as instances change without requiring revision

name: standard-consistency-before-clause-fixes
description: When reviewing a document with multiple clauses addressing the same concern: verify standard consistency across all clauses before proposing individual fixes — fixing one clause while leaving inconsistent standards elsewhere creates new ambiguity

name: outside-employment-first-for-portfolio-workers
description: When reviewing employment contracts for a portfolio worker: flag outside-employment restrictions before other issues — they are the most likely source of immediate conflict given pre-existing commitments

name: multi-audience-programme-description-set
description: Return a set of programme descriptions for distinct audiences (applicants, funders, referrers, government officials, personal network, sector-specific outreach), each with appropriate framing, emphasis, and call-to-action; produce as a navigable document with TOC and working anchor links

name: adapt-message-register-to-channel
description: When generating a message for a specified channel (WhatsApp, email, formal document), write in the register appropriate to that channel: fully casual (lowercase, conversational fragments, no formal structure) for WhatsApp and personal messages; semi-formal for email; formal prose for documents

name: trace-obligations-to-pivot-condition
description: Identify the threshold condition (date, status, or event) that determines which regulatory regime applies before listing obligations, timelines, or penalties; structure the output so the pivot appears first and consequences branch from it

name: regulatory-research-findings
description: Return a regulatory research summary with: (a) pivot condition table mapping threshold to applicable regime, (b) obligations and timelines per regime, (c) tax and duty implications, (d) practical options with tradeoffs table, (e) ambiguities requiring direct agency or legal confirmation

name: flag-regulatory-ambiguity-for-confirmation
description: When a regulatory rule is not explicitly stated in official published documentation: flag the gap as an ambiguity and recommend direct agency or legal confirmation rather than inferring a confident answer from secondary sources

name: fetch-official-then-gap-fill-with-secondary
description: Fetch official government or primary sources in parallel with secondary sources; use secondary sources only to fill gaps that primary sources leave open, not as the primary evidence base

name: corporate-estate-two-track
description: When a deceased was sole director of a private company and executor/beneficiary has existing shareholding: decompose into immediate member-rights track (no Grant needed, appoint director via members resolution) and probate-dependent share-transmission track (requires Grant). Frame Track A as executable now to avoid corporate paralysis while probate runs in parallel

name: csp-as-filing-proxy
description: When executor/beneficiary lacks officer standing for a government filing portal: route all filings through existing CSP who already holds portal access credentials, rather than attempting to establish new access. The CSPs existing relationship and credentials bypass the chicken-and-egg problem of needing officer standing to file the appointment

name: present-engagement-options-as-commitment-spectrum
description: Present engagement options as a commitment spectrum, from exploratory/advisory at the light end to scoped project work at the deep end

name: frame-advisory-recommendation-as-dual-purpose
description: Frame advisory engagement recommendations as serving two distinct purposes: client-side validation of whether the engagement is useful, and joint exploration of where more specific work would add value

name: return-consulting-engagement-menu
description: Return a consulting engagement menu with: option name, concrete scope, fit rationale, unique advisor value, and monthly retainer range per option

name: characterise-option-tiers-not-enumerate
description: When presenting a range of options to a decision-maker: characterise the tiers rather than enumerate individual options; let the recipient indicate direction before detailing specifics

name: recommend-lightest-commitment-tier-first
description: When pitching advisory engagements: recommend starting at the lightest commitment tier; justify with two distinct reasons — (a) lightweight enough for the client to validate whether the engagement is useful, (b) exploratory enough for both parties to identify where specific work adds value — not price alone

name: verify-archival-scene-sourcing
description: Verify whether each scene described in archival writing is directly cited from a source or inferred from two separately sourced facts

name: prose-style-review-output
description: Return a numbered prose-change list; each item must include: exact quoted text to change, problem statement (one sentence), proposed replacement text

name: concrete-mechanism-over-abstract-quality
description: When describing a person's contribution using an abstract quality (what they possess) vs. a concrete mechanism (what they do): prefer the concrete mechanism. Name the action, not the attribute.

name: flag-archival-inference-not-citation
description: When a scene is assembled from two separately sourced facts rather than a direct citation: signal it as inference in the prose. Do not present inferred reconstructions as sourced descriptions.

name: shared-vocabulary-as-case-connective-tissue
description: Before writing case studies that illustrate a common underlying problem, define a shared vocabulary—terms that appear in both the case descriptions and the general solution—so each case reads as an instance of the same problem rather than a separate argument

name: investor-case-qa-format
description: Write investor memo case studies as structured Q&A: (1) who the user is and population size, (2) what they want at operational specificity, (3) what they actually have, (4) the mismatch and its consequences, (5) what resolving it unlocks

name: operational-specificity-in-want-have-contrast
description: When writing the want/have contrast in a case study: prefer operational specificity (system + operation + time window + scope) over abstract framing. 'Permission for a specific agent instance to pull scheduling data for one procedure code for the next six days' is correct; 'governed access to clinical systems' is not

name: cases-before-framing-for-investor-memos
description: When developing investor memo language for a product: derive the general problem framing from concrete cases, not the reverse. Cases first reveal the mismatch operationally; the framing then names the structural cause. Starting with the framing produces abstractions that do not connect to evidence

name: investor-memo-problem-opening
description: Return a problem-opening paragraph with: (1) the gap in existing tooling named across its lifecycle (how it is issued, persists, and revoked); (2) the consequences of the gap (compliance cost, liability, process overhead); (3) what a solution unlocks in two directions—established industry use case and emerging category use case. All three components must be present

name: state-consequences-before-benefits
description: When writing a problem statement for a product or solution: state the consequences of the current gap (costs, liability, overhead) before stating what the solution unlocks. The reader must feel the pain before the relief is meaningful

name: read-governing-document-first
description: Read the specific governing document (constitution, contract, statute) before applying general principles or model forms

name: trace-argument-to-source-provision
description: Trace each legal argument to its specific source provision, citing the regulation or section number and quoting the operative text

name: name-impossibility-as-counter-argument
description: Identify when a counterparty's interpretation produces an impossible or absurd outcome, and name that outcome explicitly as a counter-argument

name: exact-quotation-over-paraphrase
description: When quoting from a legal instrument (statute, constitution, contract): prefer exact quotation of the operative text over paraphrase. Paraphrase only when the operative text exceeds ~50 words.

name: statutory-breach-over-diplomatic-hedging
description: When a legal deadlock results in an ongoing statutory breach: name the breach and its duration explicitly rather than hedging diplomatically. The breach creates urgency that outweighs reputational risk.

name: protective-rationale-collapses-when-same-person
description: When the person a legal formality is designed to protect is the same person requesting its waiver: argue that the protective rationale collapses entirely, not merely that compliance is inconvenient

name: lawyer-briefing-note
description: Return a lawyer briefing note structured as: (1) opening paragraph: purpose and urgency; (2) party facts; (3) the problem and what is blocking resolution; (4) instructing party's relevant standing and interests; (5) counterparty's position with stated rationale; (6) instructing party's legal arguments, each traced to a specific provision; (7) relevant provisions summary table; (8) courses of action with explicit questions for the lawyer; (9) what is needed from the lawyer; (10) documents available. Written in first person, addressed as a letter.

name: legal-dispute-response-letter
description: Return a legal dispute response letter structured as: (1) acknowledgment of counterparty's position; (2) material facts their position does not address; (3) legal arguments responding to each element of their position, each citing a specific provision; (4) consequences of their interpretation, naming any impossibility or absurdity explicitly; (5) specific request for one of two named paths forward. Firm tone, no diplomatic hedging.

name: verify-technical-identifiers-against-source-docs
description: Verify technical identifiers (email addresses, URLs, system names, endpoint strings) appearing in documents derived from transcripts or other lossy sources against the project's canonical source documents before finalising

name: urgency-ordered-action-list-with-responsibility-tags
description: Return a numbered action list ordered from most to least urgent, with each item tagged by the responsible party (person, role, or joint)

name: gated-roadmap-from-current-to-target-state
description: Return a numbered roadmap from current state to target state where each step includes an explicit gate condition stating what must be true before that step can begin

name: audience-segmented-meeting-agenda
description: Return a meeting agenda structured by audience segment, with items numbered continuously across all segments and each segment's purpose and expected duration stated

name: canonical-source-over-transcript-for-technical-strings
description: When forced to choose between using a technical identifier (email address, URL, system name) sourced from a speech-to-text transcript and verifying it against a written specification or configuration file: always verify against the written source; treat transcribed technical strings as unreliable

name: literary-editorial-persona
description: Apply editorial standards drawn from John McPhee and E.B. White: trust concrete detail over abstract claim; build scenes patiently before drawing conclusions; exercise economy (cut anything that does not serve the argument); maintain structural transparency so the reader always knows where they are and why; flag where abstraction substitutes for evidence

name: text-intersection-analysis
description: Return a list of thematic connection points between two source texts: for each connection, name the shared concept, quote the relevant passage from each text, and identify the specific insertion location (paragraph and transition sentence) in the target text where the connection would most naturally land, with a one-sentence rationale for the placement

name: evidence-first-structural-review
description: Review a long-form journalism or essay draft for argument-before-evidence ordering: identify each passage where an abstract claim, dismissal, or theoretical frame appears before the concrete evidence that motivates it; for each inversion, quote both passages, explain why the current order weakens the reader's engagement, and give a specific resequencing recommendation

name: voice-transcript-cleanup
description: Return a cleaned version of a voice-to-text transcript: remove filler words and false starts; fix grammar and punctuation; preserve the speaker's vocabulary, conceptual structure, and register exactly — do not rephrase into a different voice or level of formality; flag any passage where the intended meaning is genuinely ambiguous

name: mutual-discovery-advisory-opener
description: When a consultant lacks sufficient client context to scope concrete engagements, and the client lacks sufficient familiarity with the consultant to evaluate options: propose open-ended periodic advisory calls (no fixed agenda, client brings current problems) as the initial engagement form. Frame explicitly as mutual discovery — neither party can scope well yet — rather than as a lighter version of scoped work. The advisory relationship surfaces what is actually worth scoping.

name: call-transcript-to-engagement-map
description: Given a call transcript between a consultant and a prospective client, extract all potential consulting engagement areas organised into four buckets: (1) explicit client priority statements in the client's own words, (2) concrete near-term experiments or pilots mentioned, (3) strategic or positioning questions raised, (4) internal org or team issues surfaced. Flag any divergence between transcript framing and any pre-existing briefing document.

name: synthesise-product-descriptions-into-vision
description: Synthesise multiple product or service descriptions into a unified vision statement that captures the shared problem and collective solution

name: pitch-paragraph-with-problem-impact-solution
description: Return a pitch paragraph with: problem statement (concrete, 1–2 sentences), business consequences (named explicitly, not implied), solution introduction (actor + number of products/services + what they fix)

name: size-retainer-by-total-time-not-call-time
description: When pricing a consulting retainer around a fixed call cadence, calculate prep + call + post-work hours to derive the monthly total; present the breakdown to the client as justification for the fee

name: estimate-procurement-signing-authority
description: Estimate likely signing authority by seniority: VP-level at large multinationals typically USD 25k–75k per contract/year without escalation; propose a 3-month initial term to stay within VP authority and reduce procurement friction

name: contract-version-diff
description: Return a clause-by-clause diff of two contract versions: list only substantive changes (percentages, defined terms, scope, payment, termination); note but do not elevate formatting artefacts

name: persuasion-theory-distinction
description: Identify the underlying persuasion theory (reader's primary barrier) driving a copywriting approach and distinguish approaches by barrier type, not by execution style

name: framework-voice-consistency
description: Apply a specified copywriting framework consistently throughout a document without drifting into a different register

name: synthesis-source-tracking
description: Track source attribution when synthesising multiple input variants into a single output

name: handoff-instruction-content-pairing
description: Pair each section of a handoff document with both the implementation instruction and the exact content to use — not a description of the content

name: multi-offering-early-positioning
description: Position multi-offering overviews within the first two sections of any page or document

name: copywriting-approach-taxonomy
description: Return a copywriting approach taxonomy with: for each approach — name, core logic (2–3 sentences), underlying persuasion assumption (what the reader's primary barrier is), concrete example output for a consistent scenario, best-fit context/audience

name: platform-implementation-guide
description: Return a platform implementation guide with: for each page section — section name, implementation instructions (block types, settings), and the exact copy to paste (formatted as entered in the CMS, not a description)

name: multi-variant-creative-file-output
description: Return N distinct files (one per variant), each containing the full output for that variant, with the variant name and approach in the filename

name: synthesis-inline-over-subagent
description: When synthesising multiple creative variants into a single final output and forced to choose between subagent efficiency and voice consistency across the full document: prefer voice consistency. Execute inline.

name: multi-offering-completeness-over-conversion
description: When a brief has multiple offerings that should receive equal prominence and forced to choose between conversion focus (hero → primary offering only) and audience completeness (all offerings visible early): prefer audience completeness. Place multi-offering overview in section 2.

name: primary-audience-over-secondary-coverage
description: When copy for a secondary audience conflicts with messaging for the primary audience: deprioritise or omit the secondary audience. When forced to choose between comprehensive audience coverage and primary audience message clarity: prefer primary audience clarity.

name: tease-undisclosed-detail
description: When a product or programme detail is not yet available for disclosure: include a named teaser (state the name and headline metric) but do not elaborate. When forced to choose between comprehensive detail and accurate representation of what is known: prefer accuracy — name it, defer the detail.

name: map-proposal-gaps-to-funding-criteria
description: Map each identified gap in a grant proposal to the specific funding criterion it fails to address

name: assign-recommendations-to-named-owner
description: Assign each change recommendation to the specific named person responsible for answering or resolving it

name: calibrate-grant-review-against-funded-exemplars
description: Calibrate a grant proposal review against previously funded exemplars from the same programme not against abstract criteria alone

name: reframe-named-principle-as-general-practice
description: When a design principle is commonly attributed to a named individual reframe it as a general principle of the field unless the attribution is load-bearing for the argument

name: trace-new-concepts-to-source
description: Trace each concept newly introduced in a document to its source file or originating session

name: grant-review-two-list-output
description: Return two lists: (1) five elements missing from the proposal each naming the criterion affected and providing a proposed addition or a question directed at a named stakeholder; (2) five items to update or change each quoting the problematic text explaining the weakness and providing a proposed rewrite or named question

name: concept-provenance-table
description: Return a three-column table: concept name | approximately 25-word context snippet from immediately around the concept's introduction in the document | source file or session from which the concept was drawn

name: compliance-disclosure-statement
description: Return a plain-language disclosure statement of 100-200 words that: names the external organisation and its legal form; states the declaring party's role and ownership share if applicable; describes the nature of the work; and asserts the boundary between the declared interest and the declaring party's primary institutional role

name: new-versioned-file-over-in-place-edit
description: When proposing new content for a document with existing authorship in a collaborative repository: create a new versioned file rather than editing the original in place — preserves the original as a reference and makes proposed changes trackable

name: plain-language-for-compliance-disclosures
description: When a compliance or conflict-of-interest disclosure is required: describe the interest in plain matter-of-fact language stating facts without minimising or dramatising; do not use hedging language; do not use advocacy language

name: general-framing-over-named-attribution
description: When forced to choose between attributing a principle to a named individual and framing it as general professional practice: prefer the general framing unless attribution is load-bearing; unnecessary named attribution reduces transferability and increases personality-cult risk

name: extract-subject-vocabulary-before-naming
description: Extract the subject's personal vocabulary — specific images, references, and terms from their actual world — before generating name candidates

name: generate-names-from-cross-domain-collisions
description: Generate name candidates from cross-domain collisions between the subject's personal references and the target domain's vocabulary

name: apply-phone-test-to-name-candidates
description: Apply the phone test: say the name candidate in its full official form (name + official entity suffix) aloud and check it sounds professional when spoken

name: candidate-list-with-rationale-and-risk
description: Return each candidate with: the candidate itself, one-sentence rationale explaining the logic or reference, one-sentence risk or concern note

name: subject-vocabulary-over-genre-conventions-when-generic
description: When naming output is generic: prefer restarting from the subject's personal vocabulary over refining within genre conventions. Category labels anchor generation to genre expectations; personal vocabulary anchors to the subject's distinctive world.

name: write-in-forwarder-voice
description: Write third-party outreach message templates from the perspective of a knowledgeable peer forwarding information, not the operator running the programme

name: forwarder-vs-operator-framing
description: When writing outreach templates intended for third-party forwarding: use forwarder framing ("I wanted to make sure you know about X") not operator framing ("I'm running X"). Operator framing is only appropriate when the template will be sent by the operator directly.

name: qualify-per-unit-funding-amounts
description: When stating programme funding or resource amounts, qualify the scope explicitly (per participant, per cohort, per year) so the reader does not have to infer whether the amount is total or individual

name: dispatch-write-at-dispatch-time
description: In dispatch-and-collect workflows, write a partial record to the audit log at dispatch time and update it at completion. Never defer the full record write to end-of-cycle only.

name: cross-session-notebook-variable
description: When a Jupyter notebook try/except block falls back to stale data because a variable from a prior session is unavailable: create a SimpleNamespace mock to satisfy the try branch rather than re-running the upstream cell. Re-run only when the upstream cell is safe to repeat (idempotent reads, not sends).

name: extract-contract-key-terms
description: Extract key terms from a formal employment contract and organise them into a plain-language summary structured by topic: compensation, statutory contributions, benefits, hours, probation, leave, expenses, conduct, termination, confidentiality, governing law

name: employment-contract-summary
description: Return a plain-language employment contract summary with labelled sections: role and reporting, base salary (stating gross explicitly), bonus conditions, statutory contributions (applicability and mechanism), benefits, working hours, probation period and notice, annual leave (entitlement, carry-over, forfeiture), sick leave procedure, expense reimbursement, outside employment restrictions, termination conditions (standard and immediate), post-termination obligations, confidentiality, governing law

name: confirm-financial-figure-framing
description: When a financial figure is described with ambiguous framing (e.g., inclusive of X, net of Y): confirm whether the figure is gross or net before using it in any calculation or document — do not assume and proceed

name: confirm-template-variables-before-adapting
description: When adapting a document template for a new subject (person, entity, project): explicitly confirm all variable fields before drafting — do not carry forward template values as defaults for the new subject

name: replace-named-reference-with-generic
description: When removing a named organisation or product reference from public-facing copy: replace with a generic category description that preserves the functional meaning — do not simply delete the phrase

name: scan-files-for-named-references
description: Scan a set of documents for mentions of specific named organisations, products, or entities and report which files contain matches, with filename and matched line

name: enforce-application-layer-constraints
description: Enforce write-once and append-only guarantees at the application layer, not solely at the database schema layer, and document which constraints are application-enforced vs schema-enforced

name: separate-retrieval-from-scoring
description: Separate document retrieval from content scoring in multi-step analysis pipelines to prevent prior-knowledge contamination of the scoring step

name: assign-adversarial-stance-to-parallel-reviewers
description: Assign each parallel review agent a distinct adversarial stance — supporting, opposing, or structural auditing — before dispatching

name: document-minimum-verifiable-evidence-for-agent-inputs
description: Document the minimum verifiable evidence required before accepting any agent-produced value into a deterministic computation or tamper-evident audit trail

name: require-source-id-and-verbatim-quote-for-audit-trail
description: When agent-produced values must enter a tamper-evident record: require a retrievable source identifier and verbatim quoted text as minimum verifiable evidence, not the agent's assertion or paraphrase

name: decompose-large-deliverables-into-independently-completable-units
description: When a deliverable risks exceeding output capacity as a single document: decompose into independently completable and testable units, not one monolithic output

name: multi-perspective-decision-memo
description: Return a multi-perspective decision memo with: supporting case (bulleted evidence with citations), opposing case (bulleted counterevidence and weaknesses), structural audit (whether decision criteria are valid), and synthesis listing unresolved disagreements requiring human decision

name: identify-contract-template-variables
description: Identify all variable fields in a contract template — fields that differ from instance to instance (names, dates, compensation amounts, percentages, role titles) — and list each with: field name, clause number(s) where it appears, and whether it appears multiple times

name: lettered-subclauses-in-numbered-legal-documents
description: When a legal document uses numbered main clauses (1., 2., 3.): use lettered sub-items (a), (b), (c) rather than numbered sub-items (1., 2., 3.). Numbered sub-items create visual ambiguity with parent clause numbers in PDF and print rendering.

name: basic-salary-vs-gross-salary-singapore-contracts
description: In Singapore employment contracts, use 'basic salary' not 'gross salary'. 'Basic salary' is the statutory term in the Employment Act used to calculate CPF contributions, notice pay in lieu, and overtime entitlements. 'Gross salary' includes allowances and is legally distinct. Plain-language summaries may use 'gross' as shorthand; the signed contract must say 'basic'.

name: compare-contract-to-agreed-termsheet
description: Compare a finalised contract against its agreed term sheet or plain-language summary: for each section confirm whether contract wording is consistent with agreed terms, then flag (a) discrepancies where contract is more restrictive or permissive than agreed, (b) clauses carried over from prior negotiating versions that no longer apply to this hire, (c) internal cross-references that became inconsistent after edits

name: named-placeholder-format-for-contract-templates
description: When creating a reusable contract template: replace variable fields with descriptive placeholders in the format [Enter {variable name}] where the variable name is in sentence case and identifies exactly what to enter (e.g. [Enter monthly salary], not [ENTER VALUE] or [TBD]). This allows a reviewer to understand what each blank expects without a separate key.

name: informal-forwardable-over-fir-for-close-relationships
description: When drafting a forwardable outreach message and the sender has a close personal relationship with the forwarder (close friend, not a professional contact): use informal format ('know anyone? please fwd') rather than a structured FIR. Structured FIR signals professional distance and reads as stiff between close friends. FIR is appropriate for professional acquaintances.

name: whatsapp-message-format-over-email-format
description: When adapting outreach copy for WhatsApp: (1) omit salutation, (2) replace all markdown links with fully-formed bare URLs — WhatsApp does not render markdown and unrendered syntax hides the clickable URL, (3) use sentence case throughout, (4) shorten relative to email version.

name: maintain-sender-subject-identity-in-third-party-outreach
description: In third-party outreach templates: write the subject in third person, sender asks in first person. Do not mix the two identities.

name: identify-all-template-placeholders-before-requesting-values
description: Identify all template variable placeholders in a document before requesting values from the user

name: raw-syntax-over-markdown-approximation-when-renderer-diverges
description: When a markdown construct produces incorrect or unpredictable output in a target rendering engine: replace it with the engine's native raw syntax block, not an approximation in markdown

name: template-placeholder-inventory
description: Return a complete inventory of unfilled template placeholders: placeholder name, document location (section or clause), expected value type, and current value if already provided

name: diagnose-stale-jupyter-cell-output
description: When two Jupyter cells show contradictory values for the same variable, apply the single-state test: can a single kernel state produce both displayed outputs simultaneously? If not, at least one output is stale from a different run. Restart the kernel and re-run cells sequentially before looking for code bugs.

name: derive-rate-denominator-from-filtered-collection
description: When computing a rate over a filtered population, derive the denominator from the filtered collection (e.g. unique_responding + no_reply) not the original unfiltered list. This ensures exclusions reduce both numerator and denominator consistently and the rate reflects the actual pool being analysed.

name: identify-side-effect-cells-before-notebook-rerun
description: Before re-executing Jupyter notebook cells to refresh kernel state: identify all cells with irreversible side effects (email dispatch, external API writes, input() prompts) and skip them. Only execute setup and analysis cells needed to pick up code changes or fresh data.

name: catch-attributeerror-alongside-nameerror-in-stub-fallbacks
description: When a try/except block is designed to fall back gracefully when a variable is undefined (NameError), also catch AttributeError if the variable could be a mock or stub object with missing attributes. Use except (NameError, AttributeError) rather than except NameError alone. Missing AttributeError causes the fallback to silently fail when a stub exists but lacks expected fields.

name: requester-writes-fir-not-forwarder
description: When an FIR request describes a 3-party chain (requester asks user to forward to target): write the FIR from the requester's voice addressed to the user, not from the user's voice addressed to the target. The user's role is conduit, not author.

name: flag-non-comparable-line-items-in-provider-comparison
description: When comparing service providers: before building the comparison table, identify which services exist in some providers but not others. Present these as explicit gap rows (e.g. 'not offered') rather than blank cells, and call out the gap in the summary. A blank cell implies a missing price; an explicit 'not offered' signals a structural difference in service scope.

name: establish-entity-type-before-compliance-advice
description: Before advising on statutory compliance requirements (audit, filing, tax obligations): establish the legal entity type (e.g. Pte Ltd, CLG, LLP) and any special registrations (e.g. charity status, licensed entity), as these determine which statutory frameworks and exemptions apply

name: budget-three-scenario-header
description: When a budget document contains both committed and contingent spend: present three headline figures in the header (committed only / total with contingencies / ceiling with all discretionary items) rather than a single total. Label each figure clearly and identify which line items are contingent.

name: identify-statutory-employer-obligation-gaps
description: Identify statutory employer obligations absent from a budget by cross-referencing against jurisdiction-specific requirements: payroll levies, minimum insurance obligations, mandatory data protection registrations, and statutory contributions not already budgeted

name: separate-arithmetic-from-completeness-review
description: When reviewing a financial or planning document: separate numerical verification (does arithmetic hold across all rows and sections?) from content completeness review (are all required categories represented?) as independent parallel tasks rather than a combined sequential pass

name: legal-document-cost-estimate
description: Return a cost estimate for legal document preparation with: document name, scope (what the document covers), low estimate in local currency, high estimate, billing basis (per document | hourly | capped retainer), whether free templates exist, and bundling opportunities with related documents

name: diagnose-failure-mode-before-intervening
description: When a tool or mechanism shows low adoption or engagement and the cause is unclear: diagnose whether the failure mode is comprehension (users do not understand what is being asked) or burden (what is being asked genuinely exceeds their capacity or willingness). Each failure mode requires a different intervention; misdiagnosing one as the other produces ineffective fixes.

name: prefer-communication-changes-over-tool-redesign
description: When a tool or mechanism shows low adoption and the root cause is uncertain: prefer communication and framing improvements over tool redesign as the first intervention. Redesign the tool only after communication changes have been tried and demonstrably failed.

name: distinguish-user-feedback-from-sponsor-feedback
description: When characterising a problem with a mechanism or tool: distinguish between feedback from direct users (who experience the tool) and feedback from sponsors or leadership (who observe outcomes). Note which group is the source, as each may be describing a different problem.

name: check-files-against-spec
description: Check each file against a written specification, reporting PASS or FAIL per requirement with the exact content that passed or failed

name: review-config-for-failure-modes
description: Review configuration files and CI workflows for failure modes and silent failure risks beyond spec compliance

name: verify-deployment-via-url-fetch
description: Fetch live URLs after deployment and verify each against a predefined acceptance checklist, reporting PASS or FAIL per criterion

name: classify-review-findings-by-impact
description: Classify code review findings as: deployment blocker (deployment fails immediately), post-deployment defect (deployment succeeds but output is incorrect), or accepted risk (known limitation, documented)

name: per-file-compliance-report
description: Return a per-file compliance report with: requirement, status (PASS|FAIL), and the exact content that passed or failed. Final verdict: SPEC COMPLIANT or ISSUES FOUND.

name: code-quality-report
description: Return a code quality report structured as: per-file strengths and issues, each issue classified as Critical | Important | Minor, and a final verdict: APPROVED or ISSUES FOUND.

name: infrastructure-setup-spec
description: Return an infrastructure setup specification with: prerequisites (ordered, with failure mode if skipped), file structure, configuration requirements, rollout sequence (numbered steps with ordering rationale), and acceptance criteria (binary-checkable verification steps).

name: spec-compliance-before-quality-review
description: When reviewing code for correctness: run spec compliance review before code quality review. Spec compliance determines whether the right thing was built; quality review determines whether it was built well. Code that fails spec should not receive quality review.

name: prerequisites-first-with-failure-modes
description: When writing specifications for systems that require external service configuration: list all external prerequisites at the top of the document, stating the failure mode if each prerequisite is skipped.

name: trailing-phrase-cut-rule
description: When a sentence ends on a phrase that restates what the main clause already implies: cut the trailing phrase. The main clause is almost always self-sufficient without the trailing restatement.

name: institutional-benefit-specificity-over-symbolism
description: When a document lists benefits for an institutional audience: prefer specific verifiable mechanisms (usage reports, trackable metrics, direct access) over symbolic gestures (logo placement, website mentions). Flag symbolic-only benefits for removal or replacement.

name: establish-credibility-before-ask
description: When making a resource or funding ask to an institutional audience: establish organisational credibility (legal registration, existing funder, programme start date) before stating the request

name: flag-intrasentence-word-repetition
description: Flag any word that appears more than once within the same sentence as a redundancy; propose a consolidated version unless the repetition is intentional for emphasis

name: document-rejected-value-in-notes
description: When a form or portal rejects a value that accurately represents the situation: enter the nearest acceptable approximation and document the actual value with explanation in any available supplementary notes or free-text field

name: verify-account-identity-before-aggregating
description: When aggregating figures from multiple documents issued by the same institution: verify the account identifier and issuer reference on each document before treating them as a single account, since the same institution may issue separate documents for different account types

name: economic-substance-over-payer-label
description: When a source document labels income or a transaction using terminology that may not match the applicable legal or regulatory category: flag the potential mismatch and note that correct classification depends on economic substance rather than the label used by the payer

name: query-official-api-for-reference-data
description: When retrieving official reference data (exchange rates, benchmark rates, statutory thresholds) for financial calculations: query the issuing authority's data API directly rather than scraping their website, as website content is often dynamically loaded and unreliable

name: compare-document-versions-for-textual-differences
description: Compare two versions of a document and identify all textual differences, excluding formatting changes

name: document-version-diff-list
description: Return a numbered list of textual differences between two document versions; for each item: location or context (quoted phrase), text in version A, text in version B, and nature of change (word substitution | sentence restructure | addition | deletion | paragraph split/merge)

name: ambiguous-annotation-is-not-a-cut
description: When applying editorial annotations to a document: only remove or omit content if the annotation explicitly instructs removal (cut, delete, remove). Ambiguous annotations (show me, review, polish, confirm) are not removal instructions — treat the content as retained until an explicit removal instruction is given.

name: search-repo-for-primary-source-evidence
description: Search the project repository for primary source documents (archive notes, interview transcripts, evidence files) and extract verbatim passages relevant to a specified research question, citing the source file and exact passage for each finding

name: extraction-completeness-over-concision
description: When extracting and cataloguing elements from source material (interview moves, persuasion techniques, argument types): prefer completeness over brevity. A comprehensive list can be edited down; items not extracted cannot be recovered.

name: identify-recording-segments-from-content
description: Before naming or filing a recording: inspect its transcript content (overview, speaker turns, topic transitions) and cross-reference with calendar data to identify all distinct meetings or sessions contained in the recording

name: verify-technical-identifiers-against-source
description: Verify all verifiable technical identifiers (domain names, email addresses, URLs, API endpoints) against canonical source documents before including them in any output; never invent a plausible value

name: distinguish-states-from-events-in-state-machines
description: Distinguish between states (stable conditions waiting for action) and events (transition triggers that change states) when designing or reviewing workflow state machines; verify each state has a clear implied next action

name: classify-review-findings-by-decision-owner
description: Classify each review finding by decision owner: decisions requiring human judgment vs. issues resolvable from existing specifications; present human-required decisions first

name: walk-through-user-journeys-per-actor
description: Walk through each identified user journey step-by-step from the perspective of each actor type before declaring a process specification complete; record each step's expected output and flag any step with no specified behaviour

name: research-architectural-alternatives-first
description: Before researching implementation details for a specific technical approach, include at least one research question asking whether a different architectural approach would be better; do not let spec assumptions pre-select the architecture

name: prd-gap-report-with-decision-owners
description: Return a PRD gap report as a structured list where each item contains: gap title, plain-language problem statement (1–2 sentences), proposed resolution, decision owner (human required | agent-resolvable from spec), and severity (blocker | high | medium | low)

name: check-direct-integration-before-email-fallback
description: Before searching email for data from a third-party service (transcripts, exports, reports), verify whether a direct API, CLI, or MCP integration exists for that service

name: find-full-name-from-partial-identifiers
description: Find a person's full name from partial identifiers by sequentially checking appointment emails, calendar attendees, and public web sources

name: mark-inferred-identity-as-unconfirmed
description: When a person's identity is established by inferential signals (event title, filename pattern, email prefix) rather than direct evidence (named article, official profile, introduction): treat as unconfirmed; annotate the inference source; continue searching for confirmation rather than propagating the inference as fact

name: separate-facts-from-analysis-in-counsel-brief
description: When producing a document intended as a factual record for legal counsel, regulators, or other authoritative external reviewers: include only independently verifiable facts — statements traceable to a primary source document; exclude all interpretation, characterisation, and analytical conclusions, even when clearly labelled as such

name: create-fact-gap-document
description: When extracting facts from source documents to populate a formal record or brief, create a companion gap document that: lists each required fact not available from reviewed sources, names the specific document or data source that would provide it, and notes whether that source document already exists in the project repository

name: separate-facts-and-analysis-into-distinct-documents
description: When a document intended for external review (counsel, regulator, auditor) contains both verifiable facts and analytical conclusions: produce them as separate versioned documents rather than labelling or hedging analysis in-line; the external reviewer must be able to rely on the facts document without filtering

name: facts-only-brief-three-section-structure
description: Return a facts-only brief with three sections: (1) named individuals — each with verifiable attributes (identification numbers, addresses, roles, dates of appointment); (2) named entities — each with official registration particulars (registration number, entity type, incorporation date, registered address, registered activities, officers); (3) activities by organisation — each with source-traced verifiable statements; for every entry, cite the primary source document; include no interpretation, characterisation, or analytical conclusion

name: plain-language-over-internal-labels
description: When framework/internal terminology and plain language conflict in external-facing writing: use plain language; translate internal labels (gates, tiers, category types) into descriptive phrases for the external audience

name: positive-criteria-before-eliminatory
description: When ordering evaluation criteria for an applicant-facing document: lead with criteria describing what makes a strong candidate (positive filter), not with criteria that eliminate weak ones; the positive frame comes first

name: defer-structural-edits-to-active-author
description: When reviewing or implementing edits on a document the author is concurrently restructuring: apply only mechanical and line-level fixes (typos, punctuation, whitespace, apostrophe normalisation, date format) and defer all structural, ordering, and voice changes to the author, even beneficial ones; unilateral structural edits collide with the author's in-progress intent

name: report-negative-result-over-forced-fit
description: When sourcing a real example to fit a defined mechanism and no candidate clears the explicit include/exclude criteria: return the negative result with its structural reason, rather than forcing a weak-fitting candidate.

name: verify-claims-against-primary-source-flag-circular
description: Verify each load-bearing factual claim against a primary or original-language source, and mark any source that only re-cites another (e.g. a wiki citing a wiki) as non-independent.

name: depersonalise-charged-example
description: When using a politically or culturally charged example for an audience: name no specific actor and describe the phenomenon rather than the named mechanism, letting the audience supply the attribution.

name: unify-two-threads-into-governing-throughline
description: When two explanatory threads coexist awkwardly in one piece, identify the single causal chain that subsumes both and make it the governing through-line that every section serves.

name: protect-planned-reveal-from-edit-leak
description: When an edit introduces framing that names a concept the piece is structured to reveal later: strip the naming and describe only the phenomenon until the planned reveal point.

name: coherence-report-for-amended-artifact
description: Return a coherence report for an amended narrative or spec: for each issue, give the location, the type (broken callback / plant without payoff, inconsistent answer to the central question, leaked reveal, numbering or cross-reference break, stale internal reference), and a proposed fix.

name: illustrate-principle-with-paired-inverse-examples
description: Illustrate a principle with a paired example set - one case where it was violated and its structural inverse where it was followed - so the contrast carries the lesson.

name: atomise-reusable-material-by-typed-component
description: When material recurs across many composed outputs: capture it as typed reusable components - one hub type the others attach to, with a controlled vocabulary for the hub - rather than storing whole composed artifacts. This makes the material searchable and recombinable.

name: verify-delegate-report-by-independent-recheck
description: When a subagent or delegate reports a task complete: re-derive the result state independently (re-fetch the artifact, count items, check for duplicates) rather than trusting the self-report. Self-reports mask silent partial failures.

name: resolve-inherited-value-to-effective-state
description: Resolve a possibly-inherited property to its effective value by walking the parent chain, not the surface read — an unset value returns null and mimics the default.

name: reverse-engineer-spec-from-current-artifact
description: When an artifact has been edited directly past its spec, regenerate the spec from the artifact's current state rather than patching the stale spec.

name: infer-design-rules-by-diffing-revision-against-baseline
description: To extract someone's implicit design rules, diff their hand-revised version against the generated baseline and read the changes as the rules they applied.

name: reuse-validated-asset-over-regenerate
description: When a suitable validated asset already exists (a library component, a prior artifact): reuse it verbatim rather than regenerating. Regeneration duplicates effort and silently loses fidelity the source carried.

name: cue-prompt-over-full-script-for-live-delivery
description: When preparing a delivery aid for a live talk: prepare a glance-readable cue prompt (a few trigger words per slide, indexed to slide number), not the full prose script. A full script invites verbatim reading and kills freestyle delivery; keep the prose script for rehearsal only.

name: classify-decision-items-by-resolution-status
description: Classify decision items as fully resolved vs. needs-research before taking action on any item

name: read-canonical-spec-before-proposing-identifiers
description: Read the canonical specification to identify authoritative identifiers before proposing integration mechanisms

name: present-sample-workflows-before-interaction-spec
description: Present concrete sample workflows before writing formal interaction pattern specifications

name: return-resolved-vs-blocked-classification
description: Return a two-category classification: (1) fully resolved items with their resolutions, (2) blocked items with the specific question or information needed before proceeding

name: return-option-comparison-with-complexity-and-surfaces
description: Return an option comparison with for each option: name, complexity level (low/medium/high), new dependencies or integration surfaces introduced, and a ranked recommendation with one-sentence rationale

name: return-sample-interaction-workflow-with-four-cases
description: Return a sample interaction workflow showing: (1) unambiguous case, (2) disambiguation case (multiple matches), (3) combined-operation case, (4) failure/graceful-recovery case. Each case shows exact system text and user input at each step.

name: prefer-existing-integration-channel-over-new-surface
description: When choosing between integrating a new feature with an existing channel vs. adding a new integration surface: prefer the existing channel. New integration surfaces multiply failure modes; existing channels provide tested reliability.

name: research-blocked-items-before-applying-resolved-items
description: When a batch of items includes both resolved and blocked items: present research on all blocked items in one message before applying any resolved items to the artefact. Partial updates followed by a second pass degrade document coherence.

name: confirm-sample-workflow-before-writing-interaction-spec
description: When specifying a novel interaction pattern: present a sample workflow for author confirmation before writing the formal specification. Formal specs derived without confirmation embed unverified assumptions about the author's intent.

name: post-call-insight-synthesis
description: Given a call transcript and annotated call notes, generate a structured post-call note separating key analytical insights from to-dos; attribute insights to the party who contributed them; extract bilateral action items; format for email dispatch to the counterpart

name: grammar-and-formatting-cleanup-preserving-author-voice
description: Apply formatting and grammar corrections (sentence case, bold conventions, missing articles, subject-verb agreement, pronoun agreement, redundant phrases) without altering the author's vocabulary, sentence structure, stylistic fragments, or phrasing choices

name: batch-verify-names-from-all-sources
description: Extract proper names from all source documents simultaneously and present a consolidated verification list, rather than processing sources one at a time

name: use-calendar-as-authoritative-name-source
description: When verifying names in content anchored to specific dates, pull calendar events for those dates and use attendee names as the authoritative spelling source

name: stt-person-names-as-phonetic-approximations
description: When forced to choose between a name as rendered in speech-to-text output and the same name as found in calendar entries, written files, or email addresses: treat the STT rendering as a phonetic approximation; use the written source as canonical spelling

name: create-contact-file-on-new-entity-identification
description: When a new person is identified or a name error is corrected during document processing, create the contact file for the corrected identity before proceeding to the next processing phase

name: propagate-canonical-name-across-corpus
description: When establishing the canonical form of a name, search all prior documents in the working corpus for variant spellings and update them in the same session before committing

name: calculate-journey-duration-across-timezones
description: Calculate total journey duration from local departure and arrival times by converting both to UTC before computing elapsed time, accounting for timezone differences at origin and destination

name: structured-itinerary-entry
description: Return a structured itinerary entry with: flight number, carrier, departure time, departure city (airport code), arrival time, arrival city (airport code), layover duration if applicable, and total journey duration

name: unicode-file-edit-fallback
description: When exact string replacement in a file fails due to multi-byte unicode characters (e.g. →, —, curly quotes): use a programmatic replacement with explicit utf-8 encoding rather than retrying with the editor tool

name: read-derived-sheets-for-lookup
description: When populating dependent columns in a summary sheet, read existing derived sheets to build a lookup table rather than re-reading or reprocessing source data

name: mandatory-participants-within-cap-first
description: When a capacity cap is met exactly by mandatory participants: exclude non-mandatory participants; never remove mandatory participants to create room for non-mandatory ones

name: priority-flexible-participants-to-earliest-slot
description: When allocating flexible participants (available across multiple time slots) to capacity-constrained ordered cohorts: assign highest-priority flexible participants to the earliest available cohort rather than distributing them evenly

name: hard-constraints-before-capacity-constraints
description: Apply hard inclusion and exclusion constraints before capacity-based constraints when filtering a candidate set

name: verify-statutory-rates-before-computation
description: Fetch statutory contribution rates, percentage thresholds, and wage ceilings from official government or regulatory sources immediately before computation — training data captures past values and regulatory rates change on published announcement schedules

name: clarify-proration-convention-before-computing
description: When a proration calculation depends on a parameter that admits multiple valid conventions (e.g., whether public holidays count as working days): present the convention choice to the user before computing — the choice changes the denominator and cascades through all downstream figures

name: fetch-regulatory-rates-over-training-data
description: When forced to choose between using training-data regulatory figures and fetching current values from official sources: fetch from official sources — statutory rates, contribution ceilings, and levy percentages change on published announcement schedules and training data may reflect superseded values

name: apply-wage-cap-to-actual-period-wages
description: When applying a periodic statutory wage cap to a partial-period payment: apply the cap to wages actually paid in the period, not the full-period entitlement — the cap is a ceiling on wages received, not on the prorated rate

name: prorated-compensation-calculation
description: Return a prorated compensation calculation with: per-unit rate (total compensation ÷ units in period), prorated gross (per-unit rate × units worked), statutory deductions per type (rate, basis, computed amount), employee net pay (prorated gross − employee deductions), and total remittance per deduction type (employee share + employer share where applicable)

name: draft-data-collection-consent-notice
description: Draft statutory data collection consent notices specifying collection purposes, retention period, subject rights, and contact details

name: data-collection-consent-notice
description: Return a data collection consent notice with: (1) purposes list stating what data is used for, (2) retention period, (3) subject rights (access and correction), (4) contact for queries, (5) acknowledgement checkbox text

name: notification-not-opt-out-for-required-data
description: When data collection is required to deliver a service the person has voluntarily sought: use notification + express consent framing; do not use opt-out framing

name: check-daily-note-before-voice-note-insertion
description: Before adding content from a retrospective voice note to a target daily note, read the target note first to identify events already captured from prior processing sessions; insert only genuinely new content

name: stt-single-person-multiple-garbled-names
description: When a single voice-to-text transcript renders the same person as multiple different garbled names (e.g., phonetically similar variants in a list), treat all such variants as the same person; check especially when the speaker says 'X and his/her colleague Y' and both names resolve phonetically to the same known person

name: write-data-processing-handoff-on-context-pressure
description: When a session is consuming context rapidly processing multiple source files inline, write a HANDOFF.md before context runs out; include: source file paths with content-type notes, target output filenames with format notes, entity lists (new files needed and existing files to update), and next-session Agency dispatch instructions with wave structure

name: source-official-identifiers-from-primary-documents
description: Source all official identifiers (registration numbers, identification numbers, titles, appointment dates, addresses) from authoritative primary documents — filings, contracts, signed records — not from estimates, draft documents, or prior working files

name: represent-current-legal-position-in-external-documents
description: When a legal entity's authority to perform an activity is uncertain: represent the current unambiguous legal position in all external documents (insurance briefings, legal correspondence, contracts), not the intended future structure. Note the future structure as TBD separately.

name: organisational-reference-overview
description: Return an organisational reference document with: verified legal identifiers (entity name, registration number, type), named individuals with roles and tenure, programme or service parameters per offering type (scale, participant terms, funding structure), operational facts (premises, staffing, financials), and all unresolved items explicitly labelled as TBD

name: label-sections-for-counterparty-aligned-reviewer
description: When a structuring or legal document will be reviewed by a party whose interests may diverge from yours (e.g., counterparty's in-house counsel), mark each section and question [SUITABLE FOR X] or [NOT SUITABLE FOR X]; split any mixed-content sections so no SUITABLE section contains NOT SUITABLE implications. A section is NOT SUITABLE if it reveals the author's negotiating position, preferred outcome, or legal strategy against the counterparty.

name: frame-counsel-questions-as-how-not-whether
description: When asking questions of legal counsel about a desired outcome: frame as 'how do we achieve X?' not 'can we achieve X?' or 'what are our options for X?' The first framing instructs counsel to find the execution path; the second invites re-examination of the goal; the third invites broad exploration. Use the 'how' framing when the outcome is decided and you need implementation guidance.

name: map-stakeholder-interests-before-document-sharing
description: Before sharing any legal or structuring document with a third party whose interests may diverge from yours, map each section against each stakeholder's interests to identify: (a) sections that reveal your negotiating position or legal strategy vs (b) sections that provide mutually beneficial structural/regulatory context. Use this map to decide what to share, redact, or split.

name: three-category-expert-review-findings
description: Return three numbered lists: (1) APPEARS INCORRECT — claims or assertions in the reviewed document that are factually wrong or analytically incorrect from the reviewer's professional standpoint; (2) NEEDS EXPANSION — areas present in the document but covered insufficiently for professional adequacy; (3) NOT COVERED AT ALL — topics entirely absent from the document that a professional in this role would expect. Number items sequentially within each category. Order by significance, most important first.

name: multi-reviewer-synthesis-with-convergence
description: Return a deduplicated consolidated issue list preserving the source reviews' category structure. For each item: state the consolidated finding, note the convergence count (number of source reviewers who raised it), and list the distinct professional angles each reviewer contributed. Position items with convergence count ≥ 2 at the top of their category ahead of single-reviewer items.

name: spawn-synthesis-after-confirmed-parallel-completion
description: When parallel agents run before a synthesis step: spawn the synthesis agent only after receiving explicit completion confirmation from all parallel agents. Do not estimate or assume completion from elapsed time. Unconfirmed completion is not confirmed completion.

name: treat-transcript-additions-as-extensions
description: When a user supplements a voice transcript with additional items after initial extraction begins, incorporate each addition at the current phase without restarting the workflow from Phase 1

name: prefer-current-relevance-over-file-existence-for-links
description: When a repository file matching a person or topic exists but was created for a different context or time period: prefer current-activity relevance over file existence as the criterion for proposing a wikilink. Do not link to a file merely because it mentions the same entity.

name: flag-ambiguous-proper-noun-references
description: When processing input that contains references ambiguous between a proper noun and a common phrase, flag these during the initial extraction step and resolve with the user before proceeding to downstream processing phases

name: annotate-review-findings-with-proposed-fixes
description: When multi-agent review produces a structured findings document: annotate each finding with a blockquote response specifying (a) the target section(s) in the canonical document and (b) the proposed change; then use the annotated findings document as the working input for revising the canonical document. Version both files before modifying.

name: counsel-briefing-intention-not-specific-law
description: When briefing legal counsel on a structuring question: describe the intended outcome and constraints, then ask counsel to identify relevant legal and regulatory considerations — do not direct counsel to specific points of law identified through non-legal analysis. Agent-identified issue lists anchor counsel and crowd out issues they would have spotted independently. The goal of an initial brief is to establish the correct questions, not to obtain final answers.

name: structure-for-cheap-optionality
description: When advising on legal or organisational structuring with multiple possible future states: design the near-term structure to permit inexpensive realisation of desired future eventualities, not to instantiate those eventualities prematurely. For each decision point: what is the minimum needed now to keep this option open cheaply? Premature completeness adds immediate cost and complexity without adding optionality.

name: extract-fact-vs-intent-from-structuring-doc
description: Before reframing or significantly revising a legal or structuring working document: extract (1) claims of fact — what is currently known and established (entities, relationships, instruments, agreements, regulatory status) — and (2) claims of intent — what the parties have said they want or plan to do — into separate sections. Facts constrain what is possible now; intents define which options need to stay open. Conflating the two produces documents that treat desired outcomes as existing constraints.

name: write-methodology-note-in-agent-artefact
description: When producing a structured dataset in a spreadsheet or table that a future agent will need to read or update, write a methodology note to a clearly labelled cell or field in the same artefact, explaining: the data source, column structure and meaning, how to update for new entries, and how the data feeds downstream artefacts

name: deduplicate-before-appending-structured-rows
description: Before appending rows to an existing structured list (worksheet, table, or CSV), read existing entries, extract a set of unique identifiers, and write only rows whose identifier is absent from the existing data

name: state-connection-asks-as-role-context-purpose
description: When extracting requests for introductions or connections from transcripts or interviews, state each ask as role/expertise + industry/context + purpose compressed to one phrase specific enough that a person scanning their network would know who to think of; exclude tooling requests (hardware, software, API) and advisory requests (strategy, modelling); separate multiple asks with semicolons

name: guide-needs-list-from-interviews
description: Return a structured guide needs list with one row per distinct expertise type; columns: participant name(s), type of expertise (not job title), industry/sector, specific name if known, type of experience (what the guide needs to have done or know — not just their title); split compound asks into one row per distinct expertise type rather than merging to minimise row count

name: split-compound-extraction-at-semantic-boundary
description: When extracting compound items from source material into structured rows: create one row per distinct semantic unit rather than one row per source item; prefer completeness over row economy

name: create-gmail-drafts-via-oauth
description: When creating Gmail drafts programmatically for a Google Workspace account where gcloud tokens lack Gmail scope: (1) create a GCP project for the account domain, (2) enable Gmail API, (3) create an OAuth 2.0 client (Desktop app type), (4) download client JSON to ~/.config/<project>/gmail-oauth-client.json, (5) run google-auth-oauthlib InstalledAppFlow once to generate refresh token at ~/.config/<project>/gmail-token.json, (6) use google-api-python-client with Credentials.from_authorized_user_file() to call users().drafts().create(). To update a draft: delete and recreate — do not attempt in-place update.
