name: flag-and-relocate-column-collisions
description: When copying values into a spreadsheet column that may already contain non-target content: before writing, read the target column and identify cells with existing non-target content. Present collisions to the user showing current content and proposed new value. Move existing content to an adjacent empty column, then write the new value. Never silently overwrite existing cell content.

name: frame-decline-as-fit-not-merit
description: When drafting a communication declining an applicant, candidate, or proposal where reasons cannot or should not be detailed: frame the decline as a fit gap (the resources or capabilities we can offer do not match what this project or person needs) rather than a merit assessment (the project or applicant fell short). This preserves the relationship, is accurate without being specific, and keeps the door open for future engagement. Avoid words like rejection, declined, unsuccessful.

name: local-mcp-server-via-uv-fastmcp
description: When setting up a local MCP server that requires Google OAuth and must persist across Claude Code sessions: (1) write a Python script with PEP 723 inline dependency declarations (# /// script block listing mcp, google-auth-oauthlib, google-api-python-client); (2) implement tools using from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP; (3) add an --auth CLI flag that runs InstalledAppFlow.run_local_server(port=0), saves the token to ~/.config/<project>/token.json, then exits; (4) register with claude mcp add <name> -- uv run /absolute/path/to/script.py. Run the script once with --auth to complete the browser OAuth flow; subsequent MCP server runs load and auto-refresh the saved token. Store credentials JSON and token JSON in ~/.config/<project>/ — outside any repo.

name: add-gcloud-account-without-switching
description: When a GCP project is owned by a different Google account than the currently active gcloud account: run gcloud auth login (no special flags) and sign in with the owning account — gcloud preserves all previously authenticated accounts alongside the existing one. Use --account=EMAIL on all subsequent gcloud commands targeting that project. The default active account is unchanged. Note: --add-account flag does not exist in current gcloud versions.

name: launchd-one-shot-scheduled-job
description: To run a Python script once at a specific date and time on macOS: create a LaunchAgent plist at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist with StartCalendarInterval specifying Month, Day, Hour, Minute (uses local system time — verify timezone with date +%Z). Load with launchctl load <plist>. Have the script unload and delete the plist after running to prevent annual recurrence. Self-cleanup: subprocess.run(['launchctl', 'unload', str(PLIST_PATH)]) then PLIST_PATH.unlink(). Prefer over cron for macOS; launchd runs missed jobs on next wake if machine was asleep.

name: html-email-inline-base64-image
description: To embed an image (e.g. a signature) in an HTML email created via the Gmail API without CID MIME attachment complexity: read the image file, base64-encode it, and set the img src to data:image/png;base64,{b64}. Renders in Gmail and most email clients. Pattern: import base64; with open(path,'rb') as f: b64=base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode(); img_tag=f''

name: pdflatex-custom-paper-size
description: When producing a PDF with a non-standard paper size (e.g. 9x4in label, envelope, card) that does not require Obsidian wikilink resolution or system fonts: write a minimal LaTeX file and compile directly with pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode. Use \usepackage[paperwidth=X,paperheight=Y,top=...,left=...,right=...,bottom=...]{geometry} and \pagestyle{empty}. Faster and simpler than pandoc for this case; pdflatex is the native engine for Computer Modern fonts.

name: gmail-api-draft-consumed-on-failure
description: When sending Gmail drafts programmatically via users().drafts().send(): the draft is removed from the mailbox even when delivery fails due to a network error (timeout, connection reset). The draft ID becomes invalid on failure. For retry: reconstruct the full MIME message from scratch and call users().messages().send(userId='me', body={'raw': raw}) directly — no draft ID needed.

name: counsel-questions-as-client-intentions
description: When drafting questions for legal counsel, frame each question as the client's stated intention and desired outcome, not as a direction to a specific point of law — this keeps counsel free to surface considerations the non-lawyer drafter did not anticipate

name: minimum-structure-for-optionality
description: When designing a legal or corporate structure with uncertain future requirements: prefer the minimum structure that preserves desired options cheaply over a comprehensive structure that implements every possible future use case. For each design element, ask: what is the minimum we must do now to keep this option available later?

name: separate-facts-from-intents-for-counsel
description: When preparing a document for legal counsel review, separate claims of fact (statements independently verifiable by a court or regulator, describing what IS) from claims of intent (statements contingent on future decisions or aspirations, describing what parties WANT) into distinct sections

name: fact-intent-extraction-schema
description: Return two sections: (1) Claims of Fact — numbered statements independently verifiable by a court or regulator, grouped by sub-category; (2) Claims of Intent — numbered statements contingent on future decisions or aspirations, grouped by stakeholder. One claim per line. Add a third section Genuinely Ambiguous Claims for items that could be characterised as either, with the specific characterisation question stated for each.

name: raw-latex-longtable-for-column-width-control
description: When PDF output requires precise table column widths via obsidian-to-pdf.py (pandoc → xelatex pipeline): replace the markdown table with a raw {=latex} block containing a longtable environment using explicit p{X\linewidth} column specs. Pandoc pipe table separator proportions do not reliably control column widths in LaTeX output. Also: explicitly add \usepackage{longtable} to LATEX_HEADER — pandoc only auto-loads it for tables it generates itself, not for raw LaTeX blocks. Column math for 1:2.5:1:1 ratio with @{} outer padding: narrow = 0.167\linewidth, wide = 0.418\linewidth.

name: re-subn-function-for-backslash-replacements
description: When calling re.subn() or re.sub() with a replacement string containing backslashes (e.g. LaTeX strings with \linewidth or \begin), Python interprets those backslashes as regex backreference escape sequences and raises re.error: bad escape. Fix: pass a function as the replacement argument. The function receives the match object and returns the replacement string directly without regex escape interpretation.

name: filter-advisor-questions-to-expert-domain
description: When preparing questions for an external advisor (legal counsel, financial, regulatory): separate questions requiring the advisor's expert interpretation of statute, doctrine, or domain knowledge from questions that are business decisions the principals must make. Only expert-interpretation questions belong in the briefing. Business decisions should be resolved before the meeting, not delegated to the advisor.

name: analyse-individual-vs-collective-stakeholder-interest
description: Analyse where an individual stakeholder's optimal outcome diverges from the collectively optimal structure: identify the specific source of divergence (control leverage, compensation routing, liability exposure, fiduciary duty conflict) and characterise whether it is resolvable through instrument design or requires a structural trade-off between the parties.

name: tranche-investment-documentation-framework
description: Return a minimum documentation framework for tranche-based investments covering: (1) master agreement — elements governing the full relationship duration not repeated per tranche; (2) per-tranche instrument — minimum content per investment decision incorporating master by reference; (3) cumulative position register — fields tracking aggregate exposure per investee at any point; (4) investment decision memo — minimum record per decision for governance integrity and third-party due diligence.

name: document-dual-entity-functional-separation
description: When two entities controlled by overlapping principals operate as formally distinct but functionally connected units: document their operational separation with a written protocol specifying which decisions belong to each entity, who holds authority for each decision type, and the conditions under which an individual with roles in both entities must recuse — disclosure alone is insufficient.

name: verify-api-access-before-pipeline-design
description: Verify programmatic API access and data availability via live web research before declaring a source viable in a pipeline design

name: specify-tier-criteria-before-reviewing-evidence
description: Specify advancement criteria for each tier of a staged framework before reviewing evidence at that tier

name: survivorship-bias-reframe-as-signal-audit
description: When survivorship or selection bias cannot be mitigated in a validation dataset: do not claim validation. Reframe as signal existence auditing and state the reframe explicitly in all reporting.

name: recalibrate-scoring-for-source-gaps
description: When forced to choose between reporting results using a full scoring formula on an incomplete source set vs recalibrating the scoring formula to match available sources: recalibrate. Label results with the reduced formula and explicitly exclude the missing sources in all outputs.

name: pipeline-feasibility-research-output
description: For pipeline feasibility research, return: (1) data source assessment — source name, access method, API availability, temporal coverage, cost; (2) pipeline design — numbered steps from source to output with failure modes named; (3) minimal viable specification — what to build to test the pipeline; (4) 2-3 concrete verified candidates with sourcing notes; (5) feasibility verdict — high | medium | low with key constraints and improvement levers.

name: editorial-gap-compliance-review
description: Return a compliance review table for a written draft against a numbered list of editorial comments: for each comment, status (addressed | partially addressed | not addressed), evidence from the draft (quote or section reference), and if not addressed, specific gap and recommended addition. End with a summary count of statuses.

name: targeted-draft-expansion-with-insertion-points
description: Return a set of targeted draft additions: for each identified gap, proposed text with exact insertion location (sentence before/after in the target document), estimated word count, and citation requirement flags. Respect a stated word count ceiling for the final document.

name: flag-archive-only-claims
description: When fact-checking written work: distinguish web-verifiable claims from archive-only or interview-only claims; tag archive/interview claims with a flag (e.g. 📁) and exclude them from web verification; apply verification only to claims that could plausibly be confirmed or refuted by public sources.

name: inline-link-anchor-from-source-content
description: When embedding inline links in writing, use anchor text that is a natural grammatical phrase within the sentence and reflects content from the linked source — not a label describing what the source is about

name: quote-exact-text-when-flagging
description: When flagging specific passages for editorial revision, quote the exact text being flagged; do not paraphrase

name: cross-draft-synthesis-with-context
description: When identifying elements from one draft to incorporate into another, specify for each: the element to take (exact quote), the insertion location with one sentence of context before and after, and the original text at that location

name: anchor-text-content-over-label
description: When choosing anchor text for an inline link: prefer phrasing that IS the concept, term, or a brief inline definition (content from the source) over a phrase that describes what the source is about. A label fails if removing the link would leave a sentence making the same claim without the link's contribution

name: self-referential-link-naming-pattern
description: When an author links to their own prior writing: name the concept or term in the prose first, then link a brief defining clause immediately after it. The anchor text must be accurate to what the linked piece argues. Do not use the article title as anchor text unless the title itself is being discussed

name: multi-persona-editorial-synthesis
description: Return a consolidated numbered list divided into three sections: (1) keep — N items with rationale for each; (2) cut — N items with rationale; (3) change — N items each with the exact original text, the proposed replacement, and a one-sentence rationale. All items must quote exact text from the source document

name: describe-companies-on-first-link
description: When embedding a hyperlink to a named company or product in published writing, include a brief inline description of what the company does immediately adjacent to the link — as a parenthetical or which-clause — so readers unfamiliar with the company still follow the argument

name: group-claims-by-verifiability-for-fact-checking
description: When extracting claims for fact-checking, classify each as: factual (verifiable against external sources), judgment (author's interpretation), or illustrative (constructed example not representing a real entity). Apply a VERIFY flag to all claims involving specific numbers, dates, named companies, named products, or causal assertions

name: self-contained-social-posts-no-unexplained-references
description: When writing short-form social media posts: never reference a numbered type, category, or taxonomy that has not been established within the same post. If a taxonomy is central to the post's argument, briefly name it before invoking it. A reader who has not read the linked article must be able to follow the post without confusion

name: verify-before-asserting
description: When speed and accuracy conflict in answering a factual question: check the source before responding. Do not answer from a partial read or pattern-match on incomplete information. If a source check is not possible, explicitly flag the answer as unverified

name: mechanism-before-threshold-in-research-synthesis
description: When synthesising research findings for a client audience: lead with the mechanism that explains the phenomenon, not the headline statistic or threshold number. Statistics are supporting evidence; the mechanism is the argument

name: client-research-briefing-note
description: Return a briefing note (~800 words, two pages) structured as: (1) core finding — what the literature actually establishes; (2) named mechanisms — each explained individually; (3) quantitative evidence — what numbers exist and what they mean; (4) domain-specific implications — how findings apply to the client context; (5) intervention points — ranked by evidence quality. Append a full reference list

name: translate-academic-literature-for-practitioners
description: Translate findings from academic literature into practitioner-facing language: preserve the mechanism without the jargon, and distinguish clearly between what the evidence establishes and what it implies

name: proceed-autonomously-on-routine-decisions
description: When deciding whether to proceed or pause for user input: proceed autonomously on routine decisions derivable from context and preferences; pause only when the decision requires the user's subjective preference or involves irreversible actions on shared systems (external repos, production deployments, sent messages)

name: propagate-name-corrections-to-all-files
description: When an incorrect proper noun is discovered after it has already been written to multiple files: update all files containing the incorrect name before proceeding, rather than correcting only the primary document

name: create-org-level-index-for-client-files
description: When a client or organisation has accumulated many project files without an org-level index: create an index file that groups all related files by project phase or document category with wikilinks to each file

name: skill-phase-gates-apply-per-invocation
description: When a skill defines explicit phase gates with user approval checkpoints: apply those gates to every invocation of the skill within a session, not just the first. A second use of the same skill does not inherit approval from the first invocation

name: named-writer-lens-review
description: When reviewing a piece of writing adopt the editing lens of a specific named writer and apply only that writer's documented principles as criteria; map each finding to a specific passage with an exact quote

name: editorial-keep-cut-change-tripartite
description: Return three equal-length numbered lists: KEEP (exact passage quote and why it exemplifies the stated editing principle), CUT (exact passage quote and why it fails the principle), CHANGE (exact passage quote plus problem statement plus specific revised text replacing the original)

name: footnote-epistemic-caveats
description: When epistemic caveats about a claim's scope would interrupt the flow of analytical prose: consolidate them in a footnote; the inline sentence at the footnote marker must state the positive claim cleanly not the caveat itself

name: verify-academic-citation-metadata
description: For each academic citation verify on three axes before using: the DOI resolves to the named paper (not just any page loading at that URL), the listed author order matches the publication record, and the title is complete including any subtitle

name: distinguish-full-gaps-from-partial-gaps
description: In gap analysis: distinguish items fully absent from the document from items present in supporting sections but missing from primary prose

name: evaluate-full-document-not-only-prose
description: When reviewing a multi-section document: use the entire document as the evaluation surface, not only the main prose section

name: filter-examples-for-analogical-variable
description: Filter historical or case examples for the specific variable an argument claims is minimal; reject examples where that variable is high even when the general category matches

name: type-portrait-composite-for-unverified-example
description: When a concrete person example is needed but unverified, construct a type-portrait: describe the type specifically without naming or implying a real individual

name: gap-analysis-ordered-by-severity
description: When producing a gap analysis: order items by severity, most critical first, not by category or discovery sequence

name: identify-overused-rhetorical-constructions
description: Scan a draft for overused rhetorical constructions, enumerate all instances with locations, and for each propose an alternative that preserves meaning

name: write-rewrites-to-file-for-inline-editing
description: When proposing rewrites to a draft: write proposals to the beginning of the same file with originals and alternatives labelled, rather than only presenting them in conversation

name: four-lens-writing-review-with-synthesis
description: For long-form writing review: run four parallel agents — (1) craft prose quality, (2) craft structural editing, (3) genre writing guidelines, (4) genre editing guidelines — then a synthesis agent producing KEEP (max 7), CHANGE (max 10 ranked), CUT (max 6 ranked). Items flagged by 3+ agents are highest priority. Max-item constraints force prioritisation.

name: research-unknown-references-immediately
description: When processing voice notes or transcripts with unknown technical references (tool names, GitHub repos, product names): spawn a research agent in parallel with Phase 1 extraction rather than deferring to a to-do. Research enriches the current entry; deferral produces a weaker placeholder.

name: prefer-repo-paths-over-temp-paths
description: When storing tool output to files during a session: write to repo-tracked persistent paths rather than system temp paths. Temp directories (e.g. /var/folders/) do not survive session boundaries and will be silently lost.

name: verify-api-field-units-before-converting
description: Before converting any API field value using an assumed unit: cross-check the value range against a known reference (e.g. max(start_time) vs known duration) to confirm the unit before applying the conversion formula

name: composio-execute-over-run-for-structured-output
description: When extracting structured JSON from Composio tools: prefer composio execute over composio run. composio run emits ANSI escape codes and update notices to stdout even with --logs-off, corrupting structured output redirected to file.

name: attribute-all-claims-to-source-in-legal-prep
description: Attribute every factual claim, stated intention, and interpretation in a legal preparation document to its specific primary source with file path or URL; do not allow any unattributed claim to appear

name: legal-source-doc-comprehensiveness-over-concision
description: When drafting a source document for legal counsel: prefer comprehensiveness over concision; verbosity is acceptable provided all information from source documents is present and no information is duplicated

name: mark-instructing-party-interest-divergences
description: In a multi-stakeholder legal document prepared on behalf of an instructing party, identify and mark every point where the instructing party's interests diverge from those of other parties; do not mark divergences that exist only between non-instructing parties

name: attributed-comprehensive-legal-source-document
description: Return a legal source document where: every factual claim is attributed to a named source with file path or URL, every interpretation is explicitly labelled as interpretation not established fact, every stated intention is attributed to the party who stated it with date, every point of instructing-party interest divergence is marked, no information from source documents is omitted, and no information appears more than once

name: reconcile-contract-deliverables-against-payment-history
description: Cross-reference a contract's deliverable schedule against invoiced payment history to identify which deliverables have been paid, which remain outstanding, and the total value not yet invoiced

name: flag-outstanding-deliverables-past-contract-expiry
description: When outstanding deliverables exist past a contract's end date: flag the need for a contract amendment or extension before invoicing can proceed, not after submitting the invoice. Invoices submitted against an expired contract may be rejected or require rework.

name: fallback-to-local-file-on-cloud-access-failure
description: When cloud document access fails (authentication wall, MCP 'not found' error, or export URL returning a sign-in page): check the local filesystem for a downloaded copy of the same document before reporting it as inaccessible. Cloud tools authenticate as a specific account; the same document may be available locally regardless of cloud auth state.

name: scan-for-unprocessed-inline-annotations
description: Scan for unprocessed inline annotations — bracket-delimited notes and raw `- add...` bullet lines — as incompleteness signals in a synthesised document

name: evaluate-synthesis-completeness-top-down
description: When evaluating whether a synthesised document covers its source materials: read the full synthesis document first, then check sources for uncovered sections. Bottom-up (sources-first) checking produces false negatives because synthesis reorganises content from multiple sources into a different structure.

name: classify-each-content-line-by-single-type
description: Classify each substantive line in a document as exactly one type from a specified taxonomy; treat lines containing mixed types as classification errors requiring line splits

name: split-mixed-type-lines-over-dominant-type
description: When a content line contains both factual content and analysis or inference: split into separate single-type lines rather than labelling with the dominant type; classification integrity takes priority over document concision

name: type-classified-document-with-attributed-sources
description: Return a document where: every substantive content line carries exactly one type prefix in the format [TYPE | source], mixed-type lines have been split, all type prefixes conform to the specified taxonomy, attribution sources are wikilinked to primary source documents, and section headers, blank lines, and document metadata carry no type markers

name: sequence-legal-questions-for-minimum-informativeness
description: Sequence questions for legal counsel so that each question reveals only the minimum information needed for counsel to answer it, and each answer determines whether subsequent questions remain relevant or should be skipped

name: reveal-minimum-to-counsel-over-full-disclosure
description: When designing a question sequence for legal counsel: reveal only the minimum information needed for each question rather than disclosing the full strategic intent upfront; earlier answers determine whether later questions remain relevant or are moot

name: flag-entity-objects-vs-current-activities
description: Compare an entity's constitutional or statutory objects against its current operational activities; flag every activity that falls outside the stated objects as a compliance gap requiring constitutional amendment or cessation

name: gated-legal-question-sequence-document
description: Return a legal question sequence document with: a numbered factual context section attributing each fact to its primary source, a narrative section describing the entity's proposed activities, questions sequenced so each is gated on prior answers and reveals minimum information, and a terminal synthesis question that leads counsel to the target conclusion without stating it directly

name: transcribe-embedded-images-to-attributed-content-lines
description: Transcribe text from images embedded in a document, adding each transcription as a verbatim content line immediately following the embed, attributed to the document containing the embed

name: update-references-to-current-filename-not-stub
description: When a referenced document has been renamed or deprecated: update all inline references and links to use the new current filename rather than creating stub redirect files — stubs silently create empty notes on click and obscure which document is canonical

name: apply-and-remove-inline-annotation-instructions
description: Process each inline annotation instruction in a document's body text: apply the specified change to the surrounding content, then delete the annotation instruction text itself, leaving only the final edited content

name: labeled-document-compliance-check-report
description: Return a compliance check report for a labeled document with: for each compliance rule, a count of violations with exact line numbers grouped by violation subcategory; a distinction between errors and intentional exceptions; and a summary table mapping check name to issue count

name: read-all-target-documents-before-numbering-new-entries
description: When adding sequentially numbered entries to multiple existing documents, read all target documents first to verify the current last entry number before assigning new numbers

name: route-multi-date-transcript-entries-to-date-specific-files
description: When a voice transcript spans multiple calendar dates, map each activity cluster to its calendar date and write entries to the corresponding date-specific file

name: verify-visual-output-by-rendering
description: For layout, alignment, sizing, colour-space, or other visual/format requirements, verify by rendering or inspecting the produced artifact (rasterise and measure pixels, grep the compiled file for colour operators, read the true bounding box) rather than trusting source coordinates or maths; source-level correctness does not guarantee output-level correctness

name: prefer-execution-log-timestamps-for-day-attribution
description: When reconstructing which calendar day an action occurred and file mtimes, version-control author-dates, and execution-log timestamps disagree: use the execution-log timestamp, converting to local time before bucketing by day. Treat author-dates as unreliable when work is batch-committed and mtimes as unreliable when files are synced or edited later.

name: verify-no-unique-content-before-deleting-stale-file
description: Before deleting or overwriting a file described as stale or duplicate, diff it against the canonical version; if it holds unique still-active content, surface the contradiction instead of proceeding.

name: dedicated-step-with-mechanism-over-restating-ignored-instruction
description: When an instruction is reliably ignored: diagnose whether it is buried and lacks a concrete procedure, and fix by promoting it to a dedicated step that names a specific mechanism — not by restating it more forcefully.

name: rebuild-or-retire-irreconcilable-mirror
description: When a downstream mirror or derived copy has diverged from its source into an irreconcilable state (unrelated history, no fast-forward path) and holds no unique content: rebuild it wholesale from the source or retire it, rather than attempting to merge the divergent states.

name: correct-known-wrong-record-at-source
description: When you discover an earlier recorded claim, diagnosis, or attribution was wrong, correct it at the source record immediately — not only going forward; a superseded explanation left in place propagates as fact.

name: corpus-grounded-match-with-tiers-and-gaps
description: Return a per-claim match against a fixed corpus: for each extracted claim, a tier — STRONG (cite the matching item's id and why it fits), LOOSE (cite the nearest item and what differs), or NO-MATCH — plus a running gap list collecting every NO-MATCH for later authoring. Every STRONG and LOOSE must cite the actual corpus item so the grounding is inspectable; do not invent corpus support.

name: reconcile-selfreported-dates-against-calendar
description: When self-reported day or date labels in a recollection or voice note conflict with a structured schedule (calendar, itinerary) covering the same events: treat the schedule as authoritative where it is internally consistent, confirm the offset using an internal anchor in the self-report (e.g. a named weekday), apply the resulting date shift uniformly across all entries, and surface the discrepancy for confirmation before writing.

name: record-user-attested-fact-as-account
description: When a fact is attested by the user (the principal) but cannot be independently verified from a public source: record it as the user's account, attributed, and link any partially corroborating external context as unconfirmed — rather than asserting it as verified fact or omitting it.

name: execute-embedded-instructions-as-scope
description: When a source document being processed contains instructions directed at the processor (create files, look up references, enrich another file): treat them as task scope to execute, not as content to transcribe into the output.

name: sorted-insert-over-resort-or-append
description: When adding rows to an existing human-sorted reference table (registry, glossary, index): insert each row at its correct sorted position by key comparison — not re-sort the whole table (which reorders intentional manual rows) nor append at the end (which breaks the sort).

name: resolve-layer-before-judging-competition
description: When two models, instruments, or designs appear to compete, identify which structural layer each occupies before choosing between them; designs at different layers are candidates for composition rather than mutually exclusive alternatives

name: anchor-framework-in-established-tradition
description: Map each element of a novel or personal framework to a specific canonical thinker, work, and concept in the established intellectual tradition it draws on

name: commit-only-session-authored-files
description: When uncommitted changes from a parallel session are present in the working tree: stage only the files this session authored, never git add -A across the whole tree

name: project-reference-index
description: Return a project reference index grouping sources by category (work product, internal references, external references); each row contains a file link, creation date, last-touched date, and one-line description

name: extract-tracked-changes-redline
description: Extract a Word document's tracked changes (insertions, deletions, authors) into an ordered redline flagging every changed paragraph

name: review-counterparty-markup-by-materiality
description: Review a counterparty's contract markup from one party's perspective, tiering substantive changes by materiality and separating them from cosmetic edits

name: liability-carveout-outside-cap-is-unlimited
description: When a liability clause places an obligation outside both the damages exclusion and the cap (e.g. confidentiality breaches): treat it as unlimited exposure and push back; prefer excluding indirect and consequential loss while capping remaining liability at a defined low figure such as fees paid

name: breach-charge-compensatory-not-deterrent
description: When setting a charge payable on a party's breach (e.g. a late-payment surcharge): size it as a genuine pre-estimate of loss rather than a deterrent, or it risks being void as a penalty; to apply stronger pressure use a discount for compliant behaviour, which is not breach-triggered

name: list-accept-by-silence-items-in-markup-response
description: When responding to a counterparty's marked-up agreement: explicitly list the proposed changes you are not contesting as accept-by-silence items for confirmation, rather than letting a blanket 'most changes are fine' silently concede everything unraised

name: override-requires-explicit-precedence
description: When a baseline rule is meant to be overridable by a subordinate document (annex, scope of work, config): require an explicit order-of-precedence statement that the subordinate prevails on the overridden subjects, and reject any general 'parent prevails over children' clause that would silently neutralise the override

name: assess-clause-interactions-not-in-isolation
description: When reviewing a multi-part document for one party's interests: assess how individually-acceptable changes compound across parts, not each part in isolation, and flag interactions that worsen the party's position

name: contract-markup-evaluation
description: Return a contract-markup evaluation with: the reviewing party's perspective stated; a cosmetic-versus-substantive split; substantive changes tiered (push back | defensible | neutral) each with clause reference, plain-language impact, and recommendation; an accept-by-silence list; and outstanding items to fill or confirm

name: build-substance-inventory-before-paraphrasing
description: Build a numbered per-paragraph inventory of every substantive point, name, figure, date, and quote before paraphrasing a source text; use it as the drafting checklist and review baseline

name: classify-paraphrase-fidelity-per-point
description: Classify each mapped source point in a paraphrase as PRESERVED, ALTERED, or DROPPED with side-by-side quotes for changes; list ADDED substance separately

name: scope-similarity-review-with-exclusions
description: Specify an explicit exclusion list (proper nouns, official names, direct quotes, technical terms) and severity tiers when commissioning textual-similarity review

name: substance-fidelity-over-wording-distance
description: When rewording a text for republication and fidelity to substance conflicts with distance from wording: preserve substance exactly (names, numbers, quotes verbatim) and create distance only in phrasing, syntax, and ordering

name: reorder-factual-lists-to-reduce-fingerprint
description: When a reworded text retains factual lists whose item order carries no meaning: reorder the items rather than preserving source order; order is fingerprint, not substance

name: similarity-report-side-by-side
description: Return a similarity report with: findings ordered by severity tier, each quoting source and derived passage side by side with a location key, and a one-line overall distinctness verdict

name: paraphrase-fidelity-report
description: Return a fidelity report with: per-item verdicts keyed to the source inventory, side-by-side quotes for each ALTERED or DROPPED item, a separate ADDED-content list, and a verbatim-check table of names, numbers, dates, and quotes

name: avoid-overstating-legal-basis-in-claims
description: When drafting a demand, claim, or complaint, cite the applicable framework accurately and rest the claim on its strongest defensible ground; do not overstate entitlement by invoking a regulation or right that does not apply (e.g. citing a delay-compensation rule where the flight was not delayed). A single overstated basis gives the counterparty grounds to dismiss the entire claim.

name: consolidate-grievance-into-single-channel
description: Submit a multi-issue complaint or claim through one channel as a single submission rather than splitting it across issue-specific forms. Splitting generates separate case references handled by different teams, each weaker in isolation and harder to escalate as a whole. Attach supporting detail to the one submission and retain its case reference for escalation.

name: canonical-anchor-maps-sources-not-duplicates
description: When a project's model or thesis is spread across many source documents: create a canonical anchor document that maps to the authoritative sources with wikilinks (each source stays authoritative for its own content) and additionally houses only the cross-cutting theses that have no single home in any one source; do not copy source content into the anchor

name: mark-extrapolation-inline-for-author-review
description: When asked to develop a thesis or argument grounded in existing source documents: draft it from what the sources support and insert an explicit inline review marker at each claim that goes beyond the sources, so the author can adjudicate the extrapolations rather than have them silently embedded in the draft

name: distinguish-mention-from-affiliation
description: When a person describes, recommends, or cites a third-party entity, do not infer their employment, ownership, or affiliation with it; record it as a cited example unless there is direct evidence of association

name: prefer-least-external-help-in-self-service
description: When optimising a product or process for self-service and two options both satisfy a requirement: choose the option that needs the least outside help (no facilitator, no vendor contact, no specialist). Self-service is the tie-breaker for every design decision.

name: present-ranked-labelled-source-candidates-before-building
description: Before building on existing source documents, present them ranked by relevance, labelled by role (authoritative source / supporting guidance / framing material), and confirm which are authoritative before using them

name: let-timer-end-timed-phases-by-default
description: When running a timed multi-phase group process: let the phase timer end each phase by default rather than waiting for the discussion to peter out. The facilitator may override (advance early, or grant one bounded extension) only as the exception.

name: timebox-phases-with-midpoint-notification
description: Timebox each phase of a group process to a fixed determinate duration and fire a half-time notification at the temporal midpoint to trigger the group midpoint-transition effect

name: restrict-ai-to-low-discretion-support
description: When adding AI assistance to a human-judgement workflow: let the AI perform only low-discretion support tasks (paraphrase, reformat, retrieve, summarise). It must never make, merge, or finalise the humans decisions. Draft-and-suggest, never decide.

name: search-connected-sources-before-asking-user
description: When forced to choose between asking the user for missing factual details (bookings, confirmations, reference data) and searching available connected sources (email, calendar, project files): search the sources first; ask the user only after the searches return nothing

name: embed-entry-conventions-in-living-log-documents
description: Embed entry conventions (ordering, entry format, required fields) at the top of a living log document so future edits follow them without external context

name: encrypted-artefact-over-bare-hash-for-confidential-verifiability
description: When a record must be publicly tamper-evident but its content confidential: commit an encrypted artefact with a per-item key rather than a bare hash fingerprint — encryption keeps the content recoverable from the public record and per-item keys allow selective disclosure; use a salted hash only when recoverability is not required

name: sweep-downstream-artefacts-after-spec-correction
description: After a specification decision is corrected or reversed, sweep all downstream artefacts — plans, error messages, fix-text strings, tests, operator guidance — for the surviving deprecated version

name: write-resolution-back-to-soliciting-file
description: When a decision solicited in an annotatable file is resolved elsewhere, record the resolution in that file's annotation space with a pointer to the authoritative record

name: simulate-screens-as-builder
description: Simulate each specified screen as its builder: check element inventory, states (first-load/empty/error), cross-role simultaneity, data availability at render time, and transitions

name: review-confirms-what-is-sound
description: End every review report with an explicit list of what was checked and found sound, so silence is not ambiguous; keep it brief relative to findings

name: specify-empty-state-behaviour
description: When a spec promises an output for a lifecycle state where its underlying data may not exist: specify the empty or partial behaviour explicitly; never leave the missing-data case to the implementer

name: decision-landing-audit
description: When reviewing a document produced from prior decision rounds, return a decision-landing audit: for each prior decision and fix, mark LANDED | LANDED-PARTIALLY (name where it is missing) | ALTERED (name how) | NOT FOUND, ordered by the decision record

name: verify-hardest-contracts-against-chosen-platform
description: Before recommending a technology stack, walk the one or two hardest system contracts mechanism-by-mechanism against the platform's actual primitives, naming the specific APIs used — never assert fit without the walkthrough

name: structural-recovery-over-tested-recovery
description: When mitigating crash-recovery risk: prefer a design where recovery is the only code path (write-through persistence; one rebuild function used identically for cold start, crash recovery, and reconnect; timers derived from persisted state) over a separate recovery path de-risked by testing — testing then verifies the design instead of carrying the risk

name: reweigh-not-defend-on-principal-challenge
description: When the principal questions a rejected alternative: re-examine it honestly and present the choice as an explicit weighting decision showing what each option genuinely wins, rather than defending the original recommendation

name: deliver-identity-bearing-links-privately
description: When resharing a link that doubles as its holder's identity or capability (personal join link, magic link): deliver it to that person through a private channel (direct message), never into a shared or group channel — anyone using the link becomes them

name: no-authentication-on-link-fetch
description: Design emailed sign-in links to authenticate on an explicit confirm action (POST), never on the link fetch itself — corporate mail scanners pre-fetch every URL and will consume fetch-authenticated links

name: complete-partial-artifact-after-agent-death
description: When a long-running file-writing agent dies before its final report (rate limit, crash) and the target artifact is partially written: dispatch a completion agent that reads the full partial artifact and matches its conventions before continuing — do not restart from scratch or complete blind

name: partition-shared-id-namespace-before-parallel-dispatch
description: When parallel agents will each extend a shared identifier registry (finding numbers, gap IDs, decision entries): partition the namespace per agent before dispatch; on post-hoc collision, renumber at the merge boundary before any downstream consumer reads the registry

name: back-record-derived-resolutions-in-canon
description: When a downstream document resolves an open gap by derivation from the canonical design document, record the resolution in the canon immediately, citing the derivation and its source

name: blocked-stub-for-missing-policy-parameters
description: When a plan requires policy parameters that exist in no authoritative source, add a blocked stub task naming each missing parameter, what it gates, and its decision owner — never supply invented values

name: re-verify-executor-success-reports
description: When an executor agent reports success (tests passing, artifact complete): re-run the verification command independently before recording completion or evaluating the work, rather than trusting the report

name: intent-form-messages-for-pre-action-commits
description: When an audit commit lands before the database write that completes the operation: word the commit message as intention (operation in progress), so an orphaned commit reads as an aborted operation rather than tampering

name: isolate-nested-git-repo-from-parent
description: When initialising a git repository inside a directory tracked by a parent repository, untrack the subtree from the parent (git rm -r --cached) and gitignore it in the parent to prevent future gitlink entries from bulk adds

name: derive-reviewer-personas-from-venue-audience
description: When simulating peer review for a target publication venue: derive reviewer personas from the venue's actual audience communities, paired so the reviewer set spans that audience's breadth of views rather than generic distinct perspectives

name: referee-report-with-satisfaction-conditions
description: Return a referee report with: reviewer stance (2-3 sentences), summary of the work's argument as the reviewer understands it, numbered reasons to continue the review process, numbered reasons to reject each with an explicit condition that would satisfy the objection, and an overall disposition (reject | major revisions | minor revisions | accept) with rationale

name: recreate-on-stale-external-identifier
description: When a stored external identifier (project ID, task ID, resource handle) returns not-found: re-list the service's current entities and create a replacement rather than retrying or assuming transient failure, then update every continuity record that stored the stale identifier

name: report-history-section-with-time-window
description: A report produced by an agent pipeline must open with a history section stating: the originating brief, the composition method and executing-agent or task identifiers, per-step actions, and the explicit date and local-time window in which the actions occurred

name: section-files-over-shared-file-for-parallel-writers
description: When multiple parallel agents contribute sections to a single document: have each agent write its own section file and assemble them verbatim afterwards; never allow parallel agents to write concurrently to one shared file

name: resolve-most-constraining-decision-first
description: Resolve the decision that constrains the most other open decisions first, and state which downstream decisions it constrains and how

name: state-foreclosed-options-before-presenting-decision
description: When presenting a decision late in a sequence of related decisions: restate the live options, naming which original options earlier resolutions have foreclosed and why, rather than presenting the original option list unchanged

name: attack-vector-map
description: Return an attack-vector map for a contested claim: numbered attacks, each with the objection stated precisely, the community it comes from, a severity rating (HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW), and the strongest available reply with citations

name: engagement-depth-map-with-omit
description: Return an engagement-depth map for source literatures: for each cluster, the key works, an engagement level (TEXT | FOOTNOTE | OMIT), and a one-line reason. Treat OMIT as a real level: note where citing a source would signal a commitment the work does not make

name: minimal-commitment-strategy
description: Return a minimal-commitment strategy for a contested position: the smallest set of numbered commitments that sustains it, each with what it buys and what it costs, sized to a stated length budget

name: dissolve-objections-over-answering
description: When defending a claim against anticipated objections: prefer a reformulation that makes an objection inapplicable over a point-by-point reply; answer only objections that survive reformulation

name: verify-formal-support-before-defending
description: When recommending defend vs weaken for a contested claim: first check what the supporting formal material (proofs, data, specs) actually establishes; if it establishes a weaker claim, recommend the weaker claim stated precisely rather than defending the original

name: reframe-structural-objections-as-support
description: Where an objection restates a structural feature of the position, reframe it as evidence for the position instead of rebutting it

name: batch-audit-shared-artifacts-after-decision-sequence
description: When sequential decisions each affect shared artifacts (examples, cases, diagrams): audit all affected artifacts together after the full sequence resolves, not incrementally after each decision

name: walk-newcomer-entry-journey-first
description: When reviewing operating instructions or conventions, walk a newcomer's entry journey step by step before reviewing maintenance procedures; flag any entry step the document does not specify

name: declared-mutable-zones-over-blanket-immutability
description: When a file must be both append-only and kept current: declare explicit mutable zones (header block, pinned sections) that may be edited in place, rather than rewriting history or duplicating current state elsewhere; prohibit in-place edits outside declared zones

name: flag-stale-references-in-records-not-rewrite
description: When historical records contain stale paths or references after a restructure: flag the staleness in the record's header and put corrected references in the current pointer document; never rewrite the record body — that falsifies history

name: staged-migration-with-recorded-remainder
description: When a full migration or retrofit would disrupt active work: migrate in stages and record exactly what remains in a central registry until complete; never leave the remainder implicit

name: classify-files-by-change-regime
description: Classify each document as an immutable record or a living current-state document before editing, and apply the matching update discipline: records change by adding sections, living documents by creating a new version

name: operating-instructions-document
description: Return an operating-instructions document with: purpose headmatter readable by humans and machines, an entry procedure for the most common journey, core procedures in lifecycle order, declared exceptions to general rules, and a registry or index of governed items

name: merge-concurrent-writer-changes-over-reapplying
description: When an edit fails because another writer changed a shared file mid-session: re-read the file, preserve the other writer's changes, and merge your change into the file's change record; never reapply your original edit over theirs

name: stub-behind-interface-at-dependency-boundaries
description: When a capability is consumed by an earlier build phase than the one that implements it: have the earlier phase own the interface plus a minimal stub, and the later phase implement behind the unchanged interface — never pull the implementation forward or fork a temporary code path

name: plan-coverage-ownership-table
description: Return a coverage table mapping every specification item to exactly one owning phase or work package, with consumer references marked distinctly from ownership, plus a count check showing items in spec = items assigned; nothing unassigned, nothing double-owned

name: prove-safety-test-catches-planted-defect
description: Before trusting a safety-net test (crash drill, invariant check, guard), deliberately introduce the defect it exists to catch and verify the test fails

name: enforce-conventions-as-build-failing-checks
description: Convert spec and style conventions into automated build-failing checks (lint rules, CI greps) rather than relying on reviewer discipline

name: freeze-as-built-contracts-at-phase-exit
description: At the end of a build phase, reconcile planned interface contracts against the implementation, record the as-built shapes in a contracts document, and route later changes through an explicit change rule

name: update-living-links-flag-stale-in-records
description: When renaming files that other documents link to: update links in living and current documents, but do not rewrite links inside superseded or historical records — that falsifies them; flag the staleness in the record's headmatter with a pointer to where current references live

name: measure-beta-cost-in-throwaway-code-not-provisioning
description: When configuring a beta or dress-rehearsal deployment: measure cheapness in beta-only code written, not in signups or spend avoided — if a real service swaps in later by config change, reuse the borrowed one; if avoiding provisioning requires code the product will not keep, provision the real service

name: route-all-mutations-through-one-dispatch-path
description: Route every state mutation — transport events, timer firings, lifecycle calls — through a single dispatch path so serialisation, persistence ordering, and testing have one door

name: publisher-record-over-aggregator
description: When verifying a citation and sources differ in authority: accept only publisher-deposited records (CrossRef API, arXiv API, official proceedings pages); never accept an aggregator or search-summary entry over them. Verify before the reference list is finalised, not after

name: report-sweeps-as-counts
description: When reporting the result of a stylistic or vocabulary sweep: report before/after counts from a searchable pattern, not qualitative impressions. If a pattern cannot be counted, say so explicitly

name: defer-edits-to-author-open-files
description: When a target file may be open in the author's live editor: defer non-urgent in-place edits (supersession pointers, headmatter) and record the deferral in the successor document, because an external write can destroy the author's unsaved edits

name: audit-examples-jointly-with-evidence
description: Audit all illustrative examples together with the full governing decision set in context; give each a per-criterion verdict (PASS / FAIL / PASS-WITH-REWRITE) backed by quoted textual evidence

name: gate-drafting-on-fork-ratification
description: When downstream drafting depends on an open authorial fork: present the fork as options with a reasoned recommendation and do not dispatch the dependent drafting until the author ratifies

name: two-readings-example-construction
description: Rewrite an example vulnerable to a domestication objection as a two-readings case: concede the reading existing tools handle, then assert the reading they cannot

name: derive-documents-programmatically-not-by-retyping
description: When producing a derivative document that must share a body with its source (preprint from submission, mirror, excerpt): extract the shared body programmatically from the source file on disk and verify containment, rather than retyping from context. Retyped bodies silently revert author edits made since the context was loaded

name: exact-delimiter-link-renaming
description: When renaming wiki-linked files, rewrite inbound links by matching the full link token with its closing delimiter (]] or | or #), processing longest names first, so short names cannot clobber longer variants

name: runtime-clock-in-scripted-writes
description: When a script or heredoc writes a timestamp into a file: interpolate a value captured from the system clock at execution time; never embed a timestamp constant composed before the run

name: derive-check-values-from-authoritative-module
description: When building a reference-by-name or single-source check, derive the guarded value set from the authoritative constants module at check time; never hand-maintain the list; exempt only the file that IS the value-by-value spec test

name: deterministic-fault-injection-over-realistic
description: When implementing a deliberate fault for a self-check: prefer a deterministic fault (fixed delay, forced ordering) over a realistic-but-racy one; a flaky self-check is worse than a less realistic one

name: independent-projection-reference-model
description: Build consistency drills against an independent reference reducer producing a canonical comparable projection (sorted collections, volatile handles excluded); share type definitions with the system under test, never reducer code

name: torn-write-adjacency-invariants
description: Encode multi-step atomic operations as adjacency invariants over the persisted event log (step N must be immediately followed by its paired step) so partially persisted batches are detectable after a crash

name: designed-behaviour-before-code-changes
description: When a test fails after a time- or liveness-driven feature lands: first determine whether the system is behaving as designed before changing product code; if it is, fix the test fixture and leave the code alone

name: simulate-liveness-in-clock-advancing-tests
description: Route long mock-clock advances in tests through a helper that simulates participant or client liveness at sub-timeout intervals; reserve silent advances for tests of the liveness features themselves

name: deadline-keyed-fired-markers
description: Key one-shot timer fired-markers to the deadline value they fired for, so any change that moves the deadline (extension, pause shift) re-arms the timer without separate re-arm bookkeeping

name: valid-biased-generators-keep-refusals
description: When generating random command sequences for property tests: bias toward valid commands but do not filter out invalid ones; refusal paths are part of the tested surface

name: empirical-durability-floors
description: Track durability expectations empirically during driven tests: read the persisted high-water mark after each acknowledgement and require the post-crash log to meet the floor recorded at the last acknowledged command

name: as-built-contracts-document
description: Return an as-built contracts document with: per-contract API signatures as implemented, wire/event grammar with payload shapes, data schemas, every delta from the planned sketch noted in place, and a commitment-traceability table mapping each binding commitment to named passing tests

name: verify-integration-seams-against-frozen-source
description: Verify each planned integration seam against the consumed interface's actual source code, not a remembered or summarised contract

name: shared-utilities-live-in-the-shared-wave
description: When a utility is consumed by more than one parallel track: build it in the shared preceding wave, not inside one track. A parallel track must never depend on a sibling track's output.

name: rate-limit-unauthenticated-send-triggers
description: Rate-limit every unauthenticated endpoint that triggers outbound sends, per identifier and per IP, with limits as named constants

name: never-disclose-account-existence
description: When an unauthenticated request looks up an account (restore, link re-request): return an identical response whether or not a match exists. Never confirm account existence to an unauthenticated caller.

name: interim-config-over-hardcoded-placeholder
description: When a required value depends on infrastructure that does not yet exist (domain, account, address): make it a configuration key with a documented interim value - never a hardcoded placeholder, never an invented value.

name: retune-detection-when-warning-becomes-denial
description: When a detection heuristic's consequence escalates from warning to denial: retune towards fewer false positives and act only on confident detections - a false positive now blocks a legitimate user.

name: classify-approval-annotations-by-level
description: Classify each approval annotation as artefact-level or spec-level; cascade spec-level changes into a new spec version and canon record before the artefact freezes

name: hermetic-ci-with-one-real-exit-run
description: When CI determinism conflicts with end-to-end realism against an external service: run CI against a local boundary stub, and keep one recorded run against the real service's test mode as the exit gate.

name: plain-language-approval-readback
description: Return a plain-language approval readback of a technical plan: one jargon-free section per block and per decision, an annotation slot under each item (blank = approved), and a three-option approval box (approve as-is | approve with changes | hold)

name: partition-runtime-resources-for-parallel-workers
description: Partition runtime resources (ports, temporary databases, test-identifier ranges) across parallel workers explicitly in each dispatch prompt

name: single-owner-for-shared-files-in-parallel-work
description: Assign exactly one named owner for any file that multiple parallel tasks would otherwise modify

name: verify-merged-tree-after-parallel-tracks
description: Run the full combined verification suite on the merged tree after parallel tracks land and before integration work begins; treat per-track success as insufficient

name: record-as-implemented-deltas-in-frozen-contracts
description: After implementing an approved amendment to a frozen contract, record the as-implemented deltas in the contract document itself

name: resume-partial-artefact-not-restart
description: When a worker died mid-task leaving a partial artefact: inspect the artefact first; if substantially complete, continue from it matching its conventions; do not restart from scratch

name: refetch-single-use-credentials-on-failure
description: When a single-use credential fails validation: obtain a fresh credential from the issuer and transmit it verbatim; never retry or retype the failed token

name: never-lose-assertions-across-a-rewrite
description: When a refactor makes existing tests obsolete: rewrite them against the new behaviour; never let the total assertion count decrease across a change

name: diagnose-off-voice-prose-against-published-corpus
description: When a draft written in a target author's voice reads stilted or off-voice: diagnose it against the author's live published corpus using countable mechanical features (sentence-length variance, fragment rate, parenthetical density, contraction rate, transition type), not subjective feel; the fixes are mechanical

name: default-to-contractions-in-conversational-prose
description: When choosing between contracted and full verb forms in conversational or newsletter-register prose: default to contractions (roughly 75-80 percent or more of eligible instances); reserve full forms for emphasis and definitional sentences. A near-zero-contraction draft reads stilted

name: style-rule-list-with-verbatim-evidence
description: Return a writing-style rule list where each rule is a mechanically actionable instruction (an action a writer can take, or a countable quota) backed by a verbatim quote from the source corpus, grouped by dimension (openings, rhythm, diction, self-reference, links, closings)

name: verify-temporal-claims-against-canonical-source
description: Verify every temporal or factual claim in a draft (elapsed time, dates, publication gaps, counts) against the canonical live source before drafting the sentence, not after

name: do-not-force-voice-tokens-to-hit-a-register
description: When imitating an author's casual voice: deploy their signature tokens (slang, emoji, internet abbreviations) only where they arise naturally; do not insert them to hit a casualness target - forced tokens read as performed

name: verify-claim-in-native-language-before-softening
description: When an English-language search cannot verify the specifics of a claim about a non-English-speaking place, person, or institution: search the local/native-language record before softening or dropping the claim; treat an honest not-found in the native language as a valid result (soften or attribute), not merely a failed search

name: cite-the-series-that-matches-the-stated-figure
description: When a headline statistic exists in several measures or from several institutions (e.g. current-USD vs PPP, one agency vs another): cite the specific series and institution whose published value matches the number stated in the text, not a near-neighbour whose different value will read as inconsistent

name: reject-edits-that-break-a-hard-style-constraint
description: When a suggested edit would improve a text but violates a hard style constraint (e.g. a rarity limit on a punctuation mark, a prohibited-word list): reject the edit or find a rephrasing that satisfies the constraint; do not accept the local improvement at the constraint's expense

name: link-anchor-options-list
description: Return a numbered link-sourcing list where each item gives: the anchor phrase in the source text, 2-3 candidate URLs each fetched and confirmed live (with exact page title and a one-line fit note), a recommended primary pick, and any caveat where the source does not fully support the claim being linked

name: single-writer-over-section-split-for-cross-cutting-edits
description: When deciding whether to parallelise a many-fix edit of one document: if the fixes include cross-section changes, whole-document sweeps, or an identifier renumber, assign a single writer rather than section-split parallel agents; those fixes need whole-document awareness that section assembly cannot preserve.

name: dispatch-edit-agent-with-resolved-change-list
description: When dispatching an agent to apply a set of reviewed decisions to a document: give it a numbered change list that resolves each decision to a concrete edit, not the raw review and decision documents.

name: freeze-reference-docs-before-editing-body
description: When a document cites separate reference documents (constants, definitions, canon), finalise and freeze those references before editing the body, so the body is edited against stable targets.

name: treat-rippling-item-resolution-as-document-wide-sweep
description: When resolving a batch of individual review items and one item resolution changes a shared assumption (e.g. deployment topology or a global identifier): treat it as a document-wide sweep touching every affected location, not a single local edit.

name: implement-more-specific-decision-when-author-annotations-conflict
description: When two of the author's own annotations or decisions conflict (one item approves X while a stated policy rules against X): implement the more specific, placement-level decision, flag the conflict explicitly for the author rather than silently choosing, and carry the flag until the author resolves it

name: confine-specialist-vocabulary-to-specialist-section
description: When a piece must serve both a general and a specialist audience: confine specialist vocabulary to the section where the specialist reader already is and keep the body in the general register, rather than spreading jargon throughout or omitting it entirely, unless the author directs a specific term into the lede

name: cut-unverified-quote-keep-cited-paraphrase
description: When a quotation's sourcing is only secondary or unverified and a paraphrase already carries the idea: cut the quotation, keep the paraphrase, and cite the source; do not ship a quotation whose exact wording and location have not been confirmed against the primary text

name: leave-numbered-inline-review-comments
description: Review a document by leaving numbered review comments anchored inline at the exact requirement or passage each concerns, plus a comment index; do not answer your own comments.

name: answer-each-review-comment-inline-beneath-it
description: Answer each numbered review comment inline directly beneath it: resolve it with a concrete edit, or mark it as needing an owner decision; do not alter the original comments.

name: owner-decision-list-with-recommended-defaults
description: Return a prioritised, deduplicated numbered list of the decisions that still need the owner, each stating a recommended default so the owner can confirm-all or override individually; overlapping items merged, most consequential first.

name: fold-review-callouts-into-clean-body
description: Fold every decision and inline review response into the document body, then remove the review callouts — leaving a clean version with no scaffolding and no open questions.

name: integrate-feature-set-as-section-and-reconcile
description: When integrating a finished feature specification into a large existing document: add it as a new top-level section AND surgically reconcile every existing requirement the features change; do not merely append.

name: dependency-wave-build-map-schema
description: Return a dependency-wave build map with: wave-by-wave task blocks (goal, blocks, parallel tracks), a coordination-contracts register (contract, producer wave, consumer wave, contract-test location), a requirement-coverage audit placing every requirement ID with zero unplaced, and an open-questions-for-owner section separating owner decisions from plan content.

name: surface-spec-defects-found-downstream
description: When downstream work (planning, decomposition, implementation) reveals defects in the upstream specification (contradictions, duplicate identifiers, impossible requirements): report them as findings for the owner and plan around the unresolved state; never silently resolve them inside the downstream artefact.

name: review-plan-for-implementation-ambiguity-before-building
description: When a detailed implementation or build plan is ready and you could either start executing it or first review it: run a fresh-eyes coherence review of the plan for implementation ambiguity (places where an implementer would stop and guess or do two divergent things) before writing any code — a plan-stage defect is far cheaper to fix than one discovered mid-build.

name: require-incremental-file-writes-from-long-running-agents
description: When dispatching a long-running background agent to produce a sizeable file: require it to write the file early and update it incrementally rather than composing everything and writing once at the end, so a mid-run failure leaves recoverable partial work instead of an empty file.

name: match-built-code-convention-over-spec-literal
description: When a specification's literal wording conflicts with a convention the codebase has already implemented (naming, error type, data shape): match the already-built code's convention for consistency and flag the spec wording for later correction — do not introduce a second, divergent convention.

name: give-planning-agent-prior-stage-source
description: When planning a stage of work that builds on completed earlier stages: give the planning agent the actual source or artefacts of those stages, so its references to their interfaces are verified against reality rather than guessed from the specification.

name: implementation-coherence-review-report
description: Return an implementation-coherence review as: an opening verdict (executable as-is | executable-with-fixes | needs-rework) with a must-fix list; findings ranked most-severe first, each with a one-line summary, exact location, the specific ambiguity stated as two-or-more divergent interpretations, a concrete disambiguation, and a severity tag (blocker | friction | nit); and explicit mechanical cross-check results (spec-to-artefact mapping, fidelity of any transcribed tables or schemas to their source, and dependency-import fidelity).

name: ground-external-service-figures-in-current-provider-docs
description: When answering a cost, pricing, rate-limit, or capability question about a third-party API, model, or service: ground every figure in the provider's current reference documentation rather than recalled priors, and name the specific product or tier each figure applies to. Training-cutoff prices and limits go stale.

name: ground-conceptual-claims-in-author-corpus
description: When answering a conceptual question about a specific author's own framework or coined terms, and the answer could come from general model knowledge or from the author's own writing: read the author's canonical documents and ground the answer in them; do not answer from model-internal knowledge of the concept.

name: reconcile-overlapping-terms-as-register-dialects
description: When multiple terms across a body of work name closely related ideas: present them as register-specific dialects of one shared nucleus, each linked to the source where it lives, rather than collapsing them into a single term or treating them as distinct concepts.

name: per-project-status-readback
description: Return a per-project status readback where each tracked project has: current state in one line, the next concrete action, items awaiting the human, and the single canonical file to open. Group by project; order by recency of activity.

name: preserve-example-function-when-replacing
description: When replacing an illustrative example the author has rejected, preserve the structural role it plays in the argument, not its surface subject matter

name: concede-category-to-defeat-question-begging
description: When a conceptual distinction is attacked as question-begging because it defines X as outside category Y: concede that X is a kind of Y and relocate the real distinction inside Y, rather than defending X as lying outside Y

name: surface-review-fix-that-contradicts-author-instruction
description: When an evaluator or reviewer recommends a fix that contradicts an instruction the author explicitly gave: present it to the author as an explicit decision with options and a recommendation, rather than silently applying the fix or silently keeping the original

name: rest-claim-on-defensible-formulation-not-vivid-mechanism
description: When a claim can be stated as a vivid concrete mechanism (memorable but easy to attack) or as a general principle (less vivid but defensible across cases): rest the central claim on the general principle and keep the vivid mechanism only as a flagged illustration

name: isolate-manual-test-from-concurrently-writing-agent
description: When a human-driven or manual test must run in a repository where an autonomous agent is concurrently writing or committing: run the test from a separate worktree checked out at a known-good commit, with its own port and data paths, rather than sharing the active working tree

name: author-usage-overrides-style-prohibition
description: When an author deliberately uses a word or construction that appears on a style prohibition list (for example, substitutes it back in during their own edit): treat the author's usage as authoritative for their own voice and add a context carve-out to the rule — permitted in the literal or specific sense, prohibited only as vague filler — rather than enforcing the prohibition against them

name: attribute-multi-editor-diffs-via-change-reports
description: When isolating one editor's changes to a document that was edited by two parties in sequence: attribute each diff using each party's explicit change report or log, not by inferring authorship from the final text alone

name: voice-preference-extraction-report
description: Return a style-learning analysis of an author's edits with: (1) change inventory — the substantive edits the author made, listing any author-introduced errors separately as fix-not-learn items; (2) voice signals — each recurring edit pattern mapped to the underlying style preference it reveals; (3) recommended rule updates — ranked high-confidence versus speculative, each with the target style-guide location, paste-ready replacement text, and a one-sentence rationale traced to a specific edit

name: verify-plan-self-flagged-decisions-before-surfacing
description: When a plan or spec presents its own open decisions or flagged contradictions for a stakeholder to resolve: first run an independent review confirming each flagged conflict is real (checked against the authoritative source) and its proposed resolution is the minimal forward-compatible one, before surfacing the decision. Do not pass the author's self-diagnosis and recommended fix to the stakeholder unchecked.

name: check-in-source-precedent-before-new-mechanism
description: Check whether the source already draws the needed distinction elsewhere and extend that precedent rather than inventing a new mechanism

name: frozen-contract-amendment-decision-packet
description: For a decision that would change a frozen or locked contract: return the verbatim conflicting authoritative statements each with its source location, the exact locked code or test lines the change would touch, the minimal forward-compatible resolution, and the specific downstream re-freezes or corrections it obligates

name: re-freeze-frozen-tests-proven-red-first
description: When a ratified decision amends behaviour locked by frozen contract tests: re-freeze the affected tests first and run them to prove they fail against the current source, then implement — never implement first and adjust tests after

name: land-mechanical-sweep-before-semantic-change
description: When a change needs both a mechanical sweep of call sites and a semantic behaviour change: commit the sweep first as a separate no-behaviour-change step, then the semantic change as a minimal diff — never interleave them in one commit

name: sweep-dynamic-dispatch-call-sites
description: When sweeping call sites of a changed function, also search for dynamic dispatch (getattr, string-keyed tables, reflection) that direct call-site greps miss

name: adopt-and-flag-unpinned-defaults
description: When implementation needs a value or behaviour the specification does not pin: adopt a forward-compatible default and flag it prominently as unratified for owner ruling — never freeze an unratified default silently into a contract

name: name-stale-datum-in-parallel-dispatch
description: When dispatching parallel agents where one mutates a datum another reads, name that datum in the reader's prompt and designate the authoritative source to use instead

name: verify-before-recreating-flagged-missing-file
