description: When a check, subagent, or earlier analysis reports a file as missing or broken and you are about to create or recreate it: first search the whole repository by filename and by unique content it should contain. A scope-limited 'missing' result is often a false positive; recreating blindly risks clobbering real work. If the file exists elsewhere, fix the pointer rather than creating a second copy.

name: default-location-over-per-pointer-rewrite
description: When relocating a set of files into a new subfolder that many pointers reference: make the subfolder the documented default location (a bare reference resolves to it) and mark only exceptions with explicit paths, rather than rewriting every pointer. This avoids a bulk reference rewrite and its botch risk, and makes the physical move order-independent.

name: same-commit-frozen-test-edit
description: When a build step's green requires editing a frozen test (for example reversing a deliberately-frozen absence assertion so a newly-added operation is allowed): make that frozen-test edit in the same commit as the code that needs it, even though it bundles two logical changes — never leave any frozen test suite red across a commit boundary. Commit granularity yields to the per-commit green gate.

name: clear-credential-env-var-in-test-fixture
description: When a test suite makes live external calls only when a credential environment variable is present (CI passes with no credential set, but a developer who has it exported triggers real billable calls in any test that injects no stub client): clear the variable in an autouse test fixture — never by weakening the production guard or the affected tests. Verify by running the suite with and without the variable set and confirming identical results and wall-clock time.

name: bootstrap-state-checking-gate-out-of-band
description: When a fail-closed automated gate refuses the first-ever operation because it checks the prior state of the thing it protects and that state does not yet exist: perform the first operation once out-of-band as a deliberate, recorded exception, then route every subsequent operation through the gate — never weaken the gate to admit the bootstrap

name: resolve-credential-to-owning-account-before-use
description: Before using or deploying a credential where several similar accounts or environments exist, resolve it against the provider's identity endpoint to confirm it belongs to the intended account, rather than trusting the login context or the credential's label

name: wipe-validation-writes-from-recovery-store-before-deploy
description: When a pre-deployment validation writes to a store that a recovery or restore path reads on boot: delete the validation artefacts before the first deploy, so production does not restore test data as its initial state

name: prefer-system-of-record-over-user-assertion-flag-confirm
description: When a user-asserted value conflicts with an authoritative system of record (calendar, canonical document, database): record the system-of-record value, flag the discrepancy visibly in the output, and ask the user to confirm; do not silently adopt either value.

name: verify-real-production-entry-not-test-shortcut
description: When a system passes its automated tests but the tests inject state through a test-only shortcut (a bypass parameter, a fixture-set identity): treat the green suite as insufficient evidence and drive each user role through its real production entry point before declaring the flow works — the shortcut can silently become the only entry that exists.

name: confirm-silent-integration-by-direct-invocation
description: Confirm an external integration that swallows its own errors (timeouts or failures resolving to null or empty) by invoking it directly out-of-band and inspecting the returned content, not by reading logs — where success and silent failure look identical.

name: localise-fault-via-out-of-band-client-repro
description: When a UI symptom could be either a server-side or a client-side fault: reproduce the exact server interaction from a minimal out-of-band client (a scripted socket or HTTP call with the same credentials) to localise the fault before proposing a fix, rather than reasoning from UI behaviour.

name: verify-quantitative-claims-against-primary-artefact
description: When a statement includes a quantity (a duration, count, or ratio) and an intuitive figure is at hand: verify it against the underlying record — timestamps, logs, or the source file — before asserting it, and keep active processing or machine clock time distinct from elapsed calendar time. Never publish the guessed figure.

name: layered-process-talk-points
description: Return 5-8 talking points for a talk about how the speaker works. Each point includes: a one-sentence headline principle; a cited concrete example naming the specific case; a plain-language ELI12 version written to be spoken aloud; a live-demo idea drawn from current or next-stage work; and an on-screen narration line tied to the exact passage it accompanies. Also return a one-line opener, a one-line closer, and a note listing the sources read.

name: freeze-demo-source-snapshots
description: Freeze distinctly-named snapshot copies of every living document a reusable demo or presentation depends on, and repoint the demo's links to the frozen copies so it stays stable as the originals keep changing.

name: process-talk-show-real-current-work
description: When choosing what to put on screen in a talk about how you work: prefer opening the real working artefact over paraphrasing it on a slide, and prefer current or in-flight work over a polished finished result. Use a finished example only when no live one exists.

name: party-side-contract-review
description: Return a one-party (represented-side) contract review as a severity-ranked concern list (critical | high | medium | low), each concern with: clause number, exact quoted language, the risk to the represented party in plain terms, and a specific redline or negotiating ask; plus a table of missing standard protections the party should add; and a short list of the 3-5 must-win negotiating points.

name: flag-asymmetric-contract-terms
description: Review a contract from the represented party's side and flag terms that allocate risk, liability, or discretion asymmetrically against them

name: identify-missing-standard-protections
description: Identify standard protections absent from a contract that would normally protect the reviewed party (liability cap, force majeure, notice symmetry)

name: strike-mechanism-not-whole-clause
description: When a contract clause bundles an unwanted mechanism with a right the party wants to keep: delete only the mechanism, not the whole clause — removing the clause outright can also remove the beneficial right.

name: name-instrument-generically-not-fabricate-citation
description: When you cannot verify a statute section number, case name, or other legal identifier: name the instrument generically or omit the citation. Never invent a plausible-looking identifier.

name: verify-frozen-snapshot-against-design-time-state
description: When freezing snapshot copies that a reusable demo or record depends on: verify each copy against the state the artefact was designed against (the committed HEAD version, or the content the dependent references were written to), not merely the current on-disk file — a concurrent or parallel edit can drift the copy between design time and freeze time. Re-freeze from the design-time version on any mismatch.

name: gate-anticipated-change-on-one-switch-build-both-branches
description: When a feature must work one way now but an anticipated external change will later alter its behaviour: gate the difference behind one named config switch plus one named mapping, keep the mode-independent invariants outside the switch, and build AND test both branches now — do not hardcode the current mode nor leave the future branch an untested stub. The future migration is then a one-value flip, not a refactor.

name: alert-on-system-failure-not-routine-outcome
description: When deciding whether to actively notify a human about a task the system could not complete: alert only on technical or system failures (a failed dependency call, infrastructure, or an unexpected exception); leave routine business outcomes (no eligible match, a score below threshold) to the passive periodic summary.

name: key-error-on-resolution-not-inferred-intent
description: When the system cannot distinguish a caller's intent from the request alone: key the specific error on what a supplied identifier actually resolves to (for example a registered-but-inactive record), and leave the ambiguous unresolved-or-omitted case on the existing generic refusal — do not infer the caller's category to justify a more specific error.

name: enable-pipefail-from-first-gate-command
description: When running a build or CI gate through a shell: enable pipefail (or check the command's exit status directly) from the very first gate command, not only after a failure has slipped through. Never infer a green result from piped or truncated output — a pipe can mask a non-zero exit status.

name: fix-forward-never-force-push-shared-history
description: When a wrong or failing commit has already reached a shared branch: fix it forward with a new commit on top. Never force-push to rewrite pushed history on a shared branch — it can silently drop or reorder others' work and is hard to reverse.

name: content-negotiate-form-vs-api-response
description: When one HTTP endpoint serves both a plain HTML form (no client JS) and programmatic API callers: content-negotiate on the request content type — render an HTML page for the form POST, return JSON for the API caller. Returning JSON to both makes the browser navigate to and display the raw JSON body as the page.

name: operational-recovery-runbook
description: Return an operational recovery runbook with: a decision tree mapping each failure class to its entry criterion and action; numbered copy-paste commands per recovery path; honest failure notes (data-loss window, side-effects, and what the procedure is NOT); a post-recovery verification block; a timing table with the target; and a one-line operator comms script. Every step executable without improvisation.

name: fix-full-flagged-scope-not-reported-symptom
description: When a user reports a defect narrowly and the project's issue or review registry already holds a broader entry covering the same defect: fix the full flagged scope, not only the reported symptom. Check the registry before implementing a narrow fix.

name: record-state-before-irreversible-move
description: When an operation both records state and performs an irreversible move or delete of the source: record the state first, then perform the move — a crash between the two then leaves a resumable record rather than an orphaned artifact with no record.

name: live-verify-over-mocked-green-before-done
description: When a build has deferred live API or integration checks behind mocks and all mocked tests pass: run every deferred check against the real service before declaring the feature done. A stub client returns whatever the test dictates, so an invalid request schema, a wrong model id, or a bad auth shape all pass mocked-green and surface only on a real call.

name: scale-process-rigor-to-blast-radius
description: When a heavyweight process gate (multi-round review, full intake questionnaire, multi-actor sign-off) is designed for shared products but the task is a solo or greenfield tool: scale the gate down to the checks that catch irreversible errors (data loss, privacy, security) and skip the multi-actor coordination machinery.

name: build-deferred-feature-behind-stub-interface
description: Build a deferred feature as a stable interface with a stub implementation now, so the real implementation drops in later without changing any caller

name: verify-terminated-agent-work-via-git-and-tests
description: When a dispatched agent terminates abnormally, verify its work against git and the test suite before trusting its status or re-dispatching

name: advance-watermark-past-failed-items-with-downstream-dedupe
description: When advancing a single-watermark cursor over a fetched batch where individual items may fail to process: advance the cursor past every item seen (failures included) and rely on the downstream consumer's idempotent dedupe to absorb any re-processing, rather than holding the cursor back to selectively re-fetch only the failed items. Recovery for a failed item is a fresh submission, not a cursor rewind; leave the cursor unadvanced only when the entire fetch fails.

name: normalise-external-value-at-boundary-before-strict-api
description: When passing an externally-produced value (LLM output, user input, third-party field) to a downstream API with a strict format contract: normalise the value to the required format at the boundary and handle an unparseable value gracefully (skip or null, matching the empty-value path), rather than passing it through and assuming one input shape. A single successful live run does not prove the input-variety space is covered.

name: redact-url-embedded-credentials-before-logging
description: Redact credentials embedded in request URLs from exception messages before logging or re-raising them, so tokens never reach a persistent log file.

name: atomic-file-handoff-into-watched-folder
description: Stage each work item to a temp or dotfile name and atomically rename it into the shared watched folder; write only, and let the consuming scanner own dedupe.

name: resume-failed-agent-from-transcript-not-restart
description: When a spawned agent fails partway through a task with work already completed: resume it from its transcript with a follow-up message carrying the remaining instructions, rather than launching a fresh agent that repeats the completed work.

name: enumerate-candidates-on-ambiguous-match
description: When user input matches more than one candidate: reply with the enumerated candidates, each with a copy-pasteable single-token selector, and apply nothing, rather than guessing a single match or requiring the user to already know the disambiguator.

name: expose-injection-passthroughs-before-freezing-interface
description: Before freezing a component's public interface, ensure it exposes a passthrough for every dependency its internal calls inject for hermetic testing, so downstream consumers receive a complete testable surface.

name: defer-decision-to-boundary-that-builds-consumer
description: When a build surfaces a gap whose fix belongs to a not-yet-built consumer: defer the decision to the boundary that builds that consumer and record it as an explicit agenda item, rather than pulling the work forward or re-opening a frozen unit.

name: bandit-over-fixed-split-at-low-volume
description: When optimising content variants under low conversion volume: allocate traffic with a multi-armed bandit that updates its estimates under uncertainty, not a fixed-split A/B test that never reaches significance at low volume, and stay in exploration until volume supports exploitation.

name: configurable-gate-for-autonomous-spender
description: When building a loop that spends real money autonomously: make the autonomy level a configurable gate policy that defaults to proposing actions for human approval and can switch to auto-execute within caps, and treat total and per-action budget caps and a global kill switch as first-class features rather than add-ons.

name: measure-before-building-channel-generator
description: When a growth-automation feature’s payoff depends on an unproven acquisition channel: build the conversion-measurement foundation first and defer the channel-specific content generator until evidence shows the channel is worth the investment.

name: keyed-slots-for-swappable-copy
description: When UI copy must be swappable or testable across audiences: store every user-facing string as a keyed variant-slot resolved through a single function, rather than hardcoding strings, so messaging tests, SEO, and repositioning become data changes instead of code changes.

name: append-only-ledger-for-balances
description: When modelling a credit or money balance: represent it as an append-only ledger of signed, optionally-expiring entries with balance computed as the sum of non-expired deltas, never a single mutable balance field, so history stays auditable and expiry can be evaluated lazily at read.

name: locked-transaction-for-concurrent-debit
description: When debiting a shared balance under concurrency: perform the balance check and the debit write inside one transaction holding a per-account lock, rather than reading the balance and writing separately, so simultaneous operations cannot overdraw.

name: route-llm-calls-through-a-fakeable-provider
description: Place all LLM calls behind a thin provider interface with a single completion method so tests can inject a deterministic fake.

name: register-per-role-over-shared-foundation
description: When one interface serves two user roles with opposed needs — one performing focused work, one being asked to do something socially exposing: give each role its own visual register (density and warmth) over one shared design-token foundation, rather than a single compromise register for both.

name: additive-css-layer-over-existing-hooks
description: When adding styling to an application whose markup already carries semantic hooks (such as data-attributes) and has no stylesheet: deliver it as an additive CSS layer targeting those existing hooks, and do not rewrite markup or add class attributes, so existing tests and structure stay intact.

name: scope-coexisting-styles-and-verify-no-leak
description: When two visual styles must coexist on one page, scope each style's rules by an ancestor or role attribute and verify in both directions that neither style's rules reach the other's elements.

name: never-hide-test-asserted-elements-with-css
description: When CSS could hide an element that automated tests assert is visible: never apply display:none, visibility:hidden, or zero-size to a test-hooked element; keep show/hide behavioural via conditional rendering, not stylistic.

name: verify-spec-identifiers-against-code-when-planning
description: When turning a design spec into a build plan, verify every technical identifier the spec references against the actual codebase and surface each divergence from the spec as an explicit decision.

name: wcag-aa-colour-system
description: Return a colour system in which every text/background pair meets WCAG AA (>=4.5:1 for body text, >=3:1 for large text and UI boundaries); when a pair fails, darken the specific failing usage (e.g. a button background) rather than shifting the whole hue, and record the final values.

name: present-rendered-options-for-look-and-feel-decisions
description: For a look-and-feel or visual-design decision, present rendered side-by-side mockups and real reference examples for the user to select from, rather than describing the options in prose.

name: mutation-verify-never-red-test
description: Prove a test that passed without ever having been seen to fail is not vacuous: mutate the production behaviour it asserts, confirm the test turns red at the target assertion, then restore the code

name: surface-implementation-fork-for-owner-ruling
description: When the owner's stated decision maps to more than one implementation mechanism with materially different cost, risk, or scope: present the distinct mechanisms as an explicit fork and get a ruling, rather than assuming which one the owner intended

name: deploy-combined-head-after-background-fix-lands
description: When a deploy targets one shared environment and a background agent is still committing fixes to the same branch: wait for the agent to land its commit, then deploy the combined HEAD and verify once, rather than deploying the pre-fix commit or a mid-build working tree

name: verify-field-in-projection-before-styling-fix
description: When user feedback asks a UI surface to display data it does not currently show: confirm the field exists in the client-facing projection or snapshot before scoping it as a styling change; if the field is absent, treat it as a data-contract or engine change, not paint

name: pass-script-through-nested-quoting-via-base64
description: Pass a script cleanly through nested shell or SSH quoting layers by base64-encoding it locally and decoding-and-evaluating it at the far end, instead of escaping quotes by hand

name: verify-deploy-at-infrastructure-level-before-human-test
description: After a deploy, verify at the infrastructure level by fetching the health endpoint, a built asset, and a served static file and confirming their status and content type, before handing off to human interactive testing

name: re-run-known-stochastic-test-before-calling-regression
description: When a test known to be stochastic (timing, concurrency, a crash drill CI runs many times) fails once amid otherwise-passing runs: re-run it to confirm before treating the single failure as a regression, rather than blocking on the one flake

name: probe-live-api-before-building-integration
description: Before building code against an external API, call its live endpoints and read a real response to confirm exact field names, nesting keys, and sentinel values, rather than inferring them from documentation

name: supply-option-names-not-just-ids-to-model
description: When an LLM must select from a fixed set of options, present each option's human-readable name alongside its identifier and instruct it to match on the name; constrain the returned identifier with a schema enum

name: failed-refresh-degrades-to-stale-not-empty
description: When a scheduled refresh of cached external data fails: leave the previous good cache untouched and exit non-zero, rather than writing an empty or partial result; build the full replacement in memory before overwriting any file

name: send-credentials-in-request-body-not-url
description: When sending credentials to an HTTP endpoint: place them in the request body, not URL query parameters, even if the endpoint also accepts query params, because query strings leak into error messages, logs, and proxies; emit only a status code in any error message, never the stringified request

name: test-the-real-error-path-not-a-stand-in
description: When a test could either trigger the real error condition or hand-supply a substitute value: trigger it for real so the assertion exercises the production code path; a redaction test fed a fabricated error string passes whether or not redaction works

name: capture-decision-state-before-connectivity-loss
description: When the user signals imminent loss of connectivity mid-task: immediately write and commit a self-contained handoff artifact to disk before continuing any other work, rather than relying on in-flight or background work — background and API-dependent work fails the moment the connection drops, and only committed on-disk state survives

name: verify-decision-options-against-source-before-presenting
description: Before presenting a set of options for a human to rule on: verify each option against the authoritative spec or source and repair any that misstates it or asks the human to decide an already-settled value — fix the decision surface first, never let the human rule on wrong or already-resolved information

name: instruction-mechanism-not-frozen-edit-authorisation
description: When a user's instruction names a mechanism whose literal implementation would edit a frozen, sealed, or contract-locked surface but does not explicitly authorise that edit: achieve the intent with a non-invasive equivalent and record it as a flagged deviation, rather than treating the mechanism reference as licence to modify the frozen surface

name: scope-doc-change-impact-at-audit-steps
description: Scope a documentation change's downstream impact by finding which steps validate against the document text (audits, coverage checks); only those couple to its currency, not steps exercising already-built behaviour

name: probe-write-mechanics-with-disposable-test-data
description: Before a first write to a live external system, probe the write mechanics with disposable test data (create, read back, then delete) to pin uncertain fields and routes, rather than running the real batch blind

name: persist-remote-id-immediately-then-stop-on-failure
description: When creating records in an external system in a loop: persist each returned id immediately after the create returns and before any further step, and stop on the first failure, so a re-run resumes without duplicating, rather than persisting the id late or continuing past a failure

name: idempotency-via-durable-key-stamped-on-remote-object
description: When idempotency must survive losing the local record: stamp a durable domain key on each object created in the external system and adopt-by-lookup before creating, rather than relying only on a locally stored remote id

name: skip-and-flag-invalid-batch-item-not-abort
description: When a batch item fails validation: skip it, flag it, and continue with the valid items, never sending it downstream and never failing the whole batch

name: batch-validator-is-total-never-raises
description: A batch-item validator must never raise: an unparseable item returns invalid-with-a-reason so one corrupt item is skipped, rather than an unhandled error aborting the whole batch

name: stop-at-draft-for-irreversible-writes
description: When a tool writes to a financial or otherwise irreversible system: stop at an unsubmitted draft the human reviews and submits, never auto-submitting, approving, or paying

name: suspect-config-not-payload-on-vague-association-error
description: When an external API rejects a valid payload with a vague not-permitted-for-this-entity error: check the referenced object's config or preference toggle before changing the payload, rather than repositioning the field hunting for a fix

name: match-user-edited-exemplar-not-rederive
description: When propagating a style or layout across sibling elements and the user has hand-edited one as the exemplar: copy that element's exact properties to the siblings, not values you re-derive independently.

name: preprocess-asset-when-native-api-cannot
description: Pre-process an asset in an external tool and import it when the target tool's API cannot produce the required form (e.g. a non-rectangular image crop).

name: attribute-speaker-by-content-not-diarisation-label
description: When machine diarisation labels conflict with in-dialogue evidence of who is speaking: attribute each turn by content proof (a speaker named aloud, a biographical tell) and confirm the speaker mapping with the user before relabelling, not by the diarisation label

name: prefer-authoritative-source-over-lossy-derivation
description: When a value derived from a lossy source (transcript, OCR, paste) conflicts with the same value in an authoritative source document: use the authoritative document and correct the derived value; do not average the two or guess

name: flag-decision-divergence-from-proposal
description: When a recorded decision differs from the proposal that was tabled: flag the divergence explicitly for the decision owner, rather than recording only the final outcome as if it had matched the proposal

name: meeting-minutes-schema
description: Return meeting minutes with: sections mirroring the meeting agenda; each decision rendered as proposal, resolution, conditions, and owner; and a residual action-item list grouped by owner at the end

name: mechanical-only-edits-during-concurrent-authoring
description: When editing a document that its author is concurrently editing: apply only mechanical and factual corrections; hold structural, ordering, and voice changes for the author

name: strip-headmatter-into-temp-copy-for-distributable-export
description: When exporting a distributable artefact (PDF etc.) from a versioned source that carries provenance headmatter: strip the headmatter into a throwaway copy, export that copy, then delete it; never edit the versioned source to remove headmatter, so the source keeps its provenance while the distributed artefact stays clean

name: compute-fixed-form-deterministically-reserve-llm-for-open-ended
description: When a required output has a specific fixed form for a well-defined case: compute that case deterministically and call the LLM only for the open-ended remainder, rather than prompting the LLM to reproduce the fixed form

name: surface-progress-for-long-ui-triggered-operations
description: When a UI action triggers a multi-second operation: surface progress with a bar or running count rather than running silently, because silent long work reads as a hang and the user re-triggers it, risking duplicate side effects

name: refetch-shared-state-before-positional-edit
description: When a user gives a positional instruction (slide, row, or page N) for a shared artifact you last read earlier: re-fetch its current state and map the reference to that state before writing, because a concurrent edit shifts positions with no error to signal the change

name: distinguish-problem-cost-from-solution-value
description: Distinguish the cost a problem imposes on those who have it (the pain) from the value created by solving it (the prize), presenting them as separate points rather than restating one as the other

name: mark-template-placeholders-visually-distinct
description: When building a fill-in template, render placeholder guidance in a visually distinct style (such as italic) so users can tell prompts-to-replace from finished content

name: anchor-time-dependent-fixtures-relative-to-now
description: When building test fixtures for code that stamps real wall-clock timestamps and does time-window arithmetic (silence windows, escalation, staleness, retention): anchor the fixture's dates relative to the current clock (now minus N days), not to a fixed calendar date — a fixed anchor passes the day it is written then silently corrupts the window arithmetic once the wall clock advances past it, including on any later binding run

name: flag-open-decisions-with-build-around-defaults-when-approver-away
description: When executing a build loop whose pre-execution decisions normally need an approver who is unavailable, but the work itself is unblocked: attach a safe reversible default to each open decision so the build proceeds, record each as a deviation for later ratification, and stop only on a decision that is a genuine specification absence

name: raise-spec-absence-do-not-synthesise-it
description: When a coverage or completeness audit finds a required item with no defining specification, implementation, or test: raise it as a flag for the owner and leave it unbuilt; do not invent the missing specification to make the audit pass — the absence is the finding, not a gap to paper over

name: extract-multi-format-entries-by-format-union
description: When counting or extracting defined entries from a document that uses more than one definition format, match the union of all formats, dedupe, and assert the expected total so an unhandled format fails loudly instead of silently under-counting

name: calibrate-forwardable-hooks-to-target-recognition
description: When choosing how much identifying detail to put in a forwardable message: describe the intended target's specific attributes sharply enough that the right recipient recognises the fit, but stop short of naming the target or including details that make the recipient feel singled out.

name: source-before-asserting-counterparty-priority
description: When an appealing counterparty priority would strengthen a pitch but is not evidenced in a source: mark it as your own inference or omit it, rather than asserting it as the counterparty's stated priority.

name: frame-ask-as-minimum-and-preferred-tiers
description: Frame a resource ask as two tiers: a minimum viable version and a preferred fuller version, so the counterparty can accept at least the minimum.

name: defer-transient-poll-failures-hold-cursor-skip-genuine
description: When an item in a cursor-based poll fails, distinguish a transient failure (network/timeout) from a genuine one: on transient, hold the cursor and defer silently so it retries next poll with no user alarm; on a genuine non-retryable failure, skip it, advance the cursor past it, and alarm the user, rather than treating all failures alike

name: drop-parallel-approach-when-warm-intro-opens
description: When a target becomes reachable through a warm introduction while a separate cold or forwardable approach to the same target is still pending: pursue the warm channel and drop or hold the parallel approach, so the target is not approached twice.

name: frame-partnership-ask-as-reciprocal
description: When proposing a partnership, state both what you would give the counterparty and what you would want from them, not only your own ask.

name: fifo-allocation-over-filtered-sum-for-expiring-balances
description: When computing a balance over entries that can expire: replay history allocating each spend against the soonest-expiring grant still live at the spend's own timestamp, so only unspent remainders expire; never sum deltas under an expiry filter — a spent-then-expired grant goes retroactively negative.

name: gate-every-entry-surface-not-just-the-shell
description: Authorise each page and each server action or endpoint independently; never rely on a shared layout, wrapper, or navigation shell as the authorisation boundary.

name: carry-expected-state-index-on-mutations
description: Have each mutation request carry the state index it acts on; no-op on mismatch and guard the write with a conditional update on that same index so a duplicate or racing request cannot skip state.

name: freeze-structure-version-keep-display-text-live
description: Pin executing instances to an immutable structural snapshot while display text resolves live at render, so copy fixes reach in-flight runs but structural edits cannot corrupt them.

name: reverse-deterministic-escaping-with-committed-extraction-script
description: When importing content from a lossy-but-deterministic export, commit an extraction script that reverses the encoding and asserts fidelity gates: expected counts, zero escape residue, spot byte-equality against the source.

name: select-live-dataset-by-shape-assertion
description: When multiple lookalike tables or copies of a dataset exist, select the live one by asserting its expected shape (id range, row count, schema), never by position or recency alone.

name: validate-pasted-config-before-use
description: Parse and validate hand-pasted configuration values (embedded spaces, unreplaced placeholders, duplicate or empty keys) with a real parser before use; never shell-source them — a parse failure can leak secret fragments into logs.

name: check-handle-availability-inline-while-brainstorming-names
description: While generating name candidates, check handle and domain availability live so every shortlist arrives pre-filtered with claimable forms attached.

name: pivot-name-register-by-harvesting-same-meaning-traditions
description: When a name's concept is right but its register or sound is wrong, harvest same-meaning terms from other craft traditions (music, martial arts, sport, trade idiom) rather than abandoning the concept.

name: spec-governs-over-plan-mandated-code
description: When review flags code that the build plan mandates but the approved specification contradicts: the specification governs — fix the code and amend the plan; never dismiss the finding because the plan's own text requires it.

name: split-continuous-serving-from-intermittent-compute
description: When a system pairs continuous serving with heavy compute that runs only intermittently: separate them into an always-on server and a stateless opportunistic worker coordinated through a durable shared backlog, not a single host doing both.

name: count-canonicals-not-raw-when-frequency-drives-behaviour
description: When item frequency in a corpus drives system behaviour (thresholds, prioritisation, adaptive depth): deduplicate first and count only canonical items, never raw items, because duplicates inflate the signal and mis-trigger the behaviour.

name: verify-service-api-policy-before-designing-sync
description: When designing automated extraction from a third-party service: verify its current API access policy and limits before assuming programmatic sync is possible. If full sync is disallowed, use bulk export for one-time backfill plus capture-at-source for incremental, rather than building against an API that may forbid it.

name: establish-remote-access-while-on-site
description: When setting up a machine to be administered remotely: establish remote access (VPN, mesh, or tunnel) while physically on-site, as one of the first steps, before other configuration. A headless box with only LAN access is unreachable until you return in person.

name: model-groupings-as-membership-dag-not-tree
description: When modelling a classification or search taxonomy that includes functional or paraphyletic groupings (e.g. tree, reptile): represent it as a multi-parent DAG and treat every roll-up as group membership, never as exclusive descent, so classifying an item into a grouping never triggers exclusion inference about its other memberships.

name: subagent-never-executes-in-production-wired-repo
description: When a subagent must verify a runtime claim in a repository holding live credentials or a production datastore: have it report the claim as unverifiable and name what would be needed, rather than running the code. Enumerate the forbidden entry points by name in the dispatch and name the test runner as the only sanctioned execution path. Applies to reviewers and fixers, not only implementers.

name: probe-live-system-before-writing-the-spec
description: When a design assumption is inherited from a prior handoff and the target system can be queried read-only: probe it before writing the spec, not at the build's verification gate. Treat every inherited assumption as unverified until the probe confirms it, and expect the probe to change the design rather than merely confirm field names.

name: domain-argument-is-not-evidence-about-interface-behaviour
description: When deciding whether to guard an unobserved failure state: treat an argument about what the system's domain model permits as insufficient evidence about what its interface actually returns. State the claim as 'not observed in N samples', not 'impossible'. Where the guard costs little and the failure would be silent and irreversible, add it regardless of how convincing the domain argument is.

name: review-whole-branch-for-cross-file-seams
description: Review the complete branch diff as one system after per-task reviews pass, targeting defects that span files no single task's diff contained.

name: audit-and-rewrite-history-before-the-first-push
description: When a repository with no remote is about to be pushed for the first time: audit the full commit history — not the working tree — for credentials and third-party personal data, and rewrite before pushing. A clean file listing says nothing about old commits, and after the first push a rewrite becomes a shared-history problem. Mirror-clone a backup first if the repo is the only copy, then delete that backup, which retains what was scrubbed.

name: code-review-two-verdict-report
description: Return a code review with two verdicts, both required. (1) Spec compliance: one row per requirement marked met | not met | cannot-verify, plus an overall pass or fail, flagging omissions and scope creep. (2) Task quality: correctness, test hygiene, naming, dead code, error handling, marked approved or not approved. Classify every issue Critical | Important | Minor and give each a concrete failure scenario stating inputs or state leading to wrong behaviour. If a requirement lives in code the diff does not show, mark it cannot-verify and name what would be needed. Do not guess.

name: omit-traceback-when-logging-credential-bearing-exceptions
description: When logging a caught exception on a path whose exceptions can embed a credential in a URL or connection string: log a redacted message at error level and omit the traceback, rather than using the exception-level logger. The auto-attached traceback renders the original exception regardless of how the message argument is redacted, so redacting the message alone still leaks.

name: verify-an-attention-flag-has-a-reader
description: When a process writes a status flag intended to draw a human's attention: confirm some interface actually queries and displays rows carrying that flag before treating the notification requirement as satisfied. A flag nothing reads is silent data loss, and a specification asserting that it surfaces somewhere is false until the reader exists.

name: enforce-tenant-isolation-at-network-perimeter-before-app-layer
description: When forced to choose between relying on an application's own authorisation and enforcing access at the network perimeter for a self-hosted multi-tenant service: make the identity-tagged network-perimeter ACL the primary boundary, evaluated before the app authenticates, and treat app-layer auth as defence in depth. A tenant with no network route to a service cannot exploit that service's own auth flaws.

name: grant-restricted-collaborator-a-forge-and-tag-not-a-shell
description: When a collaborator on a shared machine needs repository and specific-app access but not general compute, and the OS lacks clean shell confinement: give them a forge account plus an identity-tagged network node rather than a restricted interactive shell. Without a shell, filesystem isolation holds by construction instead of by fragile per-path permission configuration.

name: choose-forge-over-bare-repo-when-collaborators-will-grow
description: When choosing between a raw bare git repo over git-shell and a self-hosted forge for collaborator repository access: choose the forge once the collaborator set may grow past one, is not uniformly command-line-git-fluent, or may need differentiated permissions, accepting one extra service to run in exchange for dashboard-managed access and browser-based editing. Choose the bare repo only for a single git-fluent collaborator where running fewer services dominates.

name: expose-self-hosted-apps-privately-by-default
description: When deciding how to expose a self-hosted app: reach it over the private mesh VPN only by default, and reserve public-internet exposure (an authenticated tunnel) for apps that genuinely must be reached without the VPN, such as a mobile client on an arbitrary network. Public exposure is opt-in per app, never the default.

name: self-managed-server-access-design
description: Return a self-managed-server access design containing: (1) hardware and container runtime; (2) each trust tier and, for every tier, exactly what it can and cannot reach; (3) where isolation is enforced (network perimeter versus application) and the ACL rule; (4) the exposure method per service; (5) a host-migration path; (6) each open decision either resolved to a default or explicitly deferred with a forward-compatible current choice.

name: assign-styling-register-by-audience-not-viewer
description: When splitting a shared UI into two visual registers: assign each element to one register by its actual render-audience — elements only one role's DOM contains go to that role's register, elements rendered for everyone go to the shared register — giving one treatment per element, rather than restyling shared elements per viewer role. Derive the audience from the code's render-gating, not from where the element visually sits

name: user-fillable-test-drive-feedback-doc
description: Return a single annotatable test-drive document for the user to fill while using a live tool: (1) a setup block listing accounts, test credentials, and any second-window/second-role needs; (2) a severity tag legend; (3) a free-form running log; (4) the product walked as user journeys, each step written as Do (the concrete action) / Look at (what to judge: function, styling, copy) / a blank notes slot; (5) a closing 'already tracked — do not re-log' list of known and deferred items

name: lead-spec-with-the-invalidating-constraint
description: Open a design specification with the constraint that would invalidate the feature, stated before the design itself

name: separate-senses-of-an-overloaded-term
description: Separate the distinct senses of an overloaded term the requester used, giving a one-line test that assigns any instance to exactly one sense

name: superseding-version-delta-table
description: Return, in a revised specification, a table listing every item from the superseded version with its status in the new one (carried | shrunk | deleted | ruled) and the reason for each removal

name: incidental-defect-section
description: Return a section listing defects found while specifying an adjacent change, each marked reachable-today or activated-only-when-this-change-lands

name: pre-step-overview-and-materials-manifest
description: Return, before any step instructions: a plain-language overview naming the total number of steps, then a materials list where each item is tagged with the step number(s) requiring it and ordered earliest-step-first

name: declare-unverifiable-procedure-at-point-of-use
description: When writing instructions someone will execute and a third-party procedure cannot be verified from available sources: mark that step unverified and point at the vendor's own documentation, rather than supplying a plausible procedure

name: recheck-dated-risk-before-acting-on-research
description: When prior research is the basis for an action and its central risk assessment was time-sensitive: re-verify that risk against current sources before acting, even when it delays the action

name: prefer-storage-that-fails-by-refusing
description: When choosing how to store a value governing who may see something: prefer the shape that fails by refusing the write over one whose absence defaults to the more permissive value

name: reuse-prior-composition-when-fresh-one-degenerates
description: When a fresh agent composition returns no primitives or a low pool match and a recent well-fitted composition exists for the same task shape: execute on the prior composition and record the pool gap

name: re-derive-challenged-constraint-scope
description: When the requester challenges a constraint you stated: re-derive its actual scope from source and state the narrowed version, rather than defending the original or dropping the constraint entirely

name: check-for-existing-mechanism-before-designing
description: Before designing a requested feature, search the codebase for a mechanism that already provides it and design only the genuine gap

name: spec-shared-infrastructure-separately-from-application
description: When a feature request bundles infrastructure shared across projects with application logic: specify the shared infrastructure as its own separate deliverable

name: classify-listing-surfaces-by-identity-for-visibility
description: For a visibility or access feature, enumerate every surface that lists the data and classify each as identity-blind (show public rows only) or actor-aware (filter rows by the acting owner)

name: run-llm-generated-sql-against-a-prefiltered-view
description: When an LLM turns user input into SQL over restricted data: run it against a pre-filtered view that enforces visibility, never the raw table. Do not rely on the generated SQL to respect access rules

name: serve-restricted-view-on-a-separate-gated-surface
description: When only some users may see restricted rows on an otherwise-shared read surface: serve their privileged view on a separate identity-gated surface rather than adding per-user auth to the shared one, keeping the leak-critical shared surface single-purpose and identity-blind

name: phase-rollout-by-expanding-the-user-set
description: When sequencing a rollout: expand the user set one class at a time (single owner, then more humans, then automated agents) and gate each capability on the phase whose users first make it meaningful, rather than shipping everything at once

name: committed-working-code-with-passing-tests
description: Return the working implementation as committed code — not a plan, pseudocode, or a description of code — with: the code written to the files the task names, the full test suite passing with pristine output (no errors or warnings), the new or changed tests that cover each behaviour, and a completion note giving the commit hash(es) and the final test count. If the task cannot be completed, return a blocker note (what failed and where) and commit no partial or untested code.

name: replace-positioned-element-by-copying-original-geometry
description: When replacing a positioned visual element with a new asset that must occupy the same footprint (a slide image, a canvas or layout node): read the original element geometry (size and transform) and copy it verbatim into the new element, then delete the original — rather than re-deriving position and dimensions by hand or by eye. Match the new asset aspect ratio to the box so the API does not distort it.

name: prove-styled-machine-readable-code-via-standard-twin
description: When a decoder rejects a machine-readable code rendered in a non-standard style (inverted or light-on-dark QR, recoloured barcode): do not conclude the code is broken from that one failed decode. Prove the payload by decoding a standard-contrast equivalent built from the same underlying matrix, and confirm the deployed instance by decoding its final render — the decoder false-negative on the styled form is not evidence of a bad payload.

name: identify-lock-holder-before-forcing-busy-resource
description: When a cleanup or maintenance operation reports a shared resource is busy or "in use" (a cache prune, an unmount, a delete, a migration), do not force it or treat it as failed: it is usually waiting on a lock, not broken. Identify the process holding the resource (lsof/pgrep), stop that process or the client that spawned it, then retry.

name: design-channel-agnostic-core-with-thin-transport-adapters
description: Structure a multi-transport feature as one channel-agnostic core plus a thin adapter per transport, so adding a channel adds an adapter, not core changes

name: inject-cross-layer-behaviour-as-callback-from-composition-root
description: Keep a low-level module from importing a higher layer by accepting the cross-layer behaviour as a callback injected at the composition root

name: verify-record-completeness-before-padding
description: When asked to produce or refresh a dated or periodic record (daily note, log, changelog) that may already exist: reconstruct what actually happened from independent authoritative clocks — VCS author-dates plus session-transcript UTC timestamps bucketed to the local calendar day — and confirm whether the existing record already covers it. If it does, leave it faithful to how much actually happened; do not pad a sparse-but-accurate record to look busier.

name: isolate-per-item-failure-in-an-unattended-loop
description: When an item in a cursor-advancing poll or batch loop fails: if the error is transient (network, timeout, rate-limit) defer it — rewind the cursor, retry next run, write nothing; for any other error consume it — log redacted, advance the cursor, continue. Never let one item’s failure abort the batch before the cursor advances. A side-effect issued after the state commit (a confirmation send) must be best-effort and must never raise a transient error, or it will rewind and re-run already-committed work.

name: audit-reader-surfaces-when-adding-a-shared-queue-writer
description: When adding a path that writes a field also read or written by another surface sharing the same work queue, audit each such surface’s read side so it preserves the new writer’s value rather than overwriting it.

name: change-wording-only-when-tuning-a-piece-to-a-new-audience
description: When adapting a finished piece to appeal to a new readership: change only word choice and phrasing to match that readership's researched dialect; never alter the arguments, examples, or claims, and flag any proposed change that would as out of scope.

name: anchor-citation-link-on-cited-work-not-author
description: When placing a hyperlink inside a citation: anchor it on the cited work's title or the exact section the URL resolves to, not on the author's name, a bare URL, or a trailing source label; keep the remaining citation apparatus as plain text around the link.

name: treat-throttled-or-accepted-http-status-as-live-in-a-link-check
description: When a pre-publish link check returns a non-200 status: treat 429 (rate-limited) and 202 (accepted) as live and keep the link; treat 404 or a connection failure as broken and fix it. Never remove a link on a throttle response.

name: reuse-the-projects-verified-citation-store-before-researching
description: Before researching citations for a piece, check the project's own working files for an existing verified-quotation store (per source: verbatim quote, citation, live link, and provenance) and reuse it; research only what it lacks.

name: open-code-against-seed-set-with-emergent-escape-hatch
description: Code each item against a seed category set, or tag it EMERGENT with a named candidate pattern when it fits none; collect the EMERGENT items separately and flag any pattern recurring three or more times as a proposed new category.

name: detect-a-pattern-by-its-counterpart-response
description: Detect instances of a behavioural pattern in a corpus by the counterpart's response signature (for example, a challenge recognised by the recipient conceding a flaw in the next turn), not only by the initiator's surface phrasing, which under-samples interrogative and reframing moves.

name: multi-review-synthesis-report
description: Return a synthesis of multiple independent reviews with: convergent findings ranked by severity and by the number of reviewers raising them (the fix-regardless items); conflicting findings flagged separately as author decisions; and a prioritised change list partitioned into certain fixes versus structural rewrite.

name: split-a-piece-for-divergent-audience-bars
description: When one piece must satisfy audiences with structurally different acceptance bars (one that must find it forward-worthy, one that must be unable to dismiss it): split into a forwardable piece written first and a rigorous companion carrying the hard argument, rather than bloating one piece to serve both.

name: ground-a-distinction-in-accountability-not-capability
description: When defending a categorical distinction between two kinds of agent: ground it in who authors and is accountable for the choice, not in a capability defined as what one side cannot do, since the capability version is circular and usually disqualifies the favoured side too.

name: separate-broad-extraction-from-the-judgment-pass
description: When a task needs both exhaustive extraction and selective judgment: run a broad mechanical extraction to produce candidates first, then filter and classify them in a separate judgment pass, rather than fusing extraction and judgment into one step.

name: dual-pointer-reference-entries
description: Return reference-document entries where every definition, claim, and example carries both a live source URL (for quoting in future writing) and a local file path (for fast machine reading).

name: partition-a-wave-by-live-dependency-build-the-hermetic-majority
description: When a build wave appears blocked on a live external dependency such as a server or credentials: triage it per item — build now everything whose green claim rests only on existing stubs and fixtures, and defer only the items whose correctness rests on the live system — rather than blocking the whole wave until the dependency exists. A method with an unverified live endpoint can still be built now if its path sits behind a clearly-named UNVERIFIED constant and no green claim depends on it.

name: two-tier-build-around-defaults-by-observability
description: When attaching build-around defaults to open decisions for an unattended build: silently default choices that only affect naming or wording, but for any default that changes user-observable behaviour apply a safe reversible default AND escalate it explicitly for ratification — do not treat cosmetic and behaviour-visible decisions the same.

name: verify-batch-source-grouping-by-provenance
description: Before ingesting a batch of source archives or split files, determine true membership from embedded provenance metadata (shared export timestamps, consecutive part numbers) rather than human-applied filenames; flag any members whose names imply a different grouping than the metadata shows

name: flag-out-of-gamut-colour-conversion
description: When converting a saturated screen or RGB colour to CMYK or Pantone: state that highly-saturated colours fall outside print gamut and will reproduce duller, give any formula or bridge values as approximate only, and recommend profile-based conversion plus a physical proof over trusting the computed value

name: drive-the-real-pipeline-seam-with-injected-input
description: To exercise or demo a fully-built pipeline without standing up its live external transport, feed synthetic inputs directly to its real internal ingestion seam with a live model — the genuine processing runs end-to-end while only the transport is bypassed. Faster and lower-risk than full live infra, and it doubles as a first-live-run that surfaces bugs the stubbed tests hid.

name: archive-a-publication-via-its-official-export
description: To build a faithful offline markdown corpus of an external publication (e.g. a Substack) rather than scraping it, use the platform's official owner export: the ZIP carries structured metadata plus one HTML file per post with images left as live CDN links — complete and offline-durable. Convert each post HTML to markdown behind a pre-pass that normalises the platform's image and embed wrapper markup so headings, links, and image URLs survive intact, and pull any per-post tags from the platform's post API when the export omits them.

name: read-via-legitimate-member-when-membership-reconciled
description: When reading from a system that reconciles its participant list against an external source of truth and evicts anyone who does not belong (e.g. a chat bridge's mirrored rooms): access the data through an existing legitimate participant identity, not a newly injected observer account — the injected account is removed and its reads silently return empty

name: diagnose-empty-read-by-checking-reader-access
description: When a read returns empty but the data demonstrably exists (visible through another path): check the reader's own access first — membership, history visibility, permission scope, auth token — before concluding the query or the data is wrong

name: reuse-existing-authenticated-session-over-reauth
description: When you need programmatic access that a running application already holds valid credentials for: reuse its stored session rather than forcing a fresh authentication that burdens the user — and stop that application first if the credential cannot be used from two connections at once

name: verify-resilience-by-inducing-the-failure
description: When claiming a system recovers from a failure mode (reboot, crash, dependency loss): induce the actual failure and observe unattended recovery, rather than asserting recovery from configuration inspection alone

name: relay-self-warned-secret-via-human-entry
description: When a secret must be entered and its issuer warns against sharing it (one-time login codes, 2FA prompts): have the human enter it themselves through their own session so it never transits the assistant, rather than asking them to paste it into the conversation

name: extract-integration-contract-from-reference-implementation
description: Before building a component that must talk to the same external system an existing project already integrates with, dispatch a read-only agent to extract that project's integration contract — dependency/library, auth mechanism, exact endpoints or calls, cursor/state handling, and its test doubles — and port the proven pattern rather than designing the integration from scratch

name: assert-reference-set-superset-before-swapping-index
description: When replacing a file whose value is the set of references it holds (an index, manifest, or link list) with a rewritten version: extract the reference set from both the old and new file and assert the new set is a superset before swapping it in, rather than trusting a read-through or visual diff to catch a dropped pointer

name: stop-compaction-at-safe-margin-not-target
description: When compacting a reference or index already in its most compact structural form: stop at a safe margin below the hard limit rather than dropping entries to hit an aggressive size target — removing content is a decision for the owner, not a mechanical compaction step

name: decide-dependency-location-before-service-host
description: When choosing where to host a service that depends on co-located infrastructure (a message bus, a bridge, a database): decide where those dependencies live first — hosting the service apart from dependencies it still reaches over the network removes no reliability. Do not evaluate the service's host in isolation from where its dependencies run.

name: build-irreversible-capture-now-defer-analysis
description: When a feature splits into capturing data and analysing it, and the capture is irreversible (data dropped now cannot be recovered later): build the capture and retention now and defer the analysis. Never defer the part you cannot backfill.

name: surface-discovered-scope-instead-of-grinding
description: When execution reveals a task is materially larger than the plan or request described: surface the newly-discovered scope and let the requester re-decide, rather than silently continuing to grind through the expanded work.

name: rewrite-parked-tests-to-surviving-behaviour
description: When un-skipping tests parked by a redesign: rewrite each assertion to the observed current behaviour, one file at a time. For a feature the redesign removed, assert the surviving behaviour and let the feature's new home cover its capability — do not reconstruct the removed feature.

name: migration-difficulty-by-carried-state
description: Return a per-service migration-difficulty assessment classifying each service by the state it must carry: small config or a single-file DB -> easy (copy); session or device-pairing state -> medium (needs re-authentication); multi-terabyte blob store -> impractical. Give the carried-state reason per verdict.

name: port-effect-not-literal-across-platforms
description: When porting a deployment or config to a platform that lacks a feature the source relied on (e.g. systemd RuntimeMaxSec on launchd): reproduce the feature's effect with the target's native idiom (a scheduled companion job) rather than a fragile hack that mimics the source literally, and document the substitution. Never degrade the property silently.

name: no-dead-config-stub
description: When asked to expose a value as user-editable configuration that the code does not actually read from that location: do not ship a stub that looks live but does nothing. Either wire the code to read it, or document where the value really lives; never leave a dead switch a later editor will trust.

name: schedule-eager-refresh-over-lazy-on-demand
description: When a resource needs refreshing at most once per period and the unconditional refresh is cheap: prefer a scheduled eager refresh over a demand-triggered one. The work a lazy path saves rarely justifies the extra interception and failure surface it adds.

name: deployment-config-parse-tests
description: Return tests that parse each deployment config file (service unit, plist, env template) as data and assert its key directives — schedule/cadence, run identity, no secret inlined, referenced launcher paths exist and are git-tracked — without invoking the service manager or starting any process.

name: verify-copy-before-deleting-irreplaceable-source
description: When relocating irreplaceable data whose source will be deleted: copy to the destination and integrity-verify the copy before deleting the source, not moving in one step; retain the source until the destination passes verification

name: database-on-native-fs-not-virtualised-mount
description: When a database's data directory would sit on a network or virtualised filesystem (NFS, SMB, or a VM-mounted host volume such as virtiofs): place it on a native block device and migrate between hosts via dump/restore, keeping only bulk file assets on the mounted volume; such filesystems break the database's fsync durability and initialisation/permission assumptions

name: trust-direct-test-over-indirect-indicator
description: When an indirect status signal (process listing, port scan, cached flag, dashboard) and a direct end-to-end test disagree about whether something works: trust the direct test. The indirect tool may lack visibility into the real state.

name: sequence-cutover-source-off-snapshot-target-on
description: When relocating a stateful service to another host, order the cutover so the two runtimes never overlap: stop the source services first, then snapshot the authoritative state (single-file DB via a hot-safe copy plus integrity check, and any single-consumer cursor/offset file), copy it to the target, then start the target services. Overlapping runtimes double-consume a single-consumer cursor (e.g. a message-queue or getUpdates offset) or diverge two separately-written DBs; snapshotting between stop and start prevents lost writes.

name: audit-dependencies-for-headless-incompatibility
description: When planning a headless (login-less) server deployment, audit each dependency for a requirement that only an interactive GUI login session satisfies — menu-bar sync clients, file-provider extensions, GUI keychain prompts — because these do not run under a login-less daemon. For each incompatible dependency, replace it (local store plus a one-way sync from a machine that does run the GUI client) or relocate that responsibility off the headless box, rather than forcing GUI auto-login.

name: strip-blanks-and-quote-json-in-sourced-env-file
description: When a service's launcher sources a 0600 env file into a config layer that returns any set variable verbatim (env overrides the code default): strip empty-value KEY= lines because a blank becomes an empty string that overrides the constant fallback, and single-quote-wrap JSON values because bash source strips their inner double-quotes and breaks JSON parsing. Prove with one manual run before installing the daemons.

name: headless-private-repo-read-only-deploy-key
description: To clone a private repository onto a headless login-less server, register the box's own SSH public key as a read-only per-repo deploy key and clone over SSH, rather than HTTPS which fails non-interactively (no credential prompt) or an account-wide personal token which grants far more than one server that only pulls needs.

name: dedicated-service-token-not-interactive-session-reuse
description: For an unattended service that must authenticate as a human's existing account, mint a dedicated device or service token via a fresh credentialed login rather than reusing an interactive client's session token, which dies when that client signs out. Have the human supply the credential directly through a hidden prompt so it never enters the automation transcript, and never echo the minted token.

name: non-destructive-dedup-disposition
description: When forced to choose between preserving original files and reclaiming storage during deduplication: keep every copy and collapse duplicates behind one canonical (link or stack), never delete. Deletion is irreversible; a link is not.

name: backup-gate-before-deleting-a-redundant-copy
description: When about to delete a data copy that currently provides redundancy: block the deletion until an independent, offsite, restore-tested backup exists. Treat RAID or mirroring as not-a-backup — it survives disk failure, not deletion, corruption, or theft.

name: continue-on-nonfatal-error-in-idempotent-bulk-import
description: When a per-item error occurs during an idempotent bulk import and the error does not risk data loss: continue and log it, rather than halting the whole run on the first error. Re-running is safe because completed items are skipped by checksum.

name: verify-content-not-names-when-scoping-files
description: When scoping files for bulk processing and folder or file names imply their contents: verify by inspecting the actual content before including them, rather than trusting the names — names mislead, especially on work or shared accounts.

name: embed-source-provenance-before-ingest
description: Embed source provenance (origin account and folder path) into each item's metadata before importing it into a shared store.

name: enumerate-remote-store-serverside-before-transfer
description: Enumerate a remote store's full contents server-side before a bulk transfer, rather than trusting the locally-synced subset.

name: bulk-import-reconciliation-report
description: Return a bulk-import reconciliation with counts per category: found, imported, skipped-as-duplicate, upgraded, and failed (each failure with its cause), plus the net change against the prior total. If a category is empty: report 0, do not omit it.

name: data-protection-plan-321-with-gate
description: Return a data-protection plan with: each copy as (location, media type, role) satisfying 3-2-1 (three copies, two media, one offsite), the one-time setup steps, a scheduled backup job, a restore-test procedure, and the explicit gate that must pass before any destructive action it protects.

name: proxy-metric-structurally-identical-to-target
description: When a test cannot yet measure the real target metric such as purchase or revenue: instrument a proxy event that is structurally identical to the real event so it stays valid when the real metric arrives, not a cheaper signal that diverges from the target.

name: record-variant-on-impression-at-arrival
description: When instrumenting a variant experiment: record which variant was shown on the impression at arrival, not only on the conversion event, otherwise the conversion rate has no denominator for the visitors who did not convert.

name: stage-experiment-dimensions-at-low-traffic
description: When testing several experiment dimensions on a low-traffic product: stage them by testing the coarser dimension first and finer levels only within the winner, not a full-factorial cross-product the traffic cannot power.

name: geo-fence-out-strict-regimes-for-v1-test
description: When a v1 demand test would otherwise require a full consent or CMP compliance layer: exclude the strict-regime geographies from targeting to run under a lighter baseline rather than building the consent layer, and document a forward-compatible path to add it later.

name: narrow-claim-to-survive-strongest-counter-evidence
description: When an evidence-anchored claim would be rebutted by the strongest available counter-evidence: state the narrower claim that survives it, not the broad version, and hedge weak sources such as preprints or correlational studies to match their strength.

name: independent-review-against-real-codebase
description: Run an implementability review as an independent agent that reads the actual target codebase, not only the design document, to surface gaps the author of the document cannot see.

name: severity-grouped-review-issue-table
description: Return a severity-grouped issue table, blockers then spec-gaps then minor, with each issue giving an engineering-language description, a plain-language restatement, and a concrete recommended fix or an explicit forward-compatible deferral.

name: verify-target-before-destructive-storage-command
description: When about to run a destructive storage command (format, erase, eject, overwrite) that targets a device or path: first enumerate and confirm the exact target from a read-only listing, rather than issuing it from an assumed identifier — a wrong identifier is unrecoverable.

name: backup-restore-verification-report
description: Return a restore-verification result with: restored record count, live record count, count-reconciliation verdict within a stated tolerance, number of original files actually sampled and checked, number missing, and a single PASS or FAIL. FAIL if zero files were checked or counts diverge beyond tolerance.

name: fail-verification-on-zero-items-checked
description: When a verification completes having actually checked zero items: return FAIL, not PASS. A vacuous pass — no failures found because nothing was examined — must never count as success; count the items examined and require it to be non-zero.

name: resolve-capable-binary-by-path-not-name
description: When a script needs a tool capability the OS default binary lacks (GNU vs BSD/openrsync, older vs newer): resolve the capable binary by explicit path plus a capability check, rather than calling the bare command name — PATH resolution differs between interactive shells and launchd/cron.

name: capture-output-before-match-under-pipefail
description: When testing a command's output inside a script under set -o pipefail: capture the full output into a variable then match it, rather than piping the producer into grep -q or head — their early pipe-close SIGPIPEs the producer, and pipefail then reports the whole pipeline as failed, a false negative.

name: guard-command-substitution-under-set-e
description: When a command-substitution assignment under set -e may legitimately fail (a query that can return nothing): append || true or handle it explicitly, so the script reaches its own informative error path instead of exiting silently at the assignment.

name: encrypt-storage-while-empty
description: When encrypting a storage volume can be done now while it is empty or deferred until after data lands: encrypt now. Encrypting afterwards is slower (re-encrypts everything) and, on SSDs, can leave plaintext remnants in flash of the very data the encryption was meant to protect.

name: merge-metadata-from-designated-source-of-truth
description: When merging two datasets whose overlapping records carry conflicting metadata: designate one dataset the source of truth, keep its values for every shared record, and take the other's values only for records unique to it. Make the source-of-truth dataset the merge destination so an automerge preserves its metadata instead of overwriting with the incoming copy.

name: dedup-keep-most-complete-and-merge-before-delete
description: When deduplicating records and choosing which copy to keep: keep the most complete copy (most attributes/formats, largest file per shared attribute); before deleting the other, merge into the keeper any attribute the loser uniquely holds. Never let a dedup drop an attribute that existed on the deleted copy.

name: serialize-writes-to-shared-mutable-store
description: When many independent units each produce changes destined for one shared mutable store (database, file, catalogue): fan the analysis and plan-building out in parallel as read-only workers, but apply the writes serially through a single writer. Never let parallel workers mutate the shared store concurrently — concurrent writes corrupt it.

name: validate-machine-generated-ops-before-applying
description: Validate machine-generated operations before applying them to a store: normalise heterogeneous outputs to one schema, then confirm every referenced id exists, no id collides across sources, and each destructive op names both its keep and delete targets.

name: primary-source-priority-for-relational-facts
description: When verifying relational reference facts (canonical ordering, membership, numbering): consult sources in priority — first-party/official (publisher, author, standards body) → structured aggregators → community reference sites → encyclopaedic. Use identity-resolution sources for identity only, not for relational facts they represent poorly. Report the source per fact and flag disputes rather than choosing silently.

name: verify-gating-assumption-with-minimal-probe
description: When a bulk or irreversible operation depends on an unverified assumption about how a target system behaves: prove the assumption with the smallest possible probe first; do not rely on documentation or reasoning

name: dry-run-mapping-before-bulk-rename
description: Before a bulk rename or file transform, produce the full source-to-target mapping with a collision check and surface it for review before executing

name: bulk-file-transform-plan
description: Return a bulk-transform plan with: every source-to-target mapping, a collision or duplicate report, count of items changed versus unchanged, and any unmapped items flagged

name: zero-pad-numbers-for-lexical-sort
description: When a consuming system orders strings lexically and numeric order matters: zero-pad embedded numbers to a fixed width; do not rely on natural numeric ordering

name: verify-example-current-health-not-just-history
description: When choosing a real organisation as a success example: verify its present-day commercial health separately from the historical facts of the decision, and prefer a currently-healthy example over one with a stronger story but a current reversal an audience could cite.

name: verify-and-attribute-quotes-drop-if-weak
description: When placing a well-known quote in a published deliverable: verify it against a primary or archive source and distinguish verbatim from paraphrase and a headline from body prose; if it can only be weakly sourced, drop it rather than caveat it in the deliverable.

name: source-licensed-images-fit-and-fetchable
description: Source openly-licensed images matching a required aspect ratio and background transparency, and confirm each is fetchable by the target platform before use

name: split-atomic-batch-into-per-item-retries
description: When a batch API call fails atomically if any single item is invalid: issue one request per item with a bounded retry loop, so one bad item drops only itself rather than failing the whole batch

name: speak-from-memory-talk-runsheet
description: Return a speak-from-memory talk runsheet: per beat, spoken lines as plain bullets with all non-spoken content in brackets, exactly one bolded takeaway line, facts (figures, dates, names) embedded in the spoken bullets, and each slide typed SET-UP or TAKEAWAY; append a sources block citing one primary or archive source per quoted claim

name: select-target-subset-by-defining-attribute-not-container
description: When a target subset shares a container (a table, folder, stack, or label) with a look-alike population that must be excluded: select the subset by its own defining attribute, not by membership in the shared container, and assert the resulting count matches expectations before any destructive or expensive step.

name: identify-removable-drive-by-sentinel-uuid
description: Identify a removable volume by a sentinel marker file holding a fixed UUID and use that volume's real resolved mountpoint, never a volume name or a hard-coded mount path.
