name: verify-source-real-and-nonempty-before-mirror
description: Before a delete-propagating mirror sync, verify the source is a real mount that is non-empty and near its expected size; abort the sync otherwise.

name: cap-destructive-sync-with-max-delete-threshold
description: Cap a delete-propagating sync with a max-delete threshold so an unexpected mass deletion aborts the run instead of executing.

name: fail-closed-on-ambiguous-safety-check
description: When a safety guard's check returns an ambiguous, empty, or unparseable result (encryption state, host identity, integrity): fail closed. Require an explicit positive confirmation to proceed, and never treat absence-of-a-negative as a pass.

name: mark-dependent-blocked-when-prerequisite-fails
description: When a pipeline step depends on another step's output and that prerequisite errors or is unavailable: mark the dependent with a distinct blocked state, never done, and never run it on stale or absent input.

name: address-swappable-host-by-role-alias
description: Address a replaceable host by a stable role alias (a DNS or SSH-config name) so the machine can be swapped by re-pointing the alias, never by hard-coding its hostname or IP.

name: compute-shared-encode-once-per-item-for-dependents
description: In a batch pipeline where several steps derive from one expensive computation, run that shared computation once per item and hold its result for all dependent steps, rather than recomputing it per step.

name: profile-prose-style-with-evidence
description: Characterise how a text is written rather than what it argues, supporting every stylistic claim with a verbatim quote from the source

name: prose-style-profile
description: Return a prose-style profile covering tone, diction, content-building, register, punctuation and typography, examples, citation habits, and sentence rhythm; back every claim with a verbatim quote and its source; add a signature-moves list and 3-5 sentences that could only be this author

name: audit-prose-against-style-tell-checklist
description: Audit a draft against a named checklist of style tells (formulaic reframes, rule-of-three, benefit-lists, banned words, em-dash density) and report each tell's count before and after editing

name: commit-to-one-register-per-piece
description: When two valid registers are available for a piece (for example cool and detached versus warm and emotive): choose one and hold it across the whole piece rather than blending them, because a warm move inside a detached frame reads as incoherent

name: verify-live-schema-before-bulk-op
description: When code assumes an external system's schema (column names, enum values and their case, path formats) and a bulk read or write is about to run: verify each against the running instance first, not against the spec, docs, or a prior assumption — an uppercase-vs-lowercase enum or a container-vs-host path silently voids the whole run

name: investigate-firing-gate-before-override
description: When a precondition or safety gate blocks on an unexpected value: investigate and explain the deviation's cause before overriding it; override only by supplying the corrected parameter once the deviation is confirmed benign — never suppress a firing gate to make the operation proceed

name: integration-smoke-before-long-unattended-run
description: Before launching a long unattended run that writes to production: execute the real pipeline (real models, real DB, real files) on 2-3 items and assert the side-effects landed; do not launch straight from green unit tests, which use injected fakes and a throwaway DB and cannot prove the live wiring

name: scope-batch-backlog-to-active-stages
description: Scope a resumable batch worker's claim query to the subset of processing stages actually being run, so a partial run drains to completion instead of re-claiming items whose un-run stages stay pending forever

name: embedding-model-by-retrieval-quality-for-backfill
description: When choosing an embedding model for a one-time backfill over a fixed corpus: optimise for retrieval quality, not encode speed or vector dimension — storage and query latency rarely bind at corpus scale, the backfill runs once, re-embedding is a cheap redo, and the dimension is fixed by the architecture rather than a free knob

name: inject-models-so-logic-core-tests-offline
description: When building a system with external-model or live-service dependencies: make them constructor-injected so the logic core (schema, state, writers, load and dedup) tests against a throwaway container DB with fakes and never touches prod, and gate the real-model wrappers plus end-to-end acceptance to a later hardware phase — rather than requiring the full rig to test anything

name: teleprompter-script-from-talk
description: Return a teleprompter-ready script of the talk's spoken text only: each section prefixed with a slide marker giving the slide number and a one-line summary of what is on that slide, with any non-spoken cue on its own clearly-marked line

name: enforce-terminal-state-at-claim-and-eligibility
description: When a retry/attempt cap must stop reprocessing a failed work item: enforce the terminal state at BOTH the claim query and the eligibility check. A cap applied only at claim is defeated when a sibling stage on the same item keeps it claimable, and the capped stage re-runs forever.

name: prefilter-poison-items-from-batch
description: When one item's exception in a batched stage would fail the whole batch: pre-filter known-bad items out and record each individually as failed, rather than letting a single poison input fail the good items with it.

name: validate-locally-before-metered-compute
description: When work will run on metered or rented compute: complete and validate all unproven or unbuilt work on local or owned hardware first, and run only proven code on the meter. Never debug new code on a per-minute meter.

name: minimal-derived-input-for-sensitive-data-offsite
description: When sensitive data must be processed on third-party or rented infrastructure: send only the minimal derived representation the task actually needs (e.g. a downscaled preview) so full-fidelity sensitive originals never leave controlled infrastructure.

name: diagnose-stalled-worker-before-assuming-resource-limits
description: Diagnose a stalled worker by querying per-item state and sampling the process's hot code path before assuming resource exhaustion.

name: verify-completeness-from-existing-records
description: Verify a dataset's completeness from the system's own verification records (checksums, count reconciliations) before re-deriving it.

name: pre-execution-engineering-review
description: Return a pre-execution engineering review with: severity-ranked blockers (each with a concrete failure scenario and fix), warnings, and friction; a point-by-point stress-test of the design's own stated assumptions plus unstated ones; and a GO / GO-WITH-FIXES / NO-GO verdict with the top-3 preconditions that must hold before starting.

name: geo-context-hint-not-driver
description: When a contextual signal (location, timestamp, source metadata) could inform a content-derived classification: use it as a soft prior that widens trust or breaks ties, never as an override that contradicts the observed content.

name: out-of-domain-confidence-is-suspect
description: When a model runs on inputs outside its training domain: treat confident predictions as suspect and raise the acceptance threshold, because out-of-domain inputs produce confident-but-wrong outputs.

name: instantiate-only-required-components
description: When running a subset of a multi-component pipeline under resource constraints: instantiate only the components that subset needs, never eager-load the full set.

name: open-vocab-needs-generative-model
description: When the requirement is open-vocabulary extraction (labels not known in advance): use a generative model, not a fixed-candidate classifier whose generality is bounded by its predefined label list.

name: corroborate-before-emitting-noisy-tag
description: When a tag is derived from noisy extraction (OCR, transcription, detection): require corroborating evidence (a contiguous run, repetition, agreement across parts) before emitting it, rather than acting on a single occurrence.

name: score-per-segment-not-concatenation
description: When classifying multi-part input where some parts are uninformative noise: score each substantial segment independently and aggregate, rather than one pass over the concatenation that noise can dominate.

name: pre-stage-before-access-is-lost
description: When a needed resource will soon become inaccessible (a drive removed, an API deprecated, an account expiring): pre-stage what later work needs while it is still available, erring toward more, because being short afterward is unfixable.

name: detect-language-script-first
description: Detect text language by Unicode-script analysis, authoritative for non-Latin scripts, using a statistical detector only for Latin scripts.

name: keep-the-pitch-implicit-when-building-authority
description: When a piece is meant to build authority or credibility: keep any pitch implicit and let demonstrated competence do the persuading, rather than adding an explicit ask or a self-promotional closer.

name: present-illustrated-regularity-as-pattern-not-law
description: When a regularity is illustrated but not proven: present it as an observed pattern and hedge the claim to match the evidence, rather than dressing it as a law.

name: quality-validation-on-available-hardware-defer-production
description: When a faster compute tier needed for a production run is unavailable but a slower tier is: run the quality-validation pass on the slower tier now — a quality or correctness read is independent of hardware speed (only the throughput and cost projection degrade) — and defer only the throughput-sensitive production run to the faster tier.

name: fixed-compute-cost-favours-faster-tier
description: When selecting hardware for a fixed-size compute job: total cost equals work times price divided by throughput, so prefer the faster tier whenever its price premium is smaller than its throughput gain. Do not assume the lower per-hour option is cheaper overall; a slow cheap tier can cost more and take far longer.

name: emit-portable-files-when-datastore-unreachable
description: When the target datastore is unreachable at compute time: emit results to portable self-describing files keyed by a stable identity and merge later via an idempotent loader, rather than blocking the compute or coupling it to the live store. The merge is a separate step run when the store is reachable.

name: guarantee-teardown-with-trap-and-independent-watchdog
description: Tear down an unattended metered resource via both a delete-on-any-exit trap and an independent wall-clock watchdog that force-deletes at a hard cap

name: exclude-via-provenance-at-query-not-drop-at-compute
description: When a subset must be excludable from results but dropping it at processing time would leave a coverage hole: process the full set and preserve a provenance or source label so the subset can be excluded at query time, rather than removing it from the pipeline. Keep sensitive identifying labels out of any untrusted environment.

name: check-network-before-assuming-credential-rotation
description: When an API auth call fails as invalid-token but the same credential worked recently: check DNS resolution, network reachability, and any IP-allowlist before assuming the credential rotated. A resolver flap or an IP access-control rejection surfaces as a generic auth error.

name: test-double-must-mirror-transport-side-effects
description: When writing a test double for an external transport (object store, queue, filesystem): reproduce its structural side effects — where it lands files, what it names them, which error codes it returns — not just its interface. A double that differs structurally hides exactly the bugs the test claims to cover.

name: isolate-one-variable-when-two-changed-together
description: When a disappointing result has two plausible causes that changed at the same time: re-run holding one constant before investing in fixing either. Improving the wrong variable is indistinguishable from improving the right one until the controlled comparison exists.

name: recompute-headline-metric-from-raw-artefact
description: When a stored summary field and the raw output it summarises both exist: recompute the metric from the raw output before citing it in a decision. Stored summaries can combine incompatible bases (a rate measured on one configuration multiplied by a price from another).

name: gate-on-downstream-effect-not-well-formedness
description: When defining the acceptance gate for a pipeline stage: gate on whether the output changes the downstream decision, not on whether it is well-formed. A format gate can pass at full marks while the stage delivers no value.

name: windowed-not-cumulative-abort-threshold
description: When setting an abort threshold on a long-running job: compute the failure rate over a trailing window, not cumulatively from the start. A cumulative ratio becomes mathematically unable to fire once enough clean history has accumulated, so the guard silently stops guarding.

name: record-why-a-value-is-absent
description: When a record can be missing for several different reasons (never attempted, attempted and found nothing, failed, deliberately excluded): store the reason alongside the absence. Absence without a recorded cause makes every negative query unsound and the failure is invisible to the person reading the results.

name: verify-completed-items-can-be-reopened
description: When a pipeline is expected to re-run over items it has already processed (better model, larger vocabulary, new stage): verify that a completed item can be re-opened through a supported path before building. Pipelines that stamp completion once treat re-running as an error, and the gap surfaces only when the second pass is already needed.

name: stamp-run-identity-on-state-row-not-output-row
description: When outputs may legitimately be empty: record the run identity and computation timestamp on the per-item state row rather than on the output rows. Staleness computed from output rows cannot see the items that produced no output — which are exactly the items a better model would newly match.

name: measure-approach-agnostic-fraction-before-switching
description: When deciding whether to change technical approach mid-project: measure what proportion of the existing code is approach-agnostic before arguing from sunk cost. The argument is usually conducted on the assumption that switching discards everything, and the measurement often shows most of the work survives any choice.

name: judge-composed-agent-by-output-not-fitness-score
description: When a composed agent reports low composition fitness or a pool-coverage warning: run it and judge the output rather than re-composing. Fitness measures how well the primitive pool covers the task, not how good the result will be — a poorly-matched composition can still produce the strongest findings.

name: code-review-with-unguaranteed-claims-list
description: Return a code review containing: (1) findings ordered by severity, each with file:line, a concrete failure scenario stating inputs or state and the resulting wrong behaviour, and a proposed fix; (2) a separate list of correctness claims made in comments and docstrings that the code does not actually guarantee; (3) an overall verdict (approve | approve with changes | request changes). If a claim cannot be checked without running the system, mark it unverified rather than assuming it holds.

name: verify-canon-claim-against-implementation-before-irreversible-advice
description: Before advising a physical or irreversible action on the basis of a design or canon document: verify the specific claim the advice turns on against the implementation record (config, code, decision log). Canon documents go wrong in the direction of what was originally planned, not what was built, so the error is systematically pointed at the decisions that changed.

name: check-what-in-flight-work-reads-before-moving-infrastructure
description: When asked whether to relocate infrastructure while work is in progress: first determine what the in-flight work actually reads. If it reads a location-independent store, the move is orthogonal to it and should be sequenced on its own merits rather than treated as blocking or blocked.

name: check-sampling-frame-before-conceding-to-counter-evidence
description: When a cited study appears to refute the claim under test: establish its sampling frame, inclusion criteria and outcome variable before conceding. If the study's population excludes the population under discussion, report it as out of frame rather than as contradicting, and say which population each result covers.

name: verify-identifier-registry-before-recording-source-dead
description: When a source URL returns an authorisation error or bot block to an automated request: verify the identifier against its registry API before recording the source as unavailable, and never substitute an aggregator or search-result URL for the canonical one. Record in the output that the registry check was performed.

name: cut-process-not-substance-when-shortening
description: When instructed to shorten a document by removing framing, hedging or provenance: remove only process sentences describing how the work was done. Never remove a claim, figure, source, or conceded objection in order to reach a shorter length. Verify afterwards that every section of the source argument is still represented.

name: treat-on-disk-file-as-authoritative-over-last-draft
description: When the file on disk differs from your last draft of it: treat the on-disk version as authoritative, build the next version on it, and enumerate the author's changes rather than overwriting them. Flag any authorial deletion you believe should be reinstated instead of silently restoring it.

name: report-absence-of-evidence-as-a-scoped-finding
description: When a search returns no evidence for a claim under test: report the absence as a scoped finding naming what was searched and what population is unmeasured, rather than substituting adjacent evidence or your own judgement. Treat a well-scoped absence as a result, not a failure.

name: distinguish-level-effect-from-rate-change
description: Distinguish a large effect within a subpopulation from a change in an aggregate rate, and state explicitly which of the two the evidence supports.

name: check-measurement-instrument-validity-for-the-period-measured
description: Check whether a measurement instrument was designed for the period, taxonomy or population being measured before treating a null result from it as informative.

name: per-claim-evidence-table
description: Return a per-claim evidence table with one row per claim: verdict (verified | partially-verified-with-correction | not-found), the finding stated in the source's own terms, the numbers, the sample and period, the full citation with identifier, and a live URL. Include a required section for evidence that contradicts or complicates the claims. If no evidence is found for a claim: return not-found. Do not infer.

name: evidence-status-register
description: Return an evidence-status register classifying every claim in the deliverable as one of: sourced-and-verified, unrefereed-must-be-labelled, author's-assertion, reasoning-not-finding, testimony-only, or not-found. Include a must-not-use list naming each specific figure or phrase that failed verification and why.

name: annotation-resolution-list
description: Return a revision that preserves the author's section names, ordering and wording, accompanied by a numbered list of their annotations with how each was addressed, and an explicit flag for any authorial deletion that was not reinstated.

name: repair-one-record-through-the-production-code-path
description: When a batch run against an external system fails partway and one record must be filed by hand: call the application's own production functions in their production order rather than composing fresh API requests, so the repaired record is indistinguishable from a normal one and the ordering contract (persist identifiers before any irreversible upload) still holds.

name: never-silently-coerce-an-unrepresentable-input
description: When an interface cannot represent an incoming or extracted value: reject it or force an explicit choice, never fall back to a valid-looking default. A silent fallback to the first option produces data that passes every downstream check while being wrong.

name: source-selector-options-from-the-downstream-validator
description: Source a selector's option list from the same authority the downstream validator checks against, so a value the validator would accept can always be selected and one it would reject cannot

name: preflight-batch-through-its-own-validator-against-live-state
description: Before triggering an irreversible batch write, run the system's own validator over every pending record against live external state and report how many would be rejected and why

name: refuse-an-action-that-would-revert-the-correction-just-made
description: When a requested action would undo a correction already applied and return the artefact to the state the user is trying to fix: apply the correction, skip the action, and state the conflict plainly rather than executing a request whose effect defeats its own purpose.

name: verify-artifact-identity-against-its-record-before-deleting
description: Before deleting a file or row that mirrors state in an external system: verify its identity against the stored hash or identifier, snapshot the datastore, and confirm the surviving counterpart still resolves — never delete on filename or position alone.

name: state-credential-without-interpreting-it
description: When citing a recipient's own credential or past work to justify approaching them: state the fact and stop. Do not append an explanation of why it matters or what role it will play — telling accomplished people the significance of their own work reads as condescending, and the bare fact is more flattering.

name: disclose-current-state-over-promising-conduct
description: When an unresolved situation could be handled by promising future disclosure ("I'll tell you once it's settled") or by disclosing the actual current state: disclose the current state, including unflattering incompleteness. A promise about future conduct is worth less to the recipient than the real picture now.

name: frame-scope-limits-as-properties-not-preferences
description: When stating what a piece of work, event, or discussion is not about: frame the limit as a property of the thing ("this session isn't about X") rather than as the author's personal preference ("I'm not looking for X"). Keep first person for the invitation or request itself.

name: check-prior-correspondence-before-outreach
description: Before drafting outreach to a named person, search the sender's own message archive for prior correspondence with them and anyone connected to the same effort; use what it returns to set the opening, the ask, and any threads left unanswered

name: state-contestable-claims-as-normative
description: When a claim would be false as a description of the world but is defensible as a value ("nobody else gets to define it for you" vs "nobody else should get to define it for you"): state it as a norm. Asserting a contestable value as a fact invites the counterexample instead of the agreement.

name: report-inconsistency-across-already-sent-messages
description: When two messages already sent by the same organisation to overlapping recipients state conflicting facts (dates, figures, names) and the conflict surfaces while drafting a third: report it to the sender rather than silently adopting either version or propagating the one nearest to hand.

name: extract-voice-rules-by-diffing-sent-against-drafted
description: When the user's final or sent version of a drafted document becomes available, diff it against the draft and record each delta as a named, reusable rule with the reason it was made; treat every cut as evidence about what the user values, not as a one-off correction

name: enumerate-container-before-declaring-item-absent
description: When a search returns a matching container (email thread, file, directory, record set), enumerate that container's contents directly before concluding any item is absent from it

name: targeted-edits-over-recomposed-body
description: When editing a document the author is also editing: apply targeted replacements checked against the file on disk, never a body recomposed from context, even for purely structural changes such as renumbering

name: propose-restoration-never-reinstate-deleted-text
description: When text the author deliberately deleted appears worth keeping: propose restoring it and let the author decide, rather than reinserting it during an unrelated edit

name: attach-explicit-request-to-every-outstanding-item
description: In a document asking a counterparty to act, attach an explicit request to every outstanding item named; stating a quantity or status is not requesting it

name: negotiation-round-response-assessment
description: Return an assessment of a counterparty's revised document against the prior list of asks: per ask, the old clause reference and wording, the new clause reference and wording, and a verdict (resolved | partial | unaddressed | regressed); plus a separate section listing obligations the revision introduces that no ask covers

name: check-revisions-for-regressions-not-only-fixes
description: When assessing a revised document, check for regressions as well as fixes: definitions dropped, terms removed, obligations tightened, protections narrowed since the prior version

name: identify-bespoke-content-dropped-by-standard-template
description: When a counterparty replaces a negotiated document with a standard template, list the negotiated content the template drops silently (clauses removed outright rather than left as marked blanks) and require its reinstatement

name: search-internal-records-for-existing-decision-before-drafting-response
description: Before drafting a response to an outstanding external request, search internal records (minutes, decision logs, prior approvals) for a decision that already answers it

name: literal-labels-over-markup-for-uncontrolled-renderers
description: When a document will be pasted into a renderer you do not control: use literal text labels for section numbering rather than list markup the renderer may renumber

name: declare-emphasis-convention-in-opening
description: When a document uses formatting to mark action items, state that convention in its opening line so the reader can triage without inferring it

name: hint-reorders-candidates-never-filters-them
description: When an optional user-supplied hint could narrow an automated candidate list (calendar events, search results, match sets): use it to reorder the candidates, never to filter them, so a hint that matches nothing leaves the pre-existing ranking intact instead of returning an empty list.

name: order-new-work-behind-the-defect-it-inherits
description: When newly captured work routes its output through a component with an already-logged defect: name that defect as an explicit prerequisite inside the new task item, rather than filing the two as independent items that can be scheduled in either order.

name: point-at-the-existing-implementation-and-name-the-difference
description: When a requested capability resembles one the codebase already implements: point the task at reusing that component and state explicitly what differs in the new context, rather than specifying a second parallel implementation.

name: human-assertion-overrides-extraction-with-recorded-provenance
description: When a human's explicit assertion accompanying a submission contradicts a value derived from the submitted content (OCR, parsing, model extraction): the assertion wins, and the output records which fields came from the human rather than from the content.

name: group-by-change-trigger-not-by-topic
description: When subdividing a body of work into folders, modules or sections and topical grouping conflicts with grouping by what changes each part: group by change trigger and the clock it runs on, not by subject matter. State the filing rule as a question about what would cause an item to change.

name: separate-reusable-template-from-filled-instance
description: When an artefact exists both as a reusable template and as a filled-in instance: file the template with the reusable material and each filled instance with the specific occasion it belongs to. Storing them together makes the next reuse start from a previous occasion’s answers.

name: stand-up-structure-defer-the-move
description: When a structural reorganisation surfaces mid-task and a time-critical deliverable depends on the same area: create the new structure and register existing items into it under their target locations, but move nothing yet. Write the migration up as a named pending task listing its prerequisites.

name: update-every-artefact-that-narrates-a-changed-process
description: When a process or mechanic changes, enumerate every artefact that describes that process and update each one, not only the artefact where the change was made. A covering note, an instruction sheet and a schedule each narrate the same procedure independently.

name: reconcile-stated-total-against-part-limits
description: When a specification states both an overall limit and per-part limits: check that the parts sum to the stated total and report the discrepancy, rather than silently honouring one of the two figures.

name: query-api-schema-before-assuming-capability-absent
description: Query an API’s discovery or schema document for the specific capability before designing around its supposed absence.

name: read-back-remote-writes-to-verify-rendering
description: After writing to a remote document or service, read the artefact back through the API and confirm each structural element rendered as specified before reporting completion.

name: insert-body-once-then-style-by-computed-offset
description: For index-addressed document APIs, insert the full text body in one operation and then apply styling using offsets computed from the known string, rather than interleaving inserts and style calls whose indices shift.

name: verify-published-artefact-from-the-consumer-endpoint
description: Verify a published artefact by fetching it from the URL or channel consumers actually use, not by inspecting the local or source copy

name: pointer-over-restatement-in-documents
description: When a document would restate a fact defined authoritatively elsewhere (a schema, a limit, a procedure): cite the source and instruct reading the live value at use time, rather than copying it in. A copy drifts silently; a pointer cannot

name: comply-with-a-blocking-gate-never-widen-it
description: When an allowlist or safety gate blocks an action: satisfy it by relocating or amending the blocked item to fit the existing rule, never by widening the rule to admit it

name: diff-both-directions-before-deleting-a-duplicate
description: Before deleting a file as a duplicate, diff it in both directions; the copy being removed may hold content the survivor lacks

name: unsolved-problem-statement-for-later-design
description: Return a problem statement for a deferred design decision containing: every observed instance of the failure; why each obvious framing of it is wrong; the questions to think through before building anything; the constraints any solution must survive; and what has already been done so it is not redone. State explicitly that it is a problem statement and not a plan

name: repair-working-documents-annotate-historical-records
description: When a defect appears in both working documents and historical records: repair the working documents in place, but in historical records leave the original and append the correction beside it with a note explaining why

name: distinguish-never-updated-from-corrupted
description: When an artefact is wrong, establish whether it was corrupted or simply never updated: a validation guard prevents the first, automation prevents the second

name: publish-from-committed-state-not-working-tree
description: When publishing an artefact from a repository another process may be writing to: publish from a committed state rather than the live working tree

name: match-destination-collection-conventions
description: Match an existing published collection's front matter, heading structure, and footer conventions by reading two or three of its siblings before authoring a new entry

name: archive-published-content-before-deleting-it
description: Archive a published artefact's content with headmatter recording its audience, its ask, and its retirement date before deleting it

name: prefer-live-surface-over-internal-doc-for-published-facts
description: When an internal document and the live published surface disagree on a fact that is already public (a stated age range, a form URL, an entity description): treat the live surface as authoritative, correct the internal document, and say which was wrong

name: unlist-before-deleting-externally-linked-content
description: When retiring published content that external recipients may hold links to: unlist it from indexes first and keep the URL alive; delete only on an explicit instruction, and only after an archived copy exists

name: fetch-served-asset-before-blaming-the-source
description: When a published page renders wrong for the author but the source looks correct: fetch the served asset over the network before editing anything; if the served copy is already correct, treat it as a caching fault and fix it with a versioned asset URL rather than changing markup

name: add-only-the-requested-section-to-an-author-edited-file
description: When adding to a document the author has edited in place: write only the requested section plus the counters and headings that would otherwise contradict it, leave every other line as the author wrote it, and report exactly what was touched

name: parallel-variant-until-the-author-chooses
description: When the author asks to see a different treatment of an existing document: produce it as a new version alongside, cross-link both, and mark neither superseded until the author picks one

name: format-per-section-not-per-document
description: When a formatting change helps some sections and hurts others: apply it section by section rather than uniformly. Bullets for lists of parameters; prose for judgement, character description, and anything a reader could mistake for eligibility criteria

name: single-body-brief-with-swappable-asks
description: Return an outreach brief with: one audience-agnostic overview usable cold by any counterparty type; one labelled ask per counterparty type, each written to follow straight on from the overview; and a separate not-for-sending section listing every claim not verified against a source plus what was deliberately left out and why

name: publication-record-for-a-pushed-artefact
description: Return a publication record with: destination repository and path, commit sha, live URL, the verification status of that URL after deployment, and the procedure to update it including where the current file sha comes from

name: omit-secondary-sourced-facts-about-the-addressee
description: When a factual claim about the person being addressed (a figure, tenure, headcount, title) can be sourced only to press or directory pages and not to a first-party page: drop the unverifiable part rather than state it back to them. They know the true value, and a wrong one costs more than the omission.

name: recheck-previously-reported-defects-on-each-review-pass
description: On each review of a revised document, re-check every defect reported in the previous pass and state which remain unfixed before reporting new ones

name: derive-next-in-series-from-last-approved-version
description: When producing the next document in a series of near-identical documents and the author edited the previous one before releasing it: build from the released version, not from your own draft or the original template. The author's edits are the current specification.

name: narrow-the-claim-when-promised-source-material-is-missing
description: When source material the deliverable was to be built on never arrives (an attachment that did not attach, a promised transcript): produce the version that stands on what is verifiable, mark the narrowed passage, and name the missing input. Do not reconstruct its content by inference, and do not block the whole deliverable on it.

name: settle-externally-sent-conflict-and-decide-correction-per-recipient
description: When a conflicting fact already sent to overlapping recipients is finally settled: record which recipients hold which version, then decide per recipient whether a correction is owed. Someone no longer involved in the affected work needs none; anyone still acting on it does.

name: reconcile-stated-quantities-with-enumerated-items-after-edits
description: After a document is edited, re-check every quantity stated in its prose against the items actually enumerated, and flag any that no longer agree

name: own-a-delimited-block-in-a-shared-document
description: When writing generated content into a document a person also edits: own a block delimited by your own heading and replace only from that heading down, so anything they wrote outside it survives every regeneration

name: assert-copies-unedited-before-propagating-a-template
description: When propagating a template change across copies that recipients may already have filled in: assert each copy still holds only template content before overwriting it, and abort on that copy rather than proceeding, so a recipient's entries are never silently replaced

name: narrowest-edit-operation-that-achieves-the-change
description: When propagating an author's edit into other copies: choose the narrowest operation that achieves it — a targeted text replacement over a section rebuild — because a rebuild puts adjacent author content at risk that a replacement cannot touch

name: validate-an-aggregation-with-an-adversarial-synthetic-record
description: Validate a computed aggregation by inserting one synthetic record built to exercise its edge cases rather than its easy path, confirming each computed figure against a hand-calculated expectation, then deleting the record

name: match-rendered-extent-not-container-bounds
description: When sizing an element to match an existing one's apparent size: measure the rendered content extent rather than the container, then derive the new container from it, because padding or quiet zones make equal containers render at unequal visible sizes

name: rule-out-validator-sensitivity-before-blaming-the-artefact
description: When a validator rejects an artefact produced by a deterministic generator: vary the validator's own inputs — scale, encoding, rendering style — before concluding the artefact is malformed, and only report failure once the tool's sensitivity is ruled out

name: cross-reference-related-record-before-merging
description: When new data appears to complete or continue an existing record: add an explicit cross-reference between the two and ask before merging them into one record. Do not merge silently — the separation may be the filing decision.

name: apply-narrowed-instruction-to-named-instance-only
description: When a requester replaces a broad instruction with a narrower one naming a specific instance: apply the change only to the named instance, then offer the remaining instances as a separate explicit choice rather than sweeping them.

name: verify-entitlement-at-the-specific-point-of-use
description: When a general entitlement, policy, or capability is claimed for a specific case: verify it holds at the exact point of use (location, variant, tier, date) and report the boundary that applies, not the general rule.

name: report-source-conflict-with-authoritative-referral
description: When sources disagree on a checkable fact, report the disagreement with each source's claim intact and name the party who can settle it authoritatively; do not average the sources or pick one silently

name: emit-ambiguity-marker-when-evidence-underdetermines
description: When the available evidence does not decide between candidate values: emit an explicit ambiguity marker and keep every candidate at an unconfident score, rather than picking the most common one. A confident wrong value is indistinguishable downstream from a confident right one, and honesty must not cost recall.

name: evaluate-with-production-grade-components
description: Run every component of an evaluation at the grade that will run in production. A stronger model standing in for a weaker one measures whether the information is present, not whether the system will recover it.

name: extract-deterministically-never-infer-verifiable-values
description: When a value is computable or decodable exactly (checksummed identifiers, timestamps, coordinates, barcodes): extract it deterministically and mark its provenance, never ask a model to read it. A model cannot answer 'I cannot read this' and will return something well-formed and wrong.

name: abort-batch-on-non-item-specific-failure
description: When a batch item fails for a reason that is not specific to the item (missing dependency, absent schema column, unreachable service): abort the batch rather than continuing. Complements per-item isolation, which applies only when the next item could plausibly succeed.

name: state-evidence-basis-before-the-claim
description: State how something is known before stating what is known: recorded, decoded, read, or inferred. A claim presented without its basis cannot be distinguished later from one that was measured.

name: stratify-fixture-toward-failure-prone-minority
description: When building a test fixture from a skewed population: stratify deliberately toward the minority cases that break things rather than sampling randomly, and record the strata. A representative sample under-represents exactly what needs testing.

name: collect-human-judgement-blind-to-condition
description: Present competing outputs to a human judge without revealing which condition produced which, with labels revealed only after judgement. Otherwise the judgement cannot be distinguished from a verdict on the hypothesis.

name: address-hosts-by-stable-name-not-cached-ip
description: When a script, alias or config must reach a host whose network address can change: address it by stable name (DNS entry, tailnet MagicDNS name), not by an IP literal. A cached address breaks every shortcut that holds it, all at once, and fails silently.

name: distinguish-unreachable-target-from-empty-result
description: Discriminate on exit code so an unreachable target and a target that returned nothing produce different messages, not identical empty output

name: bound-remote-probes-with-explicit-connect-timeout
description: Set an explicit connect timeout on every remote probe so an unreachable target fails in seconds instead of hanging for the default TCP timeout

name: exercise-the-failure-path-against-a-known-bad-target
description: Test the error branch as well as the success branch by running a copy of the code against a deliberately unreachable or invalid target

name: rule-out-stale-session-state-before-reinvestigating
description: When a fix verified correct on disk still fails for the user: rule out stale state in their already-running session (loaded config, cached definitions, open shell) before re-investigating the artefact. Ask for the exact error text and what their running process has loaded.

name: make-config-reload-idempotent-when-changing-definition-kind
description: When replacing a definition with one of a different kind, clear the old one first so reloading the config is safe in an already-configured session

name: log-unattended-job-runs-for-later-verification
description: Have every unattended or boot-triggered job append a timestamped line to a run log, so a later session can confirm whether it fired

name: inspect-rendered-output-before-reporting-complete
description: Render generated visual output (slide, page, chart, PDF) to an image and inspect it before reporting the work complete; source text alone does not reveal wrapping, overflow, or collision defects

name: box-wrap-over-manual-line-breaks
description: When laying text into a fixed-width text box in a generated document or slide: let the renderer wrap the text; never insert manual line breaks. Hand-wrapped lines leave orphaned fragments as soon as the real font metrics differ from the estimate

name: edit-published-artefact-in-place-over-republish
description: When changing an artefact whose URL has already been shared: append to or edit it in place so the URL survives, rather than generating a replacement. If a rebuild is unavoidable, retire the superseded copy so only one live version remains

name: transcribe-source-verbatim-before-restructuring
description: Transcribe a photographed or handwritten source into text verbatim, preserving its own numbering and emphasis, before reorganising or rewording it

name: expand-role-swap-instructions-in-full
description: When a procedure abbreviates a symmetric step as a role swap ("then switch A to B"): write the swapped instruction out in full with the roles substituted. Participants executing the procedure live cannot expand the abbreviation in the moment

name: mirror-direct-edits-back-into-generator
description: When a generated artefact is edited directly after generation: apply the same change to its generator script and source document. Otherwise the next rebuild silently reverts the edit

name: single-implementation-thin-callers-over-parallel-copies
description: When the same helper must be usable from two machines or contexts: put the implementation in one place and make every other entry point a thin caller of it. Two copies drift silently, because each context is exercised separately and neither reports that the other has changed.

name: exclude-the-active-resource-from-a-destructive-picker
description: Omit the resource the user is currently operating inside from a destructive picker, and label its absence so the omission is explained rather than puzzling

name: cancel-whole-selection-on-invalid-destructive-input
description: When any token in a multi-select destructive command is invalid or out of range: cancel the entire selection and act on nothing. Acting on the valid subset turns a typo into partial irreversible damage the user did not review.

name: ship-a-dry-run-mode-and-test-every-branch-through-it
description: Give every destructive command a dry-run mode, and exercise each of its branches through that mode before the first real run

name: state-what-survives-in-a-destructive-confirmation-prompt
description: Name what is destroyed, what survives, and how to recover it in the confirmation prompt itself, rather than leaving the user to infer the blast radius

name: verify-weekday-date-pairs
description: When a date arrives with a weekday attached and the two do not agree ("Tue 1 Sep 2027" for a date that is a Wednesday): check the pairing against a calendar and ask which half is correct. Do not silently trust either — the mismatch usually means a mistyped year, and the two readings can differ by a year

name: record-settled-questions-in-place
description: Write each resolved question back into the artefact that carries the open-question list, marked settled with its date and its answer, so a later reader does not re-ask what has already been decided

name: consult-record-holder-before-revising
description: When a person other than the requester holds the written record of an event (notes, minutes, observations): collect it before revising the artefact from recollection, and state in the artefact that the revision is blocked until then. Revising first silently overwrites the record

name: record-sent-artefact-not-draft
description: When the user reports sending a drafted artefact: ask which version went out and record the sent text verbatim as the new baseline. Never assume the draft was sent unedited.

name: order-parallel-dispatch-by-priority-under-shared-quota
description: When dispatching parallel agents that share a session-wide resource quota (web searches, API calls, tokens): dispatch in priority order and state the quota in each prompt. Later agents run degraded or starved, so the least important task must be the one that runs short.

name: audit-existing-artefacts-against-new-governing-decision
description: When recording a decision that governs a class of artefacts: immediately check every artefact already written against it and mark each compliant or non-compliant. Applying the decision only to future work leaves contradicting artefacts in circulation.

name: regenerate-register-variant-from-single-authoritative-source
description: When the same content must exist in two registers (first and third person, formal and casual): name one file authoritative and regenerate the other from it. Never edit both in place, because they drift silently and the stale one gets sent.

name: redesign-claim-around-unverifiable-detail
description: When a checkable detail cannot be verified and the document goes to an outside reader: rewrite so the claim no longer depends on that detail, rather than shipping it hedged or dropping the point. Restore the detail only if the user confirms it.

name: keep-internal-record-plain-under-outward-framing
description: When a project adopts an outward framing that softens or omits intent: apply it only to artefacts that leave the project and keep internal records plainly accurate. State the boundary explicitly so the framing is never mistaken for the facts.

name: name-relationship-to-a-quantity
description: When citing a figure a person or organisation is associated with: name the relationship to it (raised, arranged, committed, under management, paid from) rather than a verb implying custody. An overstated relationship is the easiest claim for a reader to puncture.

name: research-findings-with-unsubstantiated-claims-section
description: Return research findings with: finding (one sentence) plus confidence (high | medium | low) plus source link per question; and a separate section listing widely circulated claims that could NOT be substantiated from primary sources, naming what was searched for each. If a claim is repeated only by secondary or advice-industry sources: list it in that section rather than the findings.

name: maintain-dated-log-of-outward-approaches
description: Maintain a dated log of every outward approach (recipient, channel, artefact, date) so non-response reads as channel behaviour, not rejection.

name: separate-generated-files-from-authored-files
description: When one file would be both machine-regenerated and human-authored: split it into a generated mirror and an authored file. A generator must never write a file a human edits, because content the human put there that cannot round-trip through the generator's source is destroyed silently.

name: gate-writes-to-authored-artefacts-on-per-item-ratification
description: When proposing changes to a human-authored artefact: emit one numbered proposal per unit and apply only the items the human ratifies. Record rejections against a stable id so they are never re-proposed; leave undecided items open rather than defaulting either way.

name: per-item-ratification-list
description: Return a numbered proposal list, one item per unit of the target artefact, each with: what changed, the diff where one exists, the proposed edit, the unit's current full text, a stable id, an accept box, a reject box, and a free-text comment field. Apply nothing.

name: search-existing-tooling-before-accepting-an-api-limitation
description: When a documented API limitation blocks an approach: search the project's own tooling and reference notes for something that already circumvents it before designing around it. A limitation of one interface is not a limitation of what is possible.

name: assert-target-identity-before-writing-to-a-live-edited-artefact
description: When writing into an artefact a human edits concurrently: address the target by its content, not its index, and assert the identity holds immediately before the write. Abort on mismatch rather than writing to whatever now occupies that position.

name: take-metaphor-and-orientation-from-canonical-source
description: When explaining a concept that already has a canonical diagram or published treatment: take the metaphor and its orientation from that source. Never invent a metaphor, because an invented one can silently invert the direction the canonical image encodes.

name: report-divergence-between-registers-without-merging
description: When two artefacts are written in different registers by design (a verbose source and a compressed presentation of it): report what appears in one and not the other, and do not reconcile them. Neither can be derived from the other.

name: split-claim-and-evidence-across-presentation-units
description: When a slide or presentation unit carries both a claim and the evidence for it: split it into two units and repeat the title across the build, rather than compressing the prose to make both fit.

name: draft-at-target-length-to-avoid-anchoring-the-editor
description: When drafting something a human will edit down: draft at the target length, not above it. A long first draft anchors the editor high, so they trim rather than rewrite and the result stays over-long.

name: ask-for-selection-criteria-rather-than-inventing-a-rubric
description: When deciding what to include versus omit and no rubric has been stated: name the observations gathered so far, say plainly that no rubric exists yet, and ask. Do not infer one and apply it silently across the artefact.

name: record-user-reported-actions-without-fabricating-detail
description: When the user reports actions they took and only some are recoverable from a primary record: record every reported item, giving the verified ones their recovered detail and the rest only what was stated. Do not drop an item because no record backs it, and do not pad it to match the others.

name: detect-audience-specific-text-surviving-into-a-variant
description: When the same message is sent to several audiences from one template: check each variant for phrasing that only fits a different recipient. If it has already gone out, report it as a fact and do not propose a fix.

name: one-column-one-information-type
description: When a value would be written into an existing column whose type of fact it does not match: create a new column for it rather than widening the existing column's vocabulary. A column carrying two kinds of fact (how far along the work is AND what went wrong; what a thing is AND how it was produced) answers neither question cleanly, and the damage surfaces only under review. Pair every split with a closed vocabulary and a CHECK constraint.

name: unstated-over-plausible-default-for-recorded-fact
description: When choosing a default for a column that records what actually happened (provenance, source, method, author): leave it unstated (NULL) rather than assert a plausible value. A default that is right for most rows is read as definitive for all of them, so the wrong rows become undetectable. Backfill known rows explicitly per group; leave the rest empty. Distinct from an unratified spec default, where a flagged forward-compatible value is correct.

name: rehearse-billable-run-locally-before-spending
description: Before provisioning a paid instance or dispatching a remote batch, execute the same production entry point against a miniature local fixture — not the test suite, not an approximation. Build every ratified fix first, rehearse, then provision: defects found after the meter starts are paid for twice.

name: prove-a-zero-result-is-real-not-a-mislocated-read
description: When an instrument reports that nothing is wrong (zero failures, no matches, empty diff): treat the zero as unproven until the instrument has been shown reporting a case that genuinely exists. An instrument reading the wrong location, layout, or compression returns the same zero as a healthy system. Construct the failing case first, watch it register, then believe the zero.

name: report-the-tie-and-stratify-rather-than-select-an-arm
description: When a head-to-head comparison of arms returns a near-tie: report the tie as the finding and stratify the sample by input type or difficulty, rather than breaking the tie or declaring the arms equivalent. A flat aggregate is the expected signature of arms that win on different strata and cancel out; selecting off a tie hard-codes a coin flip and destroys the evidence for a routing rule.

name: coarsen-when-input-precision-cannot-support-the-finer-claim
description: When the input's precision makes the most granular assignment ambiguous or undecidable: record the next-less-granular assignment that the precision does support, and record the refusal alongside it. Never emit the granular value with implied confidence the input cannot carry, and never drop the record entirely — the refusal is itself a retrievable fact.

name: test-handed-over-command-in-the-target-shell
description: Execute any command handed to a human for them to run in their actual shell first, with a dummy value, before handing it over — shell builtins differ between bash and zsh and an untested command fails in their hands.

name: outstanding-human-decision-register
description: Return a standing register of work only the principal can do, as a numbered list where each item carries: the date and time it was added, the decision or action required in one line, the document and section holding the ratification box, and its dependency predecessors (which items must close first). Items sequenced so no item appears before what it depends on. Completed items move to a separate Completed section, and only once completion is recorded in conversation — never marked complete by inference.

name: check-quantity-over-monitor-verdict
description: When a monitor reports a status and the quantity it derives from is available: read the quantity. A monitor's verdict is a claim about the monitor, not evidence about the system it watches.

name: worker-artefact-over-relayed-log
description: When a status is available both from a log relayed through a transport and from an artefact the worker writes directly: use the artefact. A relayed log freezes when its transport dies while the worker keeps running, so the freeze reads as a stall.

name: advancing-counter-over-liveness-signal
description: When judging whether a long-running job is healthy: require a work counter that advances, not a heartbeat that merely arrives. A heartbeat proves the reporting loop runs; a hung job reports healthily until its deadline.

name: optimise-deadline-not-cost-when-budget-expires
description: When a budget expires unused if unspent: stop optimising cost and optimise for completing before the expiry with the fewest failure modes. A cheaper option carrying an unresolved risk is the more expensive one.

name: test-guards-in-both-directions-before-deploying
description: Before deploying a guard that can destroy, block or revert: test that it acts on the case it targets AND that it abstains on a healthy case. A guard tested only against the failure it catches will destroy healthy work.

name: audit-thresholds-against-what-they-watch
description: Enumerate every timeout, watchdog and abort threshold in the system, then state for each the process it acts on and what that process emits inside the threshold.

name: place-supervisor-off-the-supervised-host
description: Run the supervisor of a remote job on a different host from the one that launched it, and give the job a self-describing expiry it carries itself.

name: declare-per-component-input-requirements
description: Declare each component's minimum input requirement, group components by that requirement, and load the cheapest input satisfying each group once.

name: instrumented-run-report
description: Return an instrumented run report with: items processed, seconds per stage, seconds per component, peak memory, observed throughput against expected, and a verdict of OK or CHECK with the reason. If a quantity was not measured: return null and label it unmeasured. Never return zero for a quantity nothing measured.

name: a-timed-out-gate-has-not-rejected-anything
description: When a safety gate times out rather than failing: treat it as unfinished, not as a rejection. Reproduce its check independently to learn whether it would pass, then give it more time. Never disable the gate to fit the timeout.

name: re-derive-counts-from-the-full-set-never-a-truncated-view
description: When reporting a count taken from output that may have been truncated by a pager or a head limit: re-derive it from the full set before stating it. A number read off a clipped listing is a fabrication with a plausible shape.

name: compare-a-local-gate-against-its-remote-mirror-for-divergence
description: When a check runs both locally and in CI: diff the two rule sets before trusting either as defence in depth. Divergent patterns, missing exemptions, and a diff range that covers only the last commit each produce a gate that passes locally and fails remotely, or the reverse.

name: check-mirror-freshness-in-the-session-that-edits-the-source
description: When editing a file that is manually copied to a published location: check how far the copy has drifted in the same session, not later. Manual mirror steps fail silently and the published copy is what users actually fetch.

name: seek-the-reconciling-reading-before-declaring-a-conflict
description: When two statements from the same person appear to contradict each other: construct the reading under which both are true before recording a conflict anywhere. Only escalate if no such reading exists, and never spawn follow-up tasks off an unconfirmed one.

name: read-forwardable-copy-as-addressed-downstream
description: When someone is handed a message and asked to pass it on: the wording inside it addresses the eventual reader, not the person holding it. Do not read the copy as the ask made of the intermediary.

name: treat-empty-output-as-exception-until-proven-miss
description: When an arm in a comparison produces no output for an item: classify it as an exception (crash, OOM, unsupported format) until the error stream shows otherwise. A blank is not a miss until you have shown it is not a failure.

name: refuse-count-ranking-until-segmentation-is-commensurable
description: When two arms segment their output differently (words against lines, tokens against spans): compute and state the segmentation ratio before any count-based ranking. A ratio far from 1.0 means the counts measure the segmenter, not the thing being measured.

name: test-the-pattern-on-the-filtered-population
description: When an interesting pattern appears in hand-picked examples: define the population the pattern claims to cover, filter to it mechanically, and re-test before stating the finding anywhere it can be quoted.

name: arm-comparison-validity-report
description: Return a comparison of scored arms containing: n, the denominator and how it was filtered, per-arm exception counts broken out by class, the segmentation ratio between arms, the pre-registered null result, and the verdict — or an explicit refusal naming which of these is missing.

name: resolve-every-external-dependency-before-committing-spend
description: Before provisioning a paid resource, resolve every URL, model repository, remote path and file list the run will use, expanding shell variables and loop constructs first, and print the unverifiable items separately rather than letting a partial check imply full coverage.

name: use-the-whole-billed-unit-before-releasing
description: When a resource bills in whole units with a minimum charge (whole-hour cloud instances): never release it early. Schedule further work into the paid remainder, extend across unit boundaries when a job is still running, and never interrupt a running job to fit the unit.

name: copy-not-sync-where-a-prefix-has-two-writers
description: When adding a second writer to a shared remote prefix: use a non-deleting transfer and prove it with a dry run that reports zero deletions. A deleting sync issued by either writer removes the other's objects, and neither writer can see the other's intent.

name: verify-a-destination-is-a-mount-not-a-path
description: Before writing bulk data to a removable-volume path: compare the destination's device id against the root filesystem's. An absent mount is silently an ordinary directory on the boot disk, and filling the boot disk can corrupt anything else running on it.

name: exit-non-zero-when-a-scheduled-run-declines-the-work
description: A scheduled wrapper that can skip its work must not exit 0 on the skip path, or the scheduler and every alert built on it cannot distinguish did-not-run from succeeded.

name: stage-every-run-in-its-own-table
description: Every processing run, cloud or local, writes to a table of its own carrying the settings that produced it as columns. The production table is written only by a merge that has a documented undo, so a run is never both the experiment and the record.

name: write-the-reversal-before-the-merge
description: In a merge register entry, state how to reverse the merge before stating how to perform it. A merge whose undo cannot be written down is not ready to run.

name: randomise-arm-order-per-item-with-the-key-held-separately
description: In a human arbitration interface, randomise the order of the arms independently for each item from a fixed seed, and keep the arm-to-panel key in a separate file the judge does not open.

name: validate-an-absence-defined-control-set-by-eye
description: When a control set is defined by the absence of something (no text, no faces, no speech): show every member to a human for confirmation before use. A control set that is 86 per cent pure biases every rate computed against it, in a direction nothing downstream can detect.

name: measure-draft-style-against-author-corpus-baseline
description: Measure a draft's stylistic markers against a baseline computed from the author's own prior published work, reporting each as a rate per 1,000 words

name: re-derive-figures-from-source-artefacts
description: Trace every figure in a draft to the artefact that produced it and re-derive the value from that artefact rather than accepting the draft's statement of it

name: verify-parse-before-reporting-derived-counts
description: Before reporting any count derived from parsed text, verify the parse by checking segment boundaries against the source

name: author-edited-version-is-the-merge-base
description: When the author has edited an older version of a document than the one you revised: rebuild from the author's file as the base and port across only your changes to passages they did not touch. Never reinstate an edit the author reversed. If one of your changes is redundant against their new text, drop it and say so.

name: standing-style-rule-over-historical-voice
description: When matching an author's historical voice conflicts with a style rule they imposed later: apply the later rule, and surface the conflict with both measurements so the author decides. Do not silently pick either side.

name: author-edit-pattern-overrides-your-prior-recommendation
description: When the author's own edits show a consistent direction and one of your earlier recommendations runs against it: follow the author's pattern and state plainly that you are reversing your earlier advice. Their revision record outranks your prior reasoning.

name: skip-pipeline-append-of-content-already-present
description: When a publishing pipeline would append boilerplate the document body already contains: skip the append and record the reason in the source file, so a later run does not re-add it and duplicate the block.

name: voice-match-report
description: Return a voice-match report as a table with one row per stylistic marker (self-links, parentheticals per 1,000 words, em-dashes per 1,000 words, bolded claims, section headers, mean sentence length): baseline range with the named prior works it was computed from, the draft's value, and a gap verdict. If a marker cannot be counted mechanically: omit the row. Do not estimate.

name: claim-to-artefact-table
description: Return a claim-to-artefact table with one row per figure in the draft: the claim as written, the artefact path it came from, the value re-derived from that artefact, and a mismatch flag (match | mismatch | unverifiable). If no artefact supports a figure: mark it unverifiable and do not infer a source.

name: claim-as-reduction-not-compensation-where-damages-are-barred
description: When a contract bars claims for cost, expense, loss and damage but separately provides for rent, fee or price abatement: frame the ask as a reduction in what is contractually payable, never as compensation. The two look alike to the claimant and are treated completely differently by the instrument; wording the ask as compensation walks it into the exclusion clause.

name: run-the-claim-on-the-counterpartys-own-clause-hold-statute-in-reserve
description: When a claim could rest either on statute or on a clause of the counterparty's own contract: lead with the contract clause and hold the statutory argument for a reply to an actual refusal. Citing statute in a first approach reclassifies the matter from one the recipient can settle at their desk to one routed for a legal view, and pre-empts a defence that may never be raised.

name: volunteer-the-adverse-document-and-narrow-the-claim-by-it
description: When the counterparty holds a document that damages your position: produce it yourself in the first approach, accept what it says without qualification, and visibly limit the claim by reference to it. Do not also attack the document's formality — a concession and an attack on the same document cancel each other. Reserve the attack for a refusal that relies on it.

name: route-reviewers-to-primary-sources-not-the-authors-reasoning
description: Direct each review agent to the primary source documents and instruct it to read the author's own reasoning file last, or not at all, so findings are checked against source rather than inherited from the author

name: treat-convergence-of-opposed-reviewers-as-decisive
description: When reviewers assigned deliberately opposed stakes independently recommend the same change: treat that convergence as decisive and act on it without further deliberation. Reserve judgement for findings where the reviewers disagree, which is where the real decision sits.

name: search-the-working-files-before-asking-the-human
description: Search the working files, including free text appended after a question and diffs since the last commit, for an answer the human has already recorded in place, before adding any item to a request list

name: verification-checklist-with-per-item-fallback
description: Return a pre-delivery verification checklist with, per item: the assertion being relied on, the exact location to check it (document, page, clause), and the specific fallback to apply if it does not hold — the wording to remove and any figure to recompute. Every item must have a fallback, so no single unverified assertion can block delivery. If an assertion cannot be checked from available sources: mark it UNCHECKABLE and name the document that would settle it. Do not guess.

name: correct-your-own-recorded-argument-with-a-do-not-reinstate-note
description: When an argument you previously recorded is found unsound, replace it and leave a dated warning naming the error and instructing later readers not to reinstate it, rather than deleting it silently

name: state-accruing-figures-as-at-a-named-date-with-the-rate
description: When a claimed or reported figure accrues with time: state it as at a named date and give the accrual rate alongside, rather than a bare total. Where the rate varies by period (month length, tier, rate change), give each rate. A total without its date silently goes wrong the moment delivery slips.

name: separate-entitlement-from-quantum-and-name-the-weak-half
description: When advising on a claim, assess whether the right to anything and the amount of it stand or fall separately, and tell the principal which half is weak before they act. A clause that grants a remedy but reserves the amount to the other side's determination gives a strong entitlement and a weak quantum; the principal should expect to win the point and negotiate the figure.

name: check-settlement-release-before-accepting-a-partial-offer
description: When a partial or goodwill offer arrives carrying settlement language (full and final, without admission, in settlement of): do not accept before checking whether the release forecloses the balance of the claim. Statutory protections against contracting out commonly carve out releases given in settlement of a dispute, so a small sum accepted on those words can extinguish a much larger continuing claim.

name: supervise-a-resumable-job-to-capture-its-exit-code
description: When a long-running resumable job may be killed by the host: run it under a supervisor that records the exit code and elapsed time of every attempt. A bare job that is SIGKILLed leaves no traceback and no crash report, so the difference between an out-of-memory kill and a broken deployment is unknowable without the code.

name: stop-not-retry-when-a-worker-fails-fast-with-no-progress
description: When a supervised worker exits non-zero within seconds having advanced no state: stop and surface the error rather than restarting. A fast failure with no progress is a broken deployment, and retrying it only buries the traceback under identical restarts.

name: cryptcheck-not-check-for-an-encrypted-remote
description: When verifying a file copied to an encrypted remote: use the encryption-aware comparison. The ordinary check cannot hash through the crypt layer and reports that hashes could not be checked, which reads like a pass and is not one.

name: compute-the-parallelism-identity-before-tuning-a-worker
description: When a parallel job slows down, divide recorded per-item cost by worker count and compare with observed throughput. Matching means per-item work changed; falling short means concurrency collapsed. This separates a workload change from contention before any setting is touched.

name: remove-competing-load-before-changing-worker-settings
description: When a parallel job is slow on a saturated host: remove other load before adjusting concurrency or batch size. Worker settings cannot buy back cores that something else is holding, and changing them hides the real cause behind a second variable.

name: count-your-own-monitoring-in-the-load-you-measure
description: Include your own polling, waiting and logging in any assessment of what is loading a machine, and put a sleep in every wait loop. A busy-wait spins a full core, so the observer becomes a material part of the contention it is trying to attribute.

name: verify-a-text-payload-with-length-statistics-on-both-sides
description: After moving text out of a datastore, compare min, median and max length of what arrived against the same statistics computed in the store. Field-separated dumps split on embedded newlines and silently truncate, and every analysis downstream inherits the loss.

name: search-content-not-filenames-before-declaring-a-file-absent
description: When about to report that something was never saved: search file contents and session transcripts for the payload's own distinctive vocabulary, not for a guessed filename. A filename glob answers a different question and answers it confidently.

name: persist-human-judgement-before-the-page-is-opened
description: Any interface built for a person to rank, score or annotate must autosave, restore visibly on load, and offer export and import before it is handed over. Human judgement cannot be recomputed, so losing it costs more than losing the whole run that produced the artefact.

name: namespace-browser-storage-by-filename-under-file-urls
description: Key browser storage by page filename when pages are opened as local files. Browsers commonly treat every local-file URL as one shared origin, so unnamespaced keys silently collide between separate pages.

name: fingerprint-saved-answers-against-the-page-version
description: Store a structural fingerprint alongside saved form answers and refuse to reapply them when it no longer matches. Restoring answers onto a regenerated page attaches judgements to the wrong items, which is worse than losing them.

name: weight-a-comparison-by-substance-not-by-presence-count
description: When comparing two extractors, do not rank them by how many items produced any output. Counting presence scores a one-character hallucination equal to a full reading and can invert the verdict; weight by the size or quality of what was extracted.

name: recover-the-direction-a-store-cannot-record
description: When one side of a comparison stores only positive results, its blank cases leave no rows and any gain is invisible. Reconstruct the attempted population from the job or state log so both gains and losses are countable.

name: enumerate-the-artefact-class-before-calling-a-fix-complete
description: After fixing a defect in one artefact, list every artefact of the same kind and check each. A defect in a generated class is a property of the generator, and repairing only the instance in hand leaves the rest broken and believed fixed.

name: re-run-the-failures-with-the-suspect-parameter-varied
description: When a run produces a set of failures attributed to one parameter, re-run just those failures with that parameter changed and everything else fixed. The recovery count bounds the parameter's true contribution and is far cheaper than a full re-run.

name: record-a-deliberate-stop-that-defeats-a-restart-policy
description: When stopping a service that carries an automatic restart policy: record the stop somewhere the next operator will read. An explicit stop overrides the policy, so a later restart of the host brings back a partial system that looks healthy.

name: rank-by-negative-tail-not-average
description: When comparing options by aggregated ratings: compute the share of worst-tier ratings for each rather than comparing means. A bimodal option and a uniformly mediocre one produce the same average, and only the tail distinguishes them.

name: enumerate-non-retrofittable-preconditions
description: Before adopting an act-now-and-reconcile-later approach: enumerate which entitlements require a document, registration or authorisation to exist BEFORE the event. Those cannot be recovered afterwards and are the only real constraint on ordering.

name: sort-entitlements-by-enforceability
description: Sort claimed benefits into contractually enforceable, conditional on a component that may be dropped, and withdrawable at the provider's discretion. Never present them as one list; the middle category is what disappears silently when something else changes.

name: name-what-a-scope-narrowing-costs-the-argument
